Cover to be photographed: could not confirm which image, if any, was used as the printed front cover versus an exhibition/interior plate. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: Bowery
description:
Bowery is the sixth installment in an ongoing numbered zine series by the English, New York-based photographer Robin Broadbent, issued in a limited run of 100 copies through Dashwood Books.

Consistent with earlier volumes in Broadbent's series, the zine is issued as a small, numbered print object rather than a bound monograph; its cover is marked simply with the issue number rather than a printed title. Broadbent's photographic sensibility draws on the reductive, geometric vocabulary of Constructivism and Bauhaus design, favoring stripped-down compositions built from industrial and architectural material.

Broadbent worked as an assistant to the London photographer Robert Golden before establishing his own practice, and has continued to publish work in small, self-directed print runs alongside editorial and commercial photography. Bowery extends that self-publishing practice, taking the neighborhood as subject for a photographer whose formal interests otherwise run toward abstraction rather than documentary place-making.
notes: Numbered zine, vol. 6 in Broadbent's self-published series; edition of 100 copies. Page count and dimensions not found in any source consulted. Physical cover is marked "SIX" (the volume number) rather than the title "Bowery." Edition to be verified against the copy. No ISBN. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: The Photographic Work of Robin Broadbent by Robin Broadbent
description:
Robin Broadbent is a master photographer, sought out for his exquisite still life photographs.

An acute knack for identifying and capturing the glancing pro le of an object is part of the character of his work, which abstracts the essence from contemporary brand and fashion advertising and then combines it with the universal photographic language of the 20th century avant-garde. The starting point for Broadbent is lighting, his end-point the printed image. He works with light to give atness or depth to his images—he can make a building seem weightless or a small crater of powder epic in scale.

Being able to play with our perceptions in this way recalls the early days of Surrealism and highlights the playfulness of his work. Broadbent uses a complex and nuanced language of color and scale, guile and humour, to play with our preconceptions of fashion and abstraction. The book reads like a magazine, and there is an undercurrent that emerges suggesting these images have a meaning more than the sum of their content. This undercurrent represents the essence of the fashion world now.

title: The Photographic Work of Robin Broadbent
description:
Published by Damiani in 2017, The Photographic Work of Robin Broadbent collects two decades of the photographer's still-life abstractions, distilling everyday objects into stark, reductive forms that blur the line between fashion image-making and studio experiment.

The book's 184 pages sequence 100 color and 60 black-and-white plates in which pills, crayons, pipettes, combs, and a single oversized gold tooth are photographed against plain grounds until scale and material dissolve into pure line and shadow. Broadbent sequenced the book with designer Doug Lloyd; it opens unusually with a short story by the novelist Frederic Tuten and closes with three pages of notes listing studio equipment and the surfaces objects were shot against.

British-born and based in New York since 1999, Broadbent built his reputation shooting for Vogue, Numéro, Harper's Bazaar, and the New York Times Magazine. This volume is his third book, following the earlier black-and-white series Marmalade (1998) and Minus Sixteen (1999), and marks his first survey of personal and editorial work assembled as a single monograph.
notes: Damiani hardcover with jacket, 8.5 x 11 in, 184pp (100 color / 60 b&w), text by Frederic Tuten, sequenced with designer Doug Lloyd. Broadbent's third book, after Marmalade (1998) and Minus Sixteen (1999). Existing cover file already on disk was verified against the publisher's product image and kept. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: Typology 1979
description:
Joachim Brohm Typology 1979 No two of the little houses are the same… carefully proportioned furnishings here are wildly contradicted with slapdash decorations over there.

Everyone has thought about their buildings, brought materials, laid walls, used power drills, insulated, glued things, extended the previous tenant’s shed, retro-fitted a bigger window, added a television antenna. They are strange hybrid buildings, between tool sheds and dachas, gingerbread houses and orangeries. Ulf Erdmann Ziegler Joachim Brohm rose to prominence in the early 1980s, one of the first photographers in Europe to take pictures exclusively in colour, connecting the everyday cultural landscape with the new possibilities of colour photography.

This collection titled Typology 1979 is one of his very earliest series, depicting 35 allotment sheds from the Ruhr valley region of Germany, painterly images that are an everyday inventory – of garden structures, of human activity. Influenced by the great American photographers such as William Eggleston and Robert Adams, he also looked to his German contemporaries, Bernd and Hilla Becher, whose ‘typologies’ are heralded in the collection’s title. Joachim Brohm was born 1955 in Dülken, Germany. He lives and works in Leipzig and since 1993 he has been Professor of Photography at Leipzig Hochschule fur Grafik und Buchkunst/Academy of Visual Arts.

title: Spirit is a Bone
description:
series of portraits, which includes Pussy Riot member Yekaterina Samutsevic and many other Moscow citizens, were created by a machine: a facial recognition system recently developed in Moscow for public security and border control surveillance.

The result is more akin to a digital life mask than a photograph a three-dimensional facsimile of the face that can be easily rotated and closely scrutinised. - What is significant about this camera is that it is designed to make portraits without the co-operation of the subject four lenses operating in tandem to generate a full frontal image of the face, ostensibly looking directly into the camera, even if the subject himself is unaware of being photographed. - The system was designed for facial recognition purposes in crowded areas such as subway stations, railroad stations, stadiums, concert halls or other public areas but also for photographing people who would normally resist being photographed. Indeed any subject encountering this type of camera is rendered passive, because no matter which direction he or she looks, the face is always rendered looking forward and stripped bare of shadows, make-up, disguises or even poise. - Co-opting this device, Broomberg & Chanarin have constructed their own taxonomy of portraits in contemporary Russia that rely heavily on the oeuvre of two 20th Century German artists. August Sander produced over 300 portraits of archetypal German workers during the Weimar Republic – from the baker to the philosopher to the revolutionary.

His project, to create a comprehensive archive of society, was conceptually and formally rigorous. His subjects are positioned centre frame. Always looking into camera. Always heroic in relation to the lens. But the result, retrospectively viewed through the lens of the 2nd World War becomes unexpectedly melancholic, even sinister. - ander's contemporary, Helmar Lerski, also categorised his subjects according to profession. Lerski however rejected the singular, heroic, full body portrait. Instead he insisted on repetitive close-ups that convey a powerful sense of claustrophobia and always multiple views of the same faces shown from different viewpoints. Unlike Sander's humanistic approach, Lerski insisted that you could tell nothing from the surface of the skin. -Echoing both Sander's and Lerski's projects, Broomberg & Chanarin have made a series of portraits cast according to professions. But their portraits are produced with this new technology, with little if any human interaction. They are low resolution and fragmented. The success of these images are determined by how precisely this machine can identify its subject: the characteristics of the nose, the eyes, the chin, and how these three intersect. Nevertheless they cannot help being portraits of individuals, struggling and often failing to negotiate a civil contract with state power.
tags: Surveillance Index, Photography, Surveillance Index Edition One

title: Holy Bible
edition_printrun: check edition info. Out of print
description:
For their version of the Holy Bible, Adam Broomberg and Oliver Chanarin mined the Archive of Modern Conflict with philosopher Adi Ophir’s central tenet in mind: that God reveals himself predominantly through catastrophe.

The format of Broomberg and Chanarin’s illustrated Holy Bible mimics both the precise structure and the physical form of the King James version. By allowing elements of the original text to guide their image selection, the artists explore themes of authorship, and the unspoken criteria used to determine acceptable evidence of conflict. Inspired in part by the annotations and images Bertolt Brecht added to his own personal bible, Broomberg and Chanarin’s publication questions the clichés at play within the visual representation of conflict.
tags: illustrations, artistic-photography, god, wrath, violence, religious-aspects, bible, Photography

title: People in Trouble Laughing Pushed to the Ground Songbook
description:
Photographers Adam Broomberg and Oliver Chanarin dove into the Belfast Exposed photography archive and created a photobook called "People in Trouble, Laughing, Pushed to the Ground" published by Mack.

The archive was founded in 1983 and contains over half a million images, from which over 14,000 black-and-white contact sheets documenting the Troubles in Northern Ireland. These photos were taken by professional and amateur photographers and were censored by the governement. As a reponse to that, Belfast Exposed started to collect all these images, showing protest and terror alongside people drinking, kissing and smoking.
tags: portrait, Photography, Surveillance Index, Surveillance Index Edition One

title: Cecily Brown
description:
Presenting a world that pulses with excesses and appetites, Cecily Brown explores the breadth of human experience in her tactile oil paintings.

Broadly inspired by the history of painting—from Rubens and Veronese to the muscular expressionism of Willem de Kooning—Cecily Brown's personal vision transcends classical notions of genre and narrative, freeing her subject matter from its original context and positioning it within a new aesthetic reality.

Submerged within her vigorous gestural abstractions are scenes in which tangles of flesh dissolve into sensuous textures. Eschewing fixed meaning, Brown's paintings reflect the flux of life through fragmentary glimpses of form. This volume is published on the occasion of an exhibition of new paintings by the artist held in November 2011 at the Gagosian Gallery in Rome.

title: Cecily Brown: Rehearsal
description: Where Cecily Brown’s canvases revel in the visceral immediacy of paint, her drawings offer fragmentary motifs that build upon and undo each other. In conjunction with Cecily Brown: Rehearsal, the first exhibition dedicated to her drawings, Drawing Papers 128 features color illustrations of each work in the exhibition, including more than eighty small drawings, large-scale works, and sketchbooks. Arranged by theme, the volume guides readers through Brown’s repeated—and rehearsed—motifs.

title: Cecily Brown & Jim Lewis: The English Garden
description:
Like nature, only better. Nature with all the awkward bits smoothed out.

And then picturesque, like a landscape painting," states Jim Lewis' protagonist, defining an English garden in Cecily Brown's newest book of paintings. An imaginative pas de deux, The English Garden sees British painter Brown (born 1969) and American writer Lewis (born 1963) contribute acutely detailed and darkly sensuous allusions to the traditional 18th-century English landscape garden. Thirty-nine of Brown's paintings are interspersed throughout this compact hardcover publication as tipped-in images.

The largely abstract works, with glimpses of figurative elements, are a dichotomy of warm and subdued strokes of color, each containing an expansive landscape unto itself. Novelist and critic Jim Lewis' story transports the reader to the English countryside and investigates the seductive pull of the natural world in tandem with Brown's paintings. Combining two major voices in contemporary literature and painting, this volume is a truly

title: Rodeo
description:
Rodeo collects a lesser-known body of work by Bruce Bellas, known as Bruce of Los Angeles, one of the most prolific photographers of the male physique in mid-century America.

Curated by photography critic Vince Aletti and published by Acne Studios in 2013, the 190-page hardcover reproduces Bellas's pictures of rodeo cowboys — bronco busters and bull riders photographed off duty, resting and joking between events at Western rodeos of the 1950s, '60s, and '70s. Bound in faux leather with a printed slipcase and issued in a numbered edition of 500, the book includes several pages of hand-mounted replica prints produced on a Japanese Komori press, a production choice echoing the small-format prints Bellas once sold by mail order.

Bellas built his career, and a large mail-order business, photographing bodybuilders and physique models for magazines such as Adonis and The Male Figure, work that helped define the visual language of American beefcake photography and, later, the codes of gay visual culture more broadly. Aletti, a longtime chronicler of photography and fashion, singled out the rodeo pictures for their unguarded, documentary quality, a register distinct from the staged, statuesque nudes for which Bellas is best known.
notes: One of two copies in the collection. Edited by Vince Aletti. Hardcover in slipcase, numbered limited edition of 500 copies, 190 pages, 24 × 19 cm. No ISBN found. Cover image sourced from a small archival thumbnail (108×138px); a higher-resolution scan was not located. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: Rodeo
description:
Rodeo collects a little-known body of work by Bruce of Los Angeles, the photographer better known for the stylized male nudes that made him a founding figure of mid-century beefcake photography.

Edited by critic Vince Aletti, the book gathers Bellas's photographs of cowboys taken casually between events at Western rodeos through the 1950s, 60s, and 70s: real ranch hands and competitors, dressed and at ease, rather than posed studio subjects. Published by Acne Studios in a numbered edition of 500, the 190-page hardcover was printed on a Japanese Komori press and includes several hand-mounted replica prints, housed in a printed slipcase.

Bruce Bellas worked as a chemistry teacher in Nebraska before relocating to Los Angeles in the late 1940s to photograph bodybuilders and athletes, eventually publishing his own physique magazine, The Male Figure. His work is understood as a direct precursor to later photographers of the male body, including Robert Mapplethorpe, Herb Ritts, and Bruce Weber.
notes: One of two copies in the collection. Catalogue record listed author first name as 'Daniel'; no source connects a 'Daniel' to Bruce Bellas / Bruce of Los Angeles, so the professional name is treated here as the full author name. No ISBN found for this Acne Studios edition; numbered edition of 500, printed on a Japanese Komori press with hand-mounted replica prints, in a printed card slipcase. Edited (not photographed) by Vince Aletti. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: Cabin Fevr
edition_printrun: 500, Japanese binding, ills colour, poster dustjacket
description:
Cabin Fever is the first publication of New-York based artist Katie Burnett, and was developed in a very playful and intuitive way.

Burnett investigated the possibilities of her own environment and self. Cabin Fever is a 80-page photographic display of self-portraiture, but not the usual kind. Within the title, Burnett messes with contrast and composition to vast extremes, meaning that sometimes her imagery becomes unrecognisable.

Other times, one can plainly see that her two cats are in the picture, or that she used rubber bands, ramen noodles, sprinklers and everyday household items to merge into her abstract vision. Moving and making go hand in hand in Burnetts way of working, and she shows the viewer how the medium of photography can be pure joy.

title: Cathy John
edition_printrun: 1st, Signed. First edition, one of 500 copies printed. 8vo unpaged illustrated from photographs of Kate Bush by the author. Rare

title: Las Rutas de la Pasión (The Routes of Passion / Les Routes de la Passion)
The Readers Voice
description: Somewhere between cartoons, writing, and concrete poetry, these collages by Mitch Cairns are inspired by all these forms, and by music. As with his painting, he imposes limits that paradoxically allow freer expression for example using French, a language he doesn’t speak, or letters to make images. Cairns plays with thoughts, ideas and memories with great economy and wit, using the now-defunct Letraset, and Zazzle stickers of images from a personal archive. - Heide Museum of Modern Art

title: El Triángulo Perfecto
description:
El Triángulo Perfecto watches a police motorcycle squadron rehearse a human pyramid and finds in its collapses a portrait of authority as slapstick.

Calderón photographed the motorized unit of the Mexico City police as they practised the stunt they call the perfect triangle: riders standing on each other's shoulders as the bikes roll in formation. The pictures record the attempts as much as the pose, with officers tumbling into the sand, helmets and gloves scattered. Sixty-four pages in a pocket-sized clothbound hardcover, with a text by the writer Carlos Velázquez and a short account by the artist, published by CONACULTA in 2015 in Spanish.

Calderón (born 1971, Mexico City) co-founded the artist-run space La Panadería in 1994 and has worked across video, photography, sculpture and painting, most of it aimed at the stereotypes and rituals of Mexican public life: hunting trophies, telenovela villains, the police. He is represented by kurimanzutto and has shown at MoMA PS1, the Hammer Museum and the Museo Tamayo. This book belongs with his other photographic series in which official spectacle is allowed to fail on camera.
tags: Photography, Contemporary Art, Mexico, Latin American Art, Performance
notes: Some dealer listings give the author as Miguel Ángel Calderón; same book and ISBN. Amazon dates the edition 2014, the Mexican listings 2015. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: Some of Us Did Not Die
publisher: Tammy Rae Carland & Land and Sea

title: 3 Projects
description: Co-published by Galerie Olivier Robert and CLASSIC Paris. Softcover with silicon band, staple bound. Features 32 pages of black-and-white offset printed photography showcasing three distinct photographic projects by Asger Carlsen.

title: MAA
description:
MAA documents the funeral rituals of Manikarnika, the cremation ground on the Ganges in Varanasi, alongside the everyday life that surrounds it, drawn from roughly ten thousand photographs made over several years by local photographer Indra Kumar Jha, one of the few photographers the community permits to document the cremations.

The book's design runs two sequences at once through folded pages: the outer face of each spread presents a stream of 108 headshots, living and dead, a tribute to the goddess Kali's garland of 108 slain heads, while the inner pages hold everyday scenes from Manikarnika. Federico Carpani, an Italian photographer, met Jha by chance near the cremation ground and edited and designed the book from his archive; it was self-published in Bologna in an edition of 500, softcover with an exposed spine and gatefold construction throughout. The title is the word used across India both for one's own mother and for the various forms of the goddess.

Carpani is an Italian photographer and editor associated with Skinnerboox; MAA was recognized by the Anamorphosis Prize for its unusual cross-cultural authorship, pairing an outsider's editorial eye with an insider's decade of access.
notes: Catalogue annotation "(signed)" stripped from title; copy is signed. Co-authored with Varanasi photographer Indra Kumar Jha, whose archive the book draws from; self-published, edition of 500, no ISBN assigned. Cover image is the only resolution found online (low-resolution). Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: MEC,
description:
Despite an oeuvre spanning more than 20 years and a disavowal of any signature style, Mary Ellen Carroll has throughout her career been investigating a single, fundamental question: What is a work of art?

The resulting multifarious, provocative and often wry outpouring in architecture, writing, performance, photography, filmmaking, printmaking, sculpture and painting has been collected into this book--the New York conceptual artist's long-awaited first monograph. Carroll's work interrogates the relationship between subjectivity, language and power at its core is a dedication to political and social critique. The touchstones of her practice are the double, the imitation and the copy, and these motifs are applied to a range of ends--from conjuring the unheimlich to probing the means of distribution and interpretation of the work of art.

A Carroll piece may involve something as seemingly effortless as trademarking an idea by another artist or as complex and bold as walking out the door penniless with only her passport and the clothes on her back to spend six weeks in a foreign country. Carroll imbues all her work with a strong performative element even a new opus, involving the rotation of a Houston tract home on its foundation, is conceived as a way of making architecture perform.

title: Magnum Analog Recovery
description:
LE BAL / French / Self-published / April 2017 / 1st edition / FR.

From Robert Capa's D-Day to Gilles Peress Telex Iran to anonymous and never seen before series, this outstanding book published for the current exhibition Magnum Analog Recovery proposes an original and non official walk through the first 30 years of the Magnum Agency. In a large stiff cardboard binder reminiscent of the archive boxes where the photos were found, iconic pictures from the 20th century mix with unknown images from Henri Cartier-Bresson, Eve Arnold, René Burri, Elliott Erwitt, Alex Webb and Gilles Peress.

Far from a traditional exhibition catalogue, this outstanding book-object overlaps unique images, posters of various sizes and gorgeous black & white series. A game between what is given to see and what is hidden is slowly revealed to the reader through the folding and unfolding of all the posters and images. Texts and quotes from photographers (notes, letters, excerpts from correspondence and interviews,...) punctuate the sequence and evoke the complexity of all the different approaches within the agency's photographers. Magnum Analog Recovery is a jump in time and a walk through the golden age of the iconic agency that defined the genre of the documentary photography.

title: Paloma al Aire
description:
Paloma al Aire is Ricardo Cases's vivid portrait of colombicultura, a little-known Spanish sport in which fluorescent-dyed pigeons are trained to chase, rather than outrace, a single female through the sky.

Published in 2011 by Dewi Lewis in a spiral-bound softback of 74 pages (and the same year in Spain by Photovision), the book's 43 color photographs follow the colombicultura clubs of Valencia and Murcia, where handlers invest years and considerable resources training male pigeons, painted in bold, flag-like color combinations, whose success is measured not by speed but by the persistence and intensity of their courtship display. Cases documents the men who run behind their birds through fields and rooftops, turning an obscure regional pastime into a study of aspiration, ritual, and belonging.

Cases, born in Orihuela, Spain, in 1971, trained as a journalist before turning to photography focused on the customs and subcultures of rural Spain. Paloma al Aire, his third photobook, was included in Martin Parr and Gerry Badger's The Photobook: A History, Volume III and remains among the defining works of contemporary Spanish documentary photography.
notes: English-language edition (Dewi Lewis Publishing, 2011); a Spanish first edition was published the same year by Photovision (ISBN 9788493154653). The book has since gone through further editions through 2024. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: Nightfall
edition_printrun: Limited edition of 50, signed and numbered
description:
Giles Cassels' Nightfall collects overlooked, banal fragments of daily life and re-stages them as signifiers charged with private and cultural weight, closing a loop between waking perception and dream life.

Issued in spring 2015 as a 64-page color photobook, the volume is the second of a four-part quarterly series the artist self-published that year, following Floatation Tank. The edition was limited to fifty signed and numbered copies, several bound with an accompanying print.

The book sits within Cassels' ongoing practice of sequencing quiet, found-feeling color images into loosely narrative small-press volumes, distributed through specialist photobook shops rather than a formal publishing house.
notes: Signed, with print (collector's copy note preserved from catalogue). Self-published quarterly series, second of four 2015 volumes; edition of 50 signed/numbered copies. No ISBN identified. Cover confirmed against artist's own listing image. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: Floatation Tank
edition_printrun: Edition of 50, signed and numbered, with included print
description:
Floatation Tank is the debut installment in Giles Cassels's quarterly photobook series, a moody assemblage of American vernacular imagery that fellow photographer Tony Fouhse described as approximating a feeling of the country itself.

Self-published in a signed, numbered edition of 50 with an included print, the 64-page color book was the first of four issues Cassels released one per season through 2015, followed later that year by Nightfall. It combines dark landscapes, roadside clutter, and worn cultural icons into a fragmented sequence, an undertone of dry humor running beneath its otherwise apocalyptic mood.

Cassels is an American photographer whose ongoing quarterly series continued with Nightfall and later issues, distributed through specialist photobook dealers including photo-eye, PhotoBookStore, and Flotsam Books. The project extends a lineage of fragmented, vernacular American road photography while foregrounding the handmade, small-edition nature of the object itself.
notes: Signed edition with an included print (one of 50 signed and numbered copies); shelf record carried the annotation '(signed with print)'. First in Cassels's four-part quarterly photobook series begun winter 2015. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: Within Reach
description:
In her large-scale oil paintings, New York-based artist Jordan Casteel (born 1989) takes up questions of Black subjectivity and representation by examining the gestures, spaces and forms of nonverbal communication that underpin portraiture.

“There is a certain amount of mindfulness that it requires ... to be present with someone in a moment.” she explains. “I’ve always had an inclination towards seeing people who might be easily be unseen.” Published for Casteel’s first solo museum exhibition in New York, this volume brings together 40 large-scale paintings from throughout her career, including works from the celebrated series Visible Man (2013-14) and Nights in Harlem (2017), along with recent cropped “subway paintings” and portraits of her students at Rutgers University-Newark.

Whether depicting former classmates from Yale, nude and in serene repose street vendors near her home in Harlem anonymous New Yorkers huddled on the subway or her own students, posed largely in domestic interiors among their personal belongings, she explores how both public and private spheres can serve as frames for an inner life. This generously illustrated, oversized publication honors the larger-than-life scale of the artist's work. It is the first comprehensive monographic publication on Casteel’s work and includes texts by Dawoud Bey, Amanda Hunt and Lauren Haynes, and conversations conducted with the artist by Massimiliano Gioni and Thelma Golden.

title: Cesura Fanzine #02
edition_printrun: Edition of 150, hand-cut pages, Color offset
Spiral bound. First edition. Digital offset printing on tracing paper. Limited edition of 150 numbered and signed copies.
description: 41.667 milliseconds is the amount of time one frame lasts in a 24 fps film. All photographs in this book are appropriated from corroded vintage Scandinavian pornographic films. The book, which is meant to be looked at like a calendar, was printed on tracing paper, reminiscent of transparency films used for Super 8mm projections.

title: My Freedom
edition_printrun: First edition of 69 copies, each with a C-print
description:
My Freedom is a small, tightly limited artist book from the year Tiane Doan na Champassak's self-publishing was at its most prolific, and it keeps the intimacy of the residency in which it was made.

The photographs were taken during an artist residency in Bangkok. The book runs to 44 pages at 19.5 by 30 cm, with a wraparound colour photograph on the cover and no printed title, and was issued under the artist's own Siam's Guy Books imprint in a first edition of 69 copies, each sold with a C-print. It appeared in 2016 alongside 41.667, Tamarind Ghosts, Hardcore, Palms and Siam's Guy, the last two of which are also in this collection.

Champassak (born 1973) is a French artist of Lao descent whose work turns on sexuality, gender and the body as they pass through photography's filters of anonymity and censorship. He moves between his own pictures and appropriated material from the internet, magazines and personal ephemera, and Thailand has been a recurring site. His books have been published by Mörel, RVB and Éditions Bessard as well as under his own label.
notes: Self-published under the artist's Siam's Guy Books label; no ISBN. Edition of 69 copies, issued signed with a C-print. Copy to be checked for the print. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

title: Siam's Guy
description:
Siam's Guy takes its name from a censored Thai erotic magazine of the 1960s–70s, the found material French photographer Tiane Doan na Champassak splices with his own photographs in the book that first joined his personal practice to his art of appropriation.

Published by RVB Books (Paris) in 2016 as a 72-page softcover, 18 × 26 cm, the book layers 68 surviving pages of the original magazine, salvaged from a run of 100 issues, with new black-and-white nude photographs Champassak shot himself. The magazine's original censoring devices, black bars and circular cutouts masking genitalia, are kept rather than removed, so contemporary bodies are viewed through the same apparatus of concealment that shaped the source images decades earlier.

Born in 1973, Champassak is a French artist of Asian heritage whose practice centers on appropriation, décollage, and reiteration: repurposing photographs pulled from flea markets, family albums, and print ephemera. Siam's Guy proved foundational: he later named his own imprint, Siam's Guy Books, after it, and returned to its material for Scraps (RVB Books, 2018), assembled from off-cuts of the original edition. His artist's books have entered major collections and been shown at the Barbican, London, and the ICP Museum, New York.
tags: Collage, Photography, Found Photography, Appropriation Art, Erotic Art

title: Looters
description:
Looters is built entirely from photographs Tiane Doan na Champassak did not take: images of the riots that spread across England in August 2011, pulled from the internet in the days after they occurred.

Self-published in Paris and printed by risograph at Après Midi Lab, the book first appeared in October 2011 in an edition of 150 copies and was reprinted in an expanded second edition of 300 in March 2014, running 52 pages at roughly 15 × 21 cm. Champassak reproduces the found pictures largely without caption or comment, letting the grain and contrast of screen-grabbed and low-resolution source images stand as their own kind of evidence of a moment that unfolded, and was watched, mostly through screens.

The book belongs to a body of self-published, appropriation-based photobooks by Champassak, alongside titles such as Sonagachi and Spleen and Ideal, that treat the accumulation of found or anonymous imagery as a documentary method in its own right. Looters was included in Martin Parr and Gerry Badger's survey The Photobook: A History, Volume III, cited for its refusal to editorialize found material, letting repetition and accumulation do the work of argument.
tags: Photography, Zines, Surveillance Index, Surveillance Index Edition One
notes: Self-published, Paris, risograph printed. Second edition (2014) of 300 copies; first edition (2011) of 150 copies. Edition to be verified against the copy. No ISBN. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-27.

edition_printrun: Sewn in sections with loose dust jacket, choice of 3 cover photo insert card
description:
2041 is an artistic project by Lewis Chaplin in collaboration with Ben Weaver.

Over the course of a year, Lewis initiated a collaborative book-making project with 2041, an anonymous 83-year old British man with a fetish for being fully immersed in materials, clothes, and religious dress. The book is the result of access to 2041's hard drive of 60,000 self-portraits, taken over the course of decades to enact and document his obsession. The book contains 72 photographs and 1 illustration, offset lithoprint on coated and uncoated paper.
