title: Umschläge
edition_printrun: Numbered special edition of 1000; this copy numbered 15/1000
description:
Umschläge is a numbered special edition by the German artist Peter Piller, published by Dashwood Books, New York, in a run of 1,000 copies.

The title, German for "covers" or "envelopes," refers to the paper sleeves used to store and label negatives and prints in newspaper photo archives. They have been the raw material of Piller's practice since the early 2000s, when he began collecting, sorting and recontextualizing vernacular press photography discarded by regional German newspapers. The body of work behind this edition was shown at Andrew Kreps Gallery, New York, in 2013, the year credited on the book's photographs; this special edition followed in 2014, designed by Hans Seeger.

Piller trained as a photographer before turning to appropriation and archival research as his primary method, building series that mine the visual habits of institutional and amateur image-making. Umschläge extends that project from the photographs themselves to the everyday paper systems that once organized and preserved them.
tags: Art, Photography, Found Photography, Conceptual Art
notes: One of two copies in the collection. Catalogue title carried the annotation "(Special Edition) #15"; this refers to the copy number (15 of 1000) in Dashwood Books' numbered special edition, stripped from the title and recorded here. Publisher, edition size, designer and year were confirmed from the colophon printed on the cover itself (Dashwood Books, 2014; design by Hans Seeger; photographs ©2013 Peter Piller) after the artist's own site (peterpiller.de) confirmed Umschläge as a 2013 exhibition and body of work. No ISBN was issued for this small-press special edition. Dashwood Books' own site returns a bot-check (429) to automated requests, so no direct publisher listing could be fetched. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Umschläge
description:
Umschläge, German for "covers," is Peter Piller's deadpan study of a single Cold War-era publication reduced to its outer wrapper.

The book reproduces the front and back covers of Armeerundschau ("Army Review"), the periodical published for the East German National People's Army between 1956 and 1990. Each front cover typically portrays a piece of military hardware or combatants in action; each back cover, by contrast, carries a photograph of a civilian woman in the style of a pin-up. Piller strips the covers of surrounding text and sequences them without commentary, letting the recurring pairing of weapon and woman make its own argument about the propaganda machinery that produced it. The book is offset-printed in color, staple-bound, and was published in an edition of 1000.

Piller's practice is built on the systematic archiving, sorting, and recombination of found photographs, drawn from newspaper picture archives, real-estate listings, and official publications like Armeerundschau. Umschläge belongs to a larger ongoing project, the Archiv Peter Piller, in which found-image categories are catalogued and exhibited as evidence of the visual logic embedded in bureaucratic and state photography.
notes: One of two copies in the collection. Reproduces front and back covers of the East German army magazine Armeerundschau (1956-1990); edition of 1000. No ISBN found on the publisher's or Printed Matter's listing. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Von Willich Aus / Starting from Willich: Photographs 1973–78
description:
In 1972 Sigmar Polke (1941–2010) moved into the Gaspelshof in Willich on the Lower Rhine, which soon became an artist commune. The place had a formative influence on his output: from Willich he set off on numerous journeys with his wife, Katharina Steffen, living and working among a circle of friends. Starting from Willich gathers over one hundred photographs from this period, many never before published or exhibited.

The pictures offer a glimpse into Germany's 1970s alternative scene alongside Polke's darkroom experimentation — multiple exposure, solarization and chemical processing yielding unstable, almost transcendental images. Many stage masquerade scenes: friends in clown-like costume, and Polke himself spontaneously caught on film. An essay by Laszlo Glozer accompanies the plates.

Best known for a restless, materially experimental painting practice that ranged across Pop imagery, chemical processes and found fabrics, Polke treated photography with the same improvisational rigor. This volume offers a focused look at a body of photographic work long overshadowed by his painting.
notes: Bilingual German/English edition. Original stub title "(Starting from Willich)" is the official English half of the bilingual title, not a translator's annotation. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Die Mauer ist Weg!
description:
Die Mauer ist Weg! ("The Wall Is Gone!") revisits the British photographer Mark Power's coverage of Berlin in the days after the fall of the Wall, recasting reportage made in November 1989 as a physical artifact of the event itself.

Self-published in 2014 under Power's own imprint, Globtik Books, to mark the 25th anniversary, the volume is bound as a pastiche of the Berlin newspaper Power bought on the morning after the border opened, its cover embossed into heavy cardboard stock. The early pages read as straight photojournalism before the sequence pulls back from the crowds at the Wall to a quieter, half-emptied East Berlin, and finally to Power's search for Bertolt Brecht's grave; an accompanying essay reflects on chance, choice, and the lessons of the assignment.

Power, a longtime Magnum photographer known for large-scale documentary projects including The Shipping Forecast and 26 Different Endings, made this book from his own archive rather than on assignment, giving it a more personal register within a body of work otherwise defined by commissioned reportage.
notes: Self-published under Power's own imprint, Globtik Books. Edition to be verified against the copy; page count and dimensions not confirmed. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Hoods
description:
This monograph and artist's book documents Richard Prince's painted sculptures created between 1988-2013.

The publication features archival photographs showcasing the evolution of the "Hoods" series, including documentation of Prince's "Body Shop" studio and "Second House" in upstate New York. Prince described his approach as wanting to "paint something that was already painted." The work engages with customized American muscle car design traditions, with pieces titled "Almost Grown," "American Place," "Folksongs," and "Vanishing Point" conveying themes of nostalgia, absence, and loss.

title: American Dream
description: The Rubell Family Collection's substantial and important Richard Prince holdings showcasing his signature pop-culture appropriations wicked silk-screened jokes and pulpy paintings. With an introduction by Mark Coetzee.

title: American English
description:
An artist's book published in conjunction with Prince's exhibition at Sadie Coles HQ (23 April-31 May 2003), turning his own library into photographic subject matter.

Opens with Prince's essay "Collecting: Bring It All Back Home" about his book collection. Features photographs that juxtapose the covers and dust-jackets of American and English editions of books in Prince's collection, photographed in various un-literary backgrounds. The variant dustjackets of American and English editions are often presented side-by-side. Designed by Herman Lelie. Published in glossy pictorial semi-stiff wrappers.
tags: Art, Book Collection, Contemporary Art, Photography

title: Bettie Kline
description:
Conceived by Richard Prince and limited to a thousand copies this large-format artist's book juxtaposes Irving Klaw's photographs of 1950s pinup model Bettie Page with reproductions of artworks by Abstract Expressionist painter Franz Kline.

According to Prince's accompanying text Klaw maintained a studio at the New York address where Kline lived and worked. In Prince's account Kline would sometimes use Klaw's models for figure studies and Page became his secret subject and muse. The book's unexpected pairings of Klaw's photos with Kline's expressive marks produce a frisson of surprise and extend the art historical significance of the female nude.

title: Canal Zone
description:
Published for Prince's 2008 Gagosian exhibition, this catalog documents his Canal Zone series - works inspired by his birthplace in the Panama Canal Zone, a U.S. political exclave until 1979.

The 91-page publication features color reproductions and text by James Frey. These appropriated images became the subject of the landmark Cariou v. Prince copyright case, ultimately decided in Prince's favor on fair use grounds. The catalog's withdrawal from publication makes it a significant artifact in art law history.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Appropriation Art, Photography, Exhibition Catalog, Legal Case, Copyright, Fair Use, Controversial, Withdrawn Publication

title: Check Paintings
description: This catalogue was published in conjunction with the 2005 'Check Paintings' exhibition held at Gagosian Gallery Beverly Hills. Mining images from mass media, advertising and entertainment since the late 1970s, Richard Prince has redefined the concepts of authorship, ownership, and aura. Applying his understanding of the complex transactions of representation to the making of art, he evolved a unique signature filled with echoes of other signatures yet that is unquestionably his own.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Appropriation Art, Finance, Document, Exhibition Catalog, Gagosian

title: Covering Pollock (program)
description:
For this Guild Hall Museum exhibition, Prince created works that literally cover photographs of Jackson Pollock with paint, creating a confrontation between appropriation photography and Abstract Expressionism.

The program features a conversation between Prince and curator Lisa Phillips discussing the works' relationship to Pollock's legacy, the East Hampton art scene where both artists worked, and Prince's ongoing interrogation of authorship and art historical canon. The project connects Prince's appropriation strategies to Abstract Expressionism's gestural spontaneity while asserting his own painterly presence over documentary photography.
tags: Art, Painting, Appropriation Art, Jackson Pollock, Abstract Expressionism, Exhibition Program, East Hampton, Art History, Meta-Painting

title: Free Love
description: Published for Prince's 2016 Sadie Coles HQ exhibition, this catalog presents the Free Love series of paintings. Co-produced with Koenig Books and created in collaboration with Fraser design studio, the publication documents works executed in inkjet, acrylic, and oil stick on canvas. The paintings continue Prince's investigation of appropriated imagery and text-based work, exploring themes of desire, commerce, and digital culture through his characteristic layering techniques.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Appropriation Art, Text Art, Digital Culture, Exhibition Catalog, London, Inkjet

title: Good Life
description:
Published for an exhibition at Glenn Horowitz Bookseller in East Hampton, Good Life presents Prince's photographs of someone else's collection of books on design, photography, cooking, fashion, and interior design.

He stages these books against shifting backgrounds composed of his own artworks, publicity stills, paperbacks, first editions, and CDs. Curator John McWhinnie's introductory essay describes the result as 'an almost surreal still life of books, judged by their covers.' The project examines how books function as objects and how their visual presentation communicates cultural value.
tags: Art, Photography, Books About Books, Still Life, Appropriation Art, Collecting, East Hampton, Limited Edition

title: High Times
description:
Published for the 2018-19 Gagosian exhibitions, this remarkable catalog features reproductions of Prince's latest Hippie Paintings alongside his earlier Hippie Drawings that serve as source material.

The book's most distinctive feature: clear polythene pockets welded into the binding hold facsimile photographs, documents, postcards, and a 7-inch flexi disc of Prince's 1985 composition 'Loud Song.' Essays by Rachel Kushner join reprinted historical texts by Eve Babitz, Joan Didion, and Kim Gordon, creating a layered examination of 1960s counterculture through Prince's appropriation lens.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Counterculture, 1960s, Hippie Culture, Appropriation Art, Exhibition Catalog, Ephemera, Flexi Disc, Innovative Design

title: Inside World
description:
Published for a 1989 Kent Gallery exhibition, Inside World presents Prince's distorted photographs reflecting American machismo iconography—biker culture, heavy metal, stock car racing—alongside artworks by Richard Artschwager, Francis Picabia, Gerhard Richter, Cindy Sherman, and others examining aggressive and sexualized extremes of mass-media culture.

Beautifully bound in red linen with gold lettering, the standard edition of 250 is signed and numbered by Prince. Deluxe editions include an original signed Prince joke. The book showcases Prince's talent as a writer, featuring his understated humor and dry style.
tags: Art, Photography, Exhibition Catalog, Biker Culture, Heavy Metal, Machismo, Appropriation Art, Mass Media, Limited Edition, 1980s

title: It's A Free Concert
description:
Published in 2015 for Richard Prince's exhibition at Kunsthaus Bregenz, this 256-page illustrated hardcover provides an overview of the renowned contemporary artist's career to date.

Edited by Yilmaz Dziewior with texts by Paul Black, Kerstin Stakemeier, and the artist himself, the publication showcases Prince's extraordinary range of media usage and his pioneering appropriation practice. The large-format volume documents major series from his photography, painting, and sculpture, examining how Prince has interrogated authorship, originality, and the circulation of images in contemporary culture over four decades.

title: Jokes & Cartoons
description:
Edited by Beatrix Ruf and conceived by Richard Prince, this publication presents for the first time the complete source material for his celebrated Joke Paintings series.

Beyond the well-known finished works, the book includes never-before-seen examples from Prince's personal collection, unpublished manuscripts, and the original cartoons and jokes themselves. The compilation reveals Prince's working methods and his transformation of found humor into painted artworks, offering unprecedented insight into one of his most iconic series.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Jokes, Text Art, Appropriation Art, Painting, Source Material, Comprehensive

title: Cartoon Jokes
description:
Published for Nahmad Contemporary's 2020 exhibition, this catalog documents Prince's Cartoon Joke paintings, an impressive body of work created between 1988 and 1991.

These large-scale paintings appropriate cartoon imagery and jokes from popular media, transforming them through Prince's characteristic layering of text, image, and gesture. The publication features an essay by Michelle Molokotos, director of Nahmad Contemporary, contextualizing this important early series within Prince's broader appropriation practice.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Appropriation Art, Text Art, Cartoon, Jokes, Exhibition Catalog, 1980s Art, 1990s Art

title: Kaliflower
description:
Prince's Kaliflower appropriates and recontextualizes a Bay Area commune newspaper from the late 1960s-early 1970s, transforming hippie-era ephemera into an artwork examining counterculture idealism, communal living, and underground publishing.

Published through his Fulton Ryder imprint, the book continues Prince's investigation of American subcultures and vernacular print media. The slim hardcover presents the newspaper's raw aesthetic, including classified ads, manifestos, and graphics from the height of the commune movement.
tags: Art, Appropriation Art, Counterculture, Hippie Culture, 1960s, Bay Area, Commune, Underground Press

title: Naked Nurses
description:
Published in an edition of 1,000 copies, Naked Nurses extends Prince's engagement with the nurse as cultural archetype by appropriating vintage erotic photographs and pulp imagery.

The book functions as both artwork and source material reference, revealing the found images Prince transformed in his celebrated Nurse Paintings of the early 2000s. The publication bridges his photographic appropriation practice and his later painting series, and it shows how vernacular erotica becomes high art through recontextualization.
tags: Art, Photography, Appropriation Art, Nurses, Erotica, Vintage Photography, Pulp Culture

title: New Figures
description: New Figures presents Richard Prince's appropriated and manipulated found photographs that evoke charged imagery through drawn lines, pale washes of color, and collaged shapes. Published on the occasion of Prince's 2014 exhibition at Almine Rech Gallery in Paris.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Appropriation Art, Photography, Collage, Pictures Generation

title: Phillips
description:
This major museum catalog accompanied Prince's first significant retrospective, establishing him as a central figure in appropriation art and the Pictures Generation.

Phillips's introduction provides critical framework for understanding Prince's revolutionary rephotography practice. The extended conversation with Larry Clark explores Prince's working methods, influences, and conceptual approach to image-making. Published at a pivotal moment in Prince's career, the catalog documents his Cowboys, Girlfriends, and other iconic series that redefined authorship and originality in contemporary art.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Photography, Appropriation Art, Exhibition Catalog, Retrospective, Whitney Museum, Pictures Generation

title: Photographs / Paintings
description:
Published for major museum exhibitions in Switzerland and Germany, this elegant three-volume set is conceived and designed by Richard Prince himself.

The two main volumes are dedicated to photography and painting, each featuring full-page reproductions representing Prince's ultimate selection of works characteristic of his oeuvre. A third insert volume contains the exhibition checklist, introductions by the museum curators, and Bruce Hainley's essay 'Imitation of Life while thinking about Richard Prince.' The large-format artist's books present over 100 color plates of Prince's appropriated, repurposed, and altered images with accompanying captions.

title: Protest Paintings
description:
Published for the 2015 Skarstedt Gallery exhibition, this 168-page fully illustrated catalog is the first publication devoted to Prince's Protest Paintings series created between 1989-1995.

Painted on vertical canvases shaped like protest placards, the works alternate between monochromatic minimalism and richly layered colorful abstraction. The paintings incorporate printed and handwritten jokes and silkscreened pattern details, exemplifying Prince's appropriation practice. Accompanied by Prince's essay 'Half-Mast,' an extract from his memoirs 'Tell Me Everything,' the catalog documents this important transitional body of work.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Abstract Art, Text Art, Appropriation Art, Protest, Minimalism, Exhibition Catalog, 1990s Art

title: Richard Prince
description:
This landmark 368-page monograph accompanied Prince's major Guggenheim retrospective, presenting the full scope of his work from 1970s appropriation photography through mid-2000s Nurse and Hood paintings.

Curator Nancy Spector's extensive essay positions Prince as the defining artist of image-based appropriation, while Rian and Storr provide additional critical perspectives. The title 'Spiritual America' references Prince's controversial 1983 appropriation of Garry Gross's photograph of Brooke Shields. With 438 color images, the catalog remains the essential reference on Prince's first three decades of practice.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Photography, Painting, Appropriation Art, Exhibition Catalog, Retrospective, Guggenheim Museum, Comprehensive

title: Richard Prince + Zach Sebastian
description:
This 24-page publication is a collaboration between filmmaker Zach Sebastian and artist Richard Prince.

The images are reappropriated from an unreleased film Sebastian made about a community of Americans in Dayton, Illinois, where residents believed Japanese people were buying up the United States and organized to fight back by destroying Japanese cars and motorcycles. Sebastian initially approached Prince over email with photos and a pitch, quickly receiving approval.

The first printing (2015) was limited to 200 numbered copies a second extended edition followed in 2018 with 500 copies. Printed in black and white offset, the zine exemplifies Prince's continued engagement with appropriation, xenophobia, and American cultural paranoia.
tags: Art, Photography, Zine, Appropriation Art, Documentary, Collaboration, Limited Edition, American Culture

title: Second House
description:
Prince's Second House was a ranch-style structure in upstate New York that functioned as both gallery space and artwork.

The Guggenheim Museum acquired this installation in 2005, recognizing it as a significant work blurring boundaries between architecture, sculpture, and photography. Tragically, the structure was destroyed by a lightning-caused fire in 2007. This catalog serves as the primary documentation of an important but ephemeral work, featuring photographs of the property, its interiors, and the iconic 1973 Plymouth Barracuda that was part of the installation.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Installation Art, Architecture, Photography, Exhibition Catalog, Americana, Site-Specific Art

title: SHE
description:
This groundbreaking exhibition catalog examines the relationship between Beat artist Wallace Berman (1926-1976) and Richard Prince, focusing on their shared interest in appropriating imagery from men's magazines.

Kristine McKenna's essay provides critical context for understanding how Berman's pioneering collage work in the 1950s-60s presaged Prince's 1990s-2000s Girlfriends paintings. The publication reveals previously unseen Berman works and includes Prince's Car installation. Together they trace the lineage between Beat-era assemblage and Pictures Generation appropriation.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Photography, Collage, Exhibition Catalog, Beat Generation, Appropriation Art, Los Angeles Art

title: Special Guest
description:
Published for a 2015 Gagosian Gallery exhibition, 'Special Guest' brings together two photographers who interrogate the limits of image-making through appropriation and commercial aesthetics.

Prince, the pioneer of appropriation art, and Ethridge, known for blending commissioned photography with personal work, create a visual dialogue that reflects on each artist's practice as seen through the other's lens. The publication explores how images circulate, transform, and accumulate meaning in contemporary visual culture.
tags: Art, Photography, Collaboration, Appropriation Art, Contemporary Art, Commercial Photography

title: The Girl Next Door
description: Published for simultaneous exhibitions 'Upstate' at MAK Center Los Angeles and '4 x 4' at MAK Vienna in spring 2000. The bilingual publication examines Prince's engagement with found imagery and the mythology of American domestic life, particularly his interest in the 'girl next door' archetype drawn from mass media and advertising culture.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Photography, Appropriation Art, Exhibition Catalog, Americana, Pop Culture

title: The Magic Castle
description: Published for Prince's exhibition at Le Consortium in Dijon, this bilingual artist book presents a rare glimpse into Prince's early photographic work from his time as a student in France. The work characteristically blurs authorship by combining his own slides with appropriated commercial photographs, presaging his later practice of questioning originality and ownership in image-making.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Photography, Appropriation Art, Exhibition Catalog, Early Work

title: untitled (band) 2013/2014
description: This limited publication presents Prince's explorations of band imagery, music ephemera, and performance culture through paintings and collages. The work extends his ongoing fascination with subcultures and vernacular aesthetics, transforming found materials into artworks that question authenticity and authorship. Published by Milan's A&M bookstore Edizioni, known for experimental artist publications.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Music, Collage, Appropriation Art, Limited Edition

title: White Paintings
description: Documents Prince's exploration of painting on white or light-colored grounds, a departure from his darker canvases. The series demonstrates Prince's continued engagement with appropriation, text, and mark-making while investigating the formal properties of white space and negative image. Published by Skarstedt Gallery, which has represented Prince since the 1990s and mounted numerous solo exhibitions of his work.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Exhibition Catalog, Appropriation Art, Monochrome

title: Family Tweets
description:
Gagosian will present Family Tweets, a new book by Richard Prince published through Fulton Ryder.

Works from the publication will be on view in the 976 Madison Avenue gallery behind the bookstore. Family Tweets documents Prince's project at Desert X in Southern California's Coachella Valley in 2017. The site offered to Prince was an abandoned house in Desert Hot Springs, where he installed, inside and out, printouts from his Birdtalk blog relating to his family, most of which were posted on the @richardprince4 Twitter feed in 2014. The printouts were made in a variety of mediums.

Three days after the installation, once Prince had left, most of the works were removed, taken, seized—gobbled up, so to speak—by art hikers with flashlights." Neither he nor the organizers had any "remote viewing" about what would happen to the artworks after he left there was never any thought about "guarding" them. It wasn't exactly comme ci, comme ça, but let's just say the whole project turned into one of those sixties free concerts—80 percent of the works disappeared. The works on view are examples of what was retrieved after the event was over."

title: Untitled (Original Cowboy)
description: Matched with an artwork by Richard Prince, the publication is part of Gagosian’s Picture Books, an imprint conceived by author Emma Cline and dedicated to publishing fiction by leading authors alongside contributions by celebrated contemporary artists.

title: Yea Yea Yea
description:
Published by Harper's Books in East Hampton, this ephemeral artist publication draws parallels between Stuart Sutcliffe (the 'Fifth Beatle' who left the band to pursue painting and died young) and Prince's own appropriation strategies.

The slim booklet functions as both artwork and commentary on artistic mythology, premature death, and the romance of the artist-dropout. Prince's interest in Sutcliffe connects to his broader engagement with music culture and figures who exist at the margins of canonical narratives.

title: Bibliothèque d’un Amateur
description:
This expanded edition chronicles Prince's prolific output of self-published artist books, exhibition catalogs, and ephemera through his private Fulton Ryder imprint and various galleries.

The publication itself functions as a Prince work, cataloging his parallel practice of book-making alongside his better-known paintings and photographs. With texts by Vincent Pécoil and Yann Sérandour, it documents over 200 publications spanning Prince's engagement with appropriation, cowboys, nurses, jokes, Instagram, and ephemeral culture.

title: Provoke: Complete Reprint of 3 Volumes
binding: Softcover, boxed set of 3 volumes plus booklet
contributors: Takuma Nakahira (Photography), Yutaka Takanashi (Photography), Takahiko Okada (Text), Daido Moriyama (Photography)
description:
Provoke reproduces, in full, the three issues of the short-lived dojin-shi (self-published magazine) that reshaped postwar Japanese photography.

Founded in November 1968 by critic Koji Taki and photographer Takuma Nakahira, with poet Takahiko Okada and photographer Yutaka Takanashi as founding members, Provoke carried the subtitle "Provocative Materials for Thought." Daido Moriyama joined for the second and third issues. Each number combined grainy, blurred, out-of-focus photographs — mocked at the time as are-bure-boke — with essays and poems, and the group dissolved after a fourth publication, First, Abandon the World of Pseudo-Certainty, that surveyed the three issues together. This edition, published by Nitesha, restores the original image sizes and all original texts, including Okada's essays omitted from an earlier facsimile box set, and adds a booklet of complete English and Chinese translations.

Original copies of Provoke are almost never seen outside archives and museum collections, and its rough, anti-descriptive style went on to influence generations of Japanese photographers, Moriyama chief among them. This reprint is the fullest facsimile edition of the magazine's short run currently available.
notes: Facsimile reprint of the three 1968-1970 issues of Provoke magazine, published by Nitesha (Tokyo); catalogued under the magazine's own name, as the original publication had no single author. No ISBN found for this edition. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Rob Pruitt's eBay Flea Market: Year One
description:
Rob Pruitt's eBay Flea Market: Year One documents the opening chapter of Pruitt's ongoing flea-market project, first staged in New York and since restaged internationally.

The project takes the form of a live, open flea market: Pruitt invites artists, dealers, collectors and passersby to set up tables and sell whatever they bring, collapsing the distinctions between artwork, souvenir, and secondhand junk that structure the conventional art market. This book gathers photographic documentation of that first edition alongside a critical text by Tommaso Speretta situating the project within Pruitt's broader interest in participation, commerce, and spectacle. It was published by Bruno as a 296-page paperback.

Pruitt is an American artist known for work that moves fluidly between painting, sculpture, and social practice, often using humor and popular imagery — pandas, cocaine, celebrity gossip — to needle at ideas of taste and value in the art world. The Flea Market project extends that inquiry into a live, collective format, treating the marketplace itself as the artwork.
notes: Publisher confirmed as Bruno via AbeBooks JSON-LD; publisher location/url and exact dimensions unconfirmed this session. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Terrestre
description:
Terrestre is a photographic study of rural France by Arnaud Pyvka, published in a 156-page hardcover by the Paris house Marc Bervillé Éditions.

Pyvka's colour photographs move through the French countryside, its landscapes, weather and the people who work and live on the land, building a portrait less of any single place than of a persistent, unglamorous rural condition. The book includes a text by the writer Julien Carreyn and was designed by Myriam Barchechat, at a trim size of 20 x 29.7 cm.

Pyvka works between documentary and landscape photography, and Terrestre belongs to a body of work concerned with the physical, working land of France rather than its cities. That subject is carried by his photographs and by Carreyn's accompanying text alike.
notes: Cover sourced from Fact Form Fiction's own image gallery; the specific product page could not be re-fetched (404 on the guessed slug, and the shop's search endpoint did not return the title). Bibliographic details (publisher, pages, dimensions, contributors) confirmed by web search and consistent across sources; artist biography not found. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Black Rodeo
description: This book is published in conjunction with the artist's debut European solo exhibition, BLACK RODEO: Cowboys of the 21st Century, held between March 10 and April 16, 2022 at Almine Rech Brussels.

title: Mel Ramos: New Prints: Catalogue Raisonné of Original Prints
Neo Rauch
contributors: Wolfgang Büscher (Essay), Harald Kunde (Essay), Gary Tinterow (Essay)
description:
This oversized Taschen monograph gathers the essential overview of Neo Rauch's paintings, canvases built from startling juxtapositions of figures, architecture, and unresolved narrative.

Across 462 pages, the book reproduces Rauch's work at large scale, drawing on a deep consideration of philosophy, art history, and literature alongside the artist's own dreamscape. Essays by Wolfgang Büscher, Harald Kunde, and Gary Tinterow, edited by Hans Werner Holzwarth, situate the paintings within the history of German figurative painting and Rauch's training at the Leipzig Academy, with text in English, French, and German. The trade edition's large trim size lets the book stand as a surrogate for the paintings' own scale and detail.

Rauch emerged from the so-called New Leipzig School, absorbing the technical rigor of Socialist Realist painting under his teacher Arno Rink and redirecting it toward scenes that resist single interpretation: figures caught mid-gesture in landscapes and interiors that mix industrial infrastructure with folkloric and mythological imagery. This volume, published to accompany a period of major museum surveys, remains the fullest single-volume record of that body of work.
notes: Trade edition of Taschen's oversized Neo Rauch monograph, edited by Hans Werner Holzwarth. Original catalogue title stub read "Oversized Taschen Book -"; identified via ISBN as this 2012 monograph. Dimensions not confirmed against the copy; edition to be verified. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Neo Rauch: Paintings Edited by Hans-Werner Schmidt, Bernhart Schwenk
Dromos
contributors: Ralph Keuning (Text), Ulf Küster (Text), Harald Kunde (Text), Norman Rosenthal (Text), Klaus Werner (Text)
description:
Dromos, Paintings 1993–2017 surveys the painting career of Neo Rauch (born 1960), from his first solo exhibition in 1993 at Galerie Eigen + Art in Leipzig through the present day, tracing developments in his work with examples drawn from prominent international collections.

Accompanying essays by curators and art historians including Ralph Keuning, Ulf Küster, Harald Kunde, Norman Rosenthal and Klaus Werner provide grounding in the complex iconography and pictorial logic that runs through Rauch's oeuvre. The volume was published alongside an exhibition of the same title at Museum de Fundatie.

Rauch studied under Arno Rink at the Hochschule für Grafik und Buchkunst in Leipzig while Germany was still divided; after reunification, his large, enigmatic paintings — combining elements of Pop art, comics and socialist-era advertising graphics — established him as the leading figure of the New Leipzig School.

notes: ISBN was already known from the stub row (edition_printrun field); confirmed against AbeBooks and artbook.com. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Scenarios
description:
Scenarios presents the paintings Robert Rauschenberg made in the final years of his life, monumental compositions that fuse his signature transfer-printed photographic imagery with passages of bare, unpainted canvas.

Published by PaceWildenstein on the occasion of the exhibition at its New York gallery, January 14 - February 5, 2005, the catalogue reproduces the Scenarios series across 47 pages alongside an essay by the novelist Oscar Hijuelos. Each work pairs Rauschenberg's characteristic layering of found photographic and printed imagery, drawn from his own extensive archive, with expanses of raw canvas that isolate and quiet the surrounding imagery, a departure in restraint from the denser collage aesthetic of his earlier combines and silkscreens.

Rauschenberg (1925-2008) had by this point spent five decades dismantling the boundary between painting and everyday material, from the Combines of the 1950s through his Cardboards, Jammers, and Anagrams series; Scenarios, made in his eighties, shows that restless experimentation continuing to the end of his career.

Distinct from the related 2006 PaceWildenstein catalogue "Scenarios and the Ancient Incident" (ISBN 9781930743663); confirmed by title, essayist, and page count. title: Runts
description:
Runts documents an exhibition of new work Robert Rauschenberg made in the final years of his career, shown at PaceWildenstein in New York from January 11 to February 16, 2008.

The Runts series continues Rauschenberg's decades-long method of combining photographic transfer, collage and paint on unconventional supports, layering found street imagery, printed text and everyday objects into dense compositions. The catalogue reproduces the works shown in the exhibition, presenting them as a late chapter in a practice built on assemblage and appropriation.

Rauschenberg (1925-2008) was a central figure in postwar American art, moving between painting, sculpture, printmaking and performance and doing more than any other artist of his generation to blur the line between artwork and everyday material. Runts was among the last bodies of work he completed before his death in May 2008.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Collage, Exhibition Catalog
notes: Catalogue for Rauschenberg's Runts exhibition at PaceWildenstein, Jan 11 - Feb 16, 2008. Corrected catalogue misspelling "Rauchenberg" to "Rauschenberg". Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: The Sun's Coming Up... Like a Big Bald Head
Rogerio REIS : Ninguém é de Ninguém Impériale Collection n°4
Portraits
description:
Portraits gathers Gerhard Richter's paintings of the human face into a single survey, tracking one of the most persistent threads running through his otherwise restless body of work.

Published to accompany an exhibition at the Museumsberg Flensburg, the catalogue reproduces portraits spanning Richter's career, from the blurred, photo-derived likenesses of family members and public figures made in the 1960s to later, more painterly and abstracted treatments of the face. Essays by Stefan Gronert and Hubertus Butin examine how Richter has used the portrait to interrogate photography, memory, and the limits of painted representation, rather than to record likeness for its own sake. Hatje Cantz published the 254-page hardcover catalogue in 2006.

Richter, born in Dresden in 1932, is among the most influential painters of the postwar period, moving between photorealism, abstraction, and conceptual strategies without settling into any one of them. The portrait recurs across that range as a private counterpoint to his large abstract and history paintings, and this volume is one of the few to isolate it as a subject in its own right.
tags: Painting, Portraiture, Exhibition Catalog, Contemporary Art
notes: Exhibition catalogue published with the Museumsberg Flensburg show. Publisher url and physical dimensions unconfirmed this session. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Gerhard Richter: Life and Work in Painting Thinking is Painting
Tom
description:
Tom is a book of vintage found photographs assembled by the artist Doug Rickard, published by Little Big Man Books in a limited edition, now out of print.

Rickard built the book around a cache of anonymous photographs — black-and-white images from the 1960s of women, stockinged and stylish, shot from a distance on the streets of Los Angeles by an unknown photographer. Named for the peeping Tom, the book presents these images with their voyeuristic origin intact rather than smoothed over, letting the era's noir-tinged nostalgia sit alongside the plain fact of covert surveillance.

Rickard is known for photographic projects built from appropriated and remote-sourced imagery, including his Google Street View series A New American Picture. Tom extends that interest in found and secondhand ways of seeing into an explicitly voyeuristic historical archive, using it to draw a line from Cold War-era street surveillance to the present.
