notes: Cover sourced from the publisher's own product image; original PNG converted to JPEG. Out of print; the publisher's listing gives no page count, dimensions or numbered print run. No ISBN found. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: 78-87 London Youth
description:
Photographs taken in the streets, clubs, basements and bars of London between 1978 and 1987, celebrating the many mutations in London's youth culture from the height of punk to the birth of Acid House.

These photographs, made over a ten-year span, capture punk's evolution into goth, the skinhead revival and the New Romantic scene, and the eventual emergence of Acid House and the new psychedelia. Among those portrayed are Boy George, Andrew Logan, Leigh Bowery and his boyfriend Trojan, Michael Alig, John Galliano, Hamish Bowles, Cerith Wyn Evans, Steve Strange and Martin Kemp and Steve Norman of Spandau Ballet. A testament to the creative spirit of youth with emphasis on sartorial DIY panache.
tags: British Photography, Music & Nightlife, Punk & New Wave, Street Photography, Youth Culture, Photography, New Romantic, Goth, London, 1980s

title: Pipilotti Rist: Pixel Forest
description:
The most comprehensive monograph to date on Pipilotti Rist, this book surveys the work of a pioneer of experimental video art celebrated for installations that bridge fine art and popular culture, the natural world and the technological sublime.

Through vivid color, audaciously sensuous imagery, and playful sexuality, Rist's work, ranging from single-channel videos to multilayered environments, is presented here in a hyperfeminine aesthetic interlaced with deeper themes of pain, innocence, and transformation. The 208-page hardcover volume was published by Phaidon in association with the New Museum, New York, to accompany Pipilotti Rist: Pixel Forest, Rist's largest survey exhibition in the United States, and is edited by curators Massimiliano Gioni and Margot Norton.

Rist has worked since the late 1980s to expand video art beyond the single screen, submerging viewers in projected color, sound, and architecture. Pixel Forest, the installation that gives this book its title, hung thousands of illuminated silicone tubes through a gallery as a physical counterpart to her moving-image work, and the monograph traces that trajectory from her early single-channel videos through the room-scale environments for which she is best known.
notes: Published with the New Museum to accompany Rist's 2016 survey Pixel Forest, her largest US exhibition to date. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Elixir: The Video Organism of Pipilotti Rist
description:
Elixir: The Video Organism of Pipilotti Rist accompanied a large-scale survey of the Swiss artist's video installations, shown at Museum Boijmans van Beuningen in Rotterdam and the Museum of Contemporary Art Kiasma in Helsinki in 2009. The title frames Rist's body of work as a living organism, an apt description for practice built from saturated color, immersive projection and the body as both subject and screen.

The catalog, designed by Irma Boom, brings together essays and documentation surveying installations from across Rist's career, with contributions from curator Sjarel Ex and writer Paul Kempers among others, situating the work within her ongoing exploration of intimacy, the domestic and the natural world refracted through video.

Rist (born 1962) has been a defining figure in video art since the 1980s, pioneering immersive, room-scale installations — from Pickelporno to Pour Your Body Out at MoMA — that dissolve the boundary between screen and viewer. Elixir remains one of the fullest institutional surveys of that practice.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Video Art, Exhibition Catalog
notes: Original stub title "The video organism of Pipilotti" was a truncation of the full title "Elixir: The Video Organism of Pipilotti Rist." Two ISBNs (9789069182377 / 9789069182360) resolve to the same OpenLibrary edition record; this record uses the first. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Fifth Honeymoon
contributors: Sianne Ngai (Text), Matias Faldbakken (Text), Steinar Sekkingstad (Text), Axel Wieder (Text)
description:
Fifth Honeymoon collects Torbjørn Rødland's recent photographs, images that stage familiar subjects — hands, food, teenagers, domestic objects — until they curdle into something uncanny.

Rødland works in a highly controlled studio style closer to advertising or fashion photography than documentary practice, using that polish to unsettle rather than reassure. The pictures gathered here recur across bodies and objects treated as interchangeable material, building a private symbolic language out of banal props. The volume includes critical texts by the theorist Sianne Ngai and the artist Matias Faldbakken, alongside contributions from Steinar Sekkingstad and Axel Wieder, and was published by Sternberg Press with US distribution through MIT Press.

Rødland, a Norwegian photographer based in Los Angeles, has built a body of work that sits between fine-art photography and vernacular image-making, exhibited widely at institutions including the Serpentine Galleries and the Astrup Fearnley Museum. Fifth Honeymoon extends the deadpan, quietly disturbing register of earlier books such as Vanilla Partner and Nature Photos.
notes: Publisher's spelling "Rodland" corrected to "Rødland" per the artist's own name. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Vanilla Partner
description:
Vanilla Partner collects a body of staged color photographs by the Norwegian artist Torbjørn Rødland, built from pairings and juxtapositions that feel simultaneously banal and quietly wrong.

Rødland works in a highly controlled, almost clinical style of studio and location photography, posing bodies, food, and everyday objects into compositions that carry an undertow of discomfort, humor, or desire without resolving into any single reading. The book's title nods to the flatness and blandness Rødland's images seem to court on the surface, even as their content pushes toward the strange. MACK published the 158-page hardcover in 2012.

Rødland, based between Los Angeles and Oslo, has built a distinctive body of photographic work over three decades that treats the medium's technical polish as a tool for unease rather than reassurance, exhibiting widely at institutions including the Serpentine Galleries and Fotomuseum Winterthur. Vanilla Partner sits within a run of MACK-published monographs — including Fifth Honeymoon and The Touch That Made You — that trace this recurring visual language across his career.
notes: Publisher url and physical dimensions unconfirmed this session. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Sasquatch Century
description:
Sasquatch Century is a midcareer survey of the Norwegian photographer Torbjørn Rødland (b. 1970), published by Walther König in association with Mousse Publishing.

The book gathers a selection of Rødland's photographs from the past twenty years, guiding readers through a visual language that sits deliberately on the border between the constructed and the authentic — carefully staged images that nonetheless read with documentary conviction. Essays by curators Linda Norden and Milena Høegsberg accompany the plates in this 152-page hardcover, illustrated with 56 colour images.

Rødland has exhibited internationally since the 1990s, developing a body of work known for its uncanny mix of formal photographic control and unresolved, often uncomfortable subject matter — bodies, objects and interiors photographed with a straight-faced intensity that resists easy reading. Sasquatch Century is among the fullest surveys of that practice to date.
notes: Row author spelled without diacritics ("Torbjorn Rodland"); corrected to Torbjørn Rødland. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Confabulations
description:
A dictionary will tell you that confabulations are memory disturbances, the sincere production of fabricated, distorted memories about oneself and the world, made without any conscious intention to deceive.

With Confabulations, Torbjorn Rodland presents a set of analogue photographs that subtly misrepresent broken memories and childhood fantasies, distorting facts to get at a different order of truth. The book gathers Rodland's staged, uncannily lit images of bodies, objects, and domestic scenes, treating fragmentation not as something to reject or induce but as a starting point for unexpected connections between pictures. It is published by MACK as a clothbound hardcover with foil-stamped titling.

Rodland has spent two decades photographing with a deliberately anachronistic, almost commercial sheen, using the vocabulary of advertising and studio photography to unsettle rather than reassure. Confabulations continues that project, treating the camera and its attendant apparatus of lenses, lighting, and film as one point of connectivity among many rather than a neutral recorder of the world.
notes: Clothbound MACK hardcover; page count and trim size not confirmed against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: The Touch That Made You
description:
The Touch That Made You was published for Torbjørn Rødland's first UK exhibition, at the Serpentine Galleries in 2017. The show surveyed staged photographs spanning two decades of the Los Angeles-based, Norwegian-born artist's practice.

Rødland's images (portraits, still lifes and landscapes built from deliberately awkward staging and glossy, analog-photography surfaces) work to defamiliarize and disrupt the realm of the everyday, returning obsessively to motifs of produce, body parts and viscous substances. The exhibition also included his 2005 film 132 BPM, which animates its subjects to a driving rhythmic beat. The catalog's title, per the gallery, gestures at once to the physical and immaterial aspects of the images: the rays of light and liquid touches that reveal a photograph in the darkroom, and the framing and staging enacted through the lens.

Rødland has published extensively with MACK and other art-book presses; this Serpentine/Koenig Books catalog, edited by Amira Gad and Joseph Constable, is the institutional survey accompanying his first major UK show.
tags: Art, Photography, Contemporary Art, Exhibition Catalog
notes: No usable cover image found across AbeBooks, OpenLibrary, artbook.com, or the Serpentine/Koenig Books/MACK shop endpoints (all either 404 or don't stock this title) — cover to be photographed. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Time and Space on the Lower East Side
description:
Time and Space on the Lower East Side pairs photographs Brian Rose and Ed Fausty made of Manhattan's Lower East Side in 1980 with pictures Rose returned to shoot from the same vantage points three decades later, tracking one neighborhood's transformation street by street.

Published by Golden Section Publishers with a foreword by the musician and Lower East Side native Suzanne Vega, the 130-page book sets the 1980 and 2010 photographs of Rose and Fausty's original large-format survey against each other in matched pairs, documenting the shift from a landscape of tenement decay, empty lots, and social housing to one reshaped by gentrification. The photographers worked with a view camera on both passes, giving the comparison a consistent, deliberate formality.

Rose, based in New York and later Amsterdam, has built a career on long-duration documentary projects tracking urban change, including his ongoing photographing of the Lower East Side since the 1980s and later work along the former path of the Berlin Wall; Time and Space extends that method to the neighborhood where his career as a documentary photographer began.
notes: Published in both hardcover and softcover; some copies are signed limited editions of 1000. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Headshots
description:
Headshots collects Aura Rosenberg's series of portraits photographing male artists' faces during orgasm, cropped tight to isolate expression from context.

Rosenberg photographed each subject — largely artists and figures from New York's downtown art scene — in stark black and white, presenting the images without identifying captions so that the faces read first as abstracted studies of sensation. The book pairs the photographs with texts by novelist Lynne Tillman and writer Gary Indiana, and was published by Stop Over Press in 1996 alongside a related exhibition at Barbara Gladstone Gallery.

Rosenberg is a New York-based artist whose work across photography, sculpture and collaboration has repeatedly used sexuality and appropriated imagery to needle at ideas of authorship and desire, including her long-running collaborative project with her daughter Lena Henke and her earlier collage series pairing pornographic images with children's toys. Headshots remains one of her best-known individual bodies of work.
notes: AbeBooks lists this title's publisher as Barbara Gladstone Gallery (with text by Gary Indiana); OpenLibrary lists Stop Over Press and adds Lynne Tillman as a text contributor. Both names appear on the cover, so both are recorded as texts; likely co-published alongside a Gladstone Gallery show. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: James Rosenquist: the Big Paintings: Thirty Years
contributors: by Leo Castelli (Author), Susan Brundage (Author), Craig Adcock (Author)

title: James Rosenquist
contributors: by New York. Whitney Museum of American Art. Text by Marcia Tucker catalog of prints by Elke M. Solom (Author)

title: A Retrospective
contributors: Julia Blaut, Ruth E. Fine, Eugene E. Epstein
description:
Lipsticks, automobiles, dishwashers, men in business suits, spaghetti, rockets, airplanes, hairdryers, ice cream cones and pigtailed girls.

James Rosenquist has always known how to combine these seemingly disparate but always all-American elements into whirlwind, billboard-sized collages of airbrushed surreal euphoria, slamming colors, patterns and objects into one another with the eye of an advertising man and the heart of a Pop Artist. This momentous catalogue, published to accompany the first in-depth survey of the artist's work since 1972, gives long-overdue, in-depth attention to Rosenquist's singular achievement in American art.

Extensive illustrations cover major works in diverse media, including work on paper that reveals the artist's process, as well as extensive new and archival photography. Essays focus on areas that have only been superficially addressed in the literature to date, bringing the level of Rosenquist scholarship up to that of his Pop Art contemporaries. The book offers a comprehensive overview of Rosenquist's career, including essays on his unique style, collage, prints, and his connection to scientific phenomena. It features nearly 300 works and includes a definitive biography, exhibition history, and illustrated chronology.
tags: Art, Museum Publications, Pop Art, American Art, Contemporary Art, Collage

title: Welcome to the Walter Planet and House of Fire 1988-1989
King of Diamonds
description:
King of Diamonds began as an editorial photography assignment at Miami's King of Diamonds strip club and was reshaped by Ben Rosenzweig into a self-published artist's book.

Working afterward with an art director friend, Rosenzweig re-edited and re-sequenced the material away from its original editorial context, producing a small, perfect-bound paperback of roughly 32 pages issued in a numbered edition of 100. The book circulated through independent photobook venues, including Dashwood Books, Printed Matter in New York, and Colette in Paris, and a selection of its images was recognized in the American Photography 31 annual.

Rosenzweig is a New York-based photographer whose editorial and personal work often turns commercial or documentary assignments into more open-ended, self-authored projects. King of Diamonds is an example of that process, a commissioned shoot recast as an independently published book.
notes: No ISBN — self-published, numbered edition of 100. Sold through Dashwood Books, Printed Matter, and Colette. Cover auto-cropped from an angled product photo; edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Secrets
binding: Loose sheets, printed card cover, in slipcase
edition_printrun: First edition, loose sheets under printed card cover, in slipcase
description:
Secrets is a collection of black-and-white portraits by the Italian photographer Paolo Roversi, published under his own imprint, Editions Stromboli, to coincide with a 2013 exhibition at the Fotografiska museum in Stockholm.

The photographs draw on both Roversi's fashion work and more personal, unpublished images, presented not as a bound book but as loose printed sheets housed under a card cover and slipcase. The format treats the pictures as individual objects rather than fixed pages. The project was produced with Antoine de Beaupré.

Roversi has photographed for the world's leading fashion magazines and houses for four decades, working largely with Polaroid and large-format cameras to build a body of work defined by soft focus, muted tone and a persistent sense of intimacy bordering on mystery. Secrets gathers material that sits outside that commercial output, closer to the photographer's own private register.
notes: Sources disagree on page count (40 pages per the publisher's own current listing vs. 76 pages per a French bookseller listing) and print run (1000 vs. 1500 copies), and the publisher's own site currently dates the listing to October 2015, which most likely reflects a later restock rather than the first edition — most booksellers, including a listing explicitly marked "FIRST EDT," give 2013. Recorded here as the 2013 first edition; page count and print run left unresolved rather than forced to a single figure. No ISBN — small-press, self-published imprint. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Superstition
description:
Superstition exists in a castle in the sky: a sequence of dream-like landscapes and portraits by Henry Roy, drawn from different times and places, that settles into one coherent, self-evolved atmosphere rather than a single story.

The book was edited and designed by Études Studio and published by Études Books, Paris, as the eighteenth title in their publications series. It runs 48 pages in full-color offset, bound in blue cloth with cover embossing on the front, spine, and back, with text in both English and French. Roy's images move associatively between portraiture and landscape, favoring atmosphere and psychological suggestion over documentary record.

Born in Port-au-Prince and based in Paris since childhood, Roy began publishing photobooks in 1996 with Regards Noirs, a series of portraits of prominent Black French figures made in the manner of Richard Avedon and Irving Penn. Superstition is one of six artist's books he has produced since, a body of work that also includes Out of the Blue, Spirit, Mirage, and Ibiza Memories.
notes: Études Books N°18; edition of 300; ISBN taken from the cover imprint. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: LA/BJ
description:
Struck by the eerie similarities between the giant megalopolises of Los Angeles and Beijing, Sterling Ruby (born 1972) takes the reader into his own journalistic vision, sourcing photographs of landscapes and interiors of the two cities, both shot and found by the artist. Each page is claustrophobically framed by collaged imagery of stalagmites and stalactites; where the two cities merge, the book gives rise to a dystopian scene that reads like science fiction.

LA/BJ was commissioned by the Ullens Center for Contemporary Art (UCCA) in Beijing as part of The Los Angeles Project, a series of individual artist books following in the tradition of John Baldessari and Edward Ruscha. Ruby was joined by fellow Los Angeles artists Kathryn Andrews, Aaron Curry, Alex Israel, Matthew Monahan, Ryan Trecartin and Kaari Upson, each contributing a book exploring the LA–Beijing pairing.

Ruby's practice spans sculpture, ceramics, textile and photography, frequently addressing incarceration, urban decay and the built environment; LA/BJ extends that interest in fractured, entropic cityscapes into a photographic and collage format.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Photography, Artist Book
notes: Part of a series of individually authored artist books commissioned by UCCA Beijing for 'The Los Angeles Project'; identified via WebSearch after the AbeBooks/OpenLibrary/publisher ladder missed it (title too short/generic to match on AbeBooks). Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Interieurs
publisher: Verlag der Buchhandlung Walther und Franz König
description:
Interieurs collects photographs Thomas Ruff made as a student at the Dusseldorf Art Academy, quiet, precisely framed pictures of the modest apartments of family and friends in Germany's Black Forest region.

Published by Verlag der Buchhandlung Walther und Franz König and edited by Martin Germann, the 108-page hardcover reproduces the series in 48 color images and one black-and-white photograph, accompanied by text from the writer Thomas Bernhard. Made between 1979 and 1983 under Bernd Becher's tutelage, the photographs isolate rooms and furnishings with the same flat, deadpan objectivity Ruff would later bring to his portraits and star charts, capturing what he has called the "epitome of petite bourgeoisie" with neither irony nor sentimentality, even as the images register as a document of his own upbringing.

Ruff, born in 1958, went on to become one of the most influential photographers to emerge from the Becher school, moving between series, Portrats, Sterne, Nachte, Substrate, and jpegs, that each interrogate photography's claim to objectivity; Interieurs, his earliest sustained body of work, already stakes out that territory.
notes: Out of print at time of research. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Lichten
contributors: Philippe Van Cauteren (Text), Robert Fleck (Text), Gregor Jansen (Text), Martin Germann (Text), Valeria Liebermann (Text)
description:
Lichten brings together five bodies of work spanning Thomas Ruff's career, from the late 1970s through 2014, organized around the shift from natural to virtual light in photography over the past three decades.

The book reproduces selections from Interiors (1979-1983), Stars (1989-1992) and Nights (1992-1996), together with work from his more recent Negatives (2014-) and Photograms (2012-2014) series, the latter a digitally generated simulation of the historic darkroom technique. It was published by Roma Publications to accompany simultaneous exhibitions at S.M.A.K. in Ghent and the Kunsthalle Düsseldorf, with texts by Philippe Van Cauteren, Robert Fleck, Gregor Jansen, Martin Germann and Valeria Liebermann.

Ruff, a former student of Bernd and Hilla Becher at the Düsseldorf Academy, has built a body of work defined by systematic series that interrogate photography's claims to objectivity rather than photographing the world directly. Lichten traces that method across three decades, from analog interiors and night skies to his most recent digital experiments.
notes: Published in conjunction with joint 2014 exhibitions at S.M.A.K. Ghent and Kunsthalle Düsseldorf. Design by Roger Willems and Hans Gremmen. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Catalogue Raisonné of the Paintings, Volume One: 1958-1970
description:
Catalogue Raisonné of the Paintings, Volume One: 1958-1970 opens the multi-volume scholarly record of Edward Ruscha's paintings, documenting the years in which his signature vocabulary of words, signs, and Los Angeles vernacular imagery first took shape.

The volume reproduces and catalogues every known painting from the period, accompanied by essays from curator Walter Hopps and art historian Yve-Alain Bois that trace Ruscha's emergence from a Pop-adjacent sensibility toward the deadpan, text-driven language for which he became known. Published jointly by Gagosian Gallery and Steidl, the 464-page hardcover is issued in a slipcase, in keeping with the series' function as a definitive reference rather than a trade monograph.

Ruscha, born in 1937 and based in Los Angeles since the late 1950s, is one of the defining figures of postwar American art, known equally for his paintings, photobooks, and prints built around language, signage, and the built landscape of Southern California. This first volume anchors the ongoing catalogue raisonné project that continues to document his paintings decade by decade.
notes: First of a multi-volume catalogue raisonné series; publisher url and physical dimensions unconfirmed this session. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Los Angeles Apartments
edition_printrun: Also issued through Harry N. Abrams, 1993 (ISBN 9780810968080)
description:
Los Angeles Apartments is the catalogue for a 1990 Whitney Museum of American Art exhibition devoted to Edward Ruscha's 1965 self-published artist book of the same name, organised by curator Richard Marshall.

Ruscha's original 1965 book presented deadpan, frontal photographs of Los Angeles apartment buildings, part of a series of small self-published photobooks — alongside Twentysix Gasoline Stations and Every Building on the Sunset Strip — that treated the vernacular architecture of the city as a found conceptual subject. This 63-page paperback catalogue, shown at the Whitney from July to October 1990, reproduces the project and situates it within Ruscha's early photographic practice.

Ruscha (b. 1937) emerged in the 1960s Los Angeles art scene working across painting, printmaking and photography, and his self-published books are now considered foundational to the artist's book as a form. This catalogue was also issued through Harry N. Abrams in a 1993 edition, extending the exhibition's reach beyond the museum run.
notes: Row title given simply as "Los Angeles Apartments"; several distinct Ruscha-related publications share this title, including his own 1965 self-published book, this 1990 Whitney/Marshall exhibition catalogue, a Getty/Heckert companion volume, and a Steidl/Müller edition. Identified as the Whitney Museum catalogue based on an exact plain-title match on AbeBooks, confirmed via OpenLibrary and Library of Congress data (LCCN 91142387, OCLC 22582068). Also issued through Harry N. Abrams in 1993 under a different ISBN (9780810968080). If the shelf copy is Ruscha's own self-published original or one of the other editions rather than this catalogue, this record should be corrected. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Metro Mattresses
description:
Metro Mattresses collects the paintings Ed Ruscha showed under that title at Sprüth Magers, Berlin, continuing his decades-long interest in language treated as both image and object.

The 28-page hardcover catalogue is bound in linen with a plain paper title label, echoing the deadpan typographic presentation of Ruscha's paintings themselves. It was designed by Swantje Hoffmann and published by Sprüth Magers to document the exhibition, and issued together with a promotional poster.

Ruscha has worked since the 1960s across painting, photography, and artist's books, treating words, phrases, and vernacular Los Angeles imagery as material for repeated formal investigation. Metro Mattresses extends that practice into a further set of paintings built around a found or invented phrase, presented with the same restraint that has defined his word paintings since the 1980s.
notes: Issued with a promotional poster for the exhibition. Exhibition dates not confirmed against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: The Tree Show
description:
The Tree Show collects the paintings from Mark Ryden's 2007 exhibition at Michael Kohn Gallery, Los Angeles, in which the artist absorbs the Roman poet Ovid's tales of transformation from the Metamorphoses and refracts them through his own dense vocabulary of art-historical figuration and contemporary pop culture.

Populated by porcelain-skinned girls, taxidermied creatures, religious iconography and confectionery color, the paintings return again and again to trees and the forest as sites of metamorphosis, drawing equally on Old Master painting technique and the visual language of vintage illustration. An accompanying text by critic Holly Myers situates the work within Ryden's broader mythology. The catalog was published by Porterhouse Fine Art Editions in both trade and limited editions.

Ryden (born 1963), a central figure of the Los Angeles "pop surrealist" or "lowbrow" movement, built his reputation on meticulously rendered, uncanny tableaux that fuse Renaissance-derived technique with children's-book sweetness and occult symbolism; The Tree Show is among his most fully developed single-exhibition bodies of work.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Exhibition Catalog
notes: A separate deluxe/limited edition of the same catalog exists (ISBN 9781931955096); this record is the standard trade hardcover. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Tea Ceremony Manual
publisher: Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum
description:
Tea Ceremony Manual is Tom Sachs's illustrated guide to the ritual he devised for performing the Japanese tea ceremony through his own workshop's materials and codes, plywood, foamcore, hand tools, and handwritten labels standing in for lacquer and ceramic.

Published by the Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum on the occasion of the exhibition Tom Sachs: Tea Ceremony (March 23 - July 24, 2016), the 278-page book follows the format of the niche instructional manuals Sachs collects and imitates, laying out step-by-step host and guest procedures alongside a statement by the artist, an essay and haiku by curator Dakin Hart, a foreword by museum director Jenny Dixon, and a visual index of his tea-related sculpture.

Sachs has spent much of his career restaging systems of ritual and craft, from NASA space programs to McDonald's, using bricolage construction to expose the values embedded in objects and procedures; Tea Ceremony Manual applies that method to a tradition he first encountered as a teenager, translating its codes into his own workshop vocabulary.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Sculpture, Exhibition Catalog
notes: Edition to be verified against the copy; dimensions not confirmed. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Discordia
description:
Discordia takes its title from the Roman goddess of discord and strife, and gathers Moises Saman's photographs made between 2011 and 2014 while he worked as a photojournalist across Tunisia, Egypt, Libya, Iraq, Lebanon and Syria during the Arab Spring.

Rather than the captioned, event-driven images Saman filed for The New York Times, The New Yorker and TIME, the book strips away text and chronology, building long sequences of double-page spreads, isolated images and provocative juxtapositions to convey what he has described as the way the era's overlapping revolutions blurred into a single memory. The volume includes a series of photo collages made by the Dutch-Iranian artist Daria Birang from Saman's negatives, cutting and repeating fragments of gesture and crowd, and closes with short essays by Saman describing individual encounters from his years living in the region. The project was supported by the Incite Project, the Guggenheim Foundation, the W. Eugene Smith Fund and Magnum's Collectors Circle, and was self-published in 2016.

Saman, a Peruvian-Spanish photographer and member of Magnum Photos, has covered conflict and its aftermath across the Middle East, Africa and Asia for two decades. Discordia stands apart from his editorial assignments as a personal, subjective account of the same events, and won the 2016 Anamorphosis Prize for self-published photobooks.
notes: Self-published; no imprint. Pagination and physical dimensions not confirmed this session. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Altered States: The Library of Julio Santo Domingo
description:
Altered States: The Library of Julio Santo Domingo documents one of the largest private archives of countercultural material ever assembled: the collection built over decades by Julio Mario Santo Domingo Jr.

Santo Domingo, heir to a Colombian brewing fortune, spent much of his life gathering rare books, manuscripts, artworks, and ephemera tracing the history of drugs, psychedelia, rock music, and countercultural movements from the nineteenth century to the present. This 479-page volume, photographed by Jason Brownrigg with text by Peter Watts and designed by Yolanda Cuomo, moves through the collection's rooms and holdings, treating the library itself (its shelving, objects, and juxtapositions) as much as the individual items in it. It was published in a single-volume trade edition by Anthology Editions in 2017, following Santo Domingo's death in 2009 and the collection's eventual dispersal.

The book's front board carries only a bookplate reading "Ex Libris / Julio Santo Domingo", the collector's own library mark, rather than the published title, which appears on the dust jacket; catalogue records that cite the cover text alone have listed the book as "Ex Libris" for that reason. Altered States stands as the primary published record of a collection otherwise known mainly through scholarly and curatorial circles.
notes: Catalogued title was 'Ex Libris,' the collector's-bookplate text stamped on the front cloth board; the book's actual published title is Altered States: The Library of Julio Santo Domingo (confirmed by cover inspection and matching the row's own note: 480-page, single-volume trade edition). Author spelling 'Juilo' corrected to 'Julio.' Santo Domingo is the collection's subject, not its writer. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Of Mud and Lotus
description:
Of Mud and Lotus is a photobook by the Dutch photographer Viviane Sassen, published by Artbeat Publishers, Tokyo, in an embroidered hardcover limited to 1,000 copies.

The 108-page book gathers colour photographs that draw on Sassen's recurring interests — the body, shadow, colour and abstraction — worked through in images that move between documentary observation and staged composition. Design is by Shigeo Goto and Yoshihisa Tanaka, with editing by Sawako Fukai, and the embroidered cloth cover is treated as part of the work rather than incidental packaging.

Sassen trained first in fashion design before turning to photography, and her work now moves fluidly between fashion commissions, gallery exhibitions and self-directed long-term projects, often shaped by her childhood years in Kenya. Of Mud and Lotus belongs to the more personal, art-book side of that practice, produced in the small-edition, design-forward format Artbeat Publishers has used across several of its artist titles.
notes: Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Sketches: Polaroids made in Africa, 2002-2010
description:
Sketches gathers Polaroids Viviane Sassen made across Africa between 2002 and 2010, a compact counterpart to the more finished photographs of her earlier book Flamboya.

Where Flamboya presents Sassen's formal, color-saturated studio and location work, Sketches shows the instant-film images she made alongside it, offered here without captions or extended text as a self-contained visual record. Designed by Sybren Kuiper and published by Kominek Books, Berlin, the book was conceived less as documentation of a larger project than as a small object with its own internal logic.

Sassen, trained first as a fashion photographer before turning toward a more personal, abstracted body of work, has repeatedly returned to Africa, where she spent part of her childhood, as a recurring subject and site. Sketches sits alongside Flamboya, Parasomnia, and Umbra in a body of work that treats the continent's light and landscape as material for an increasingly formal, painterly photographic language.
notes: Companion volume to Sassen's Flamboya. No ISBN found for this title; the artist's own site lists only an Amazon identifier (ASIN B006Q355EG), not a true ISBN. Cover to be photographed. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Roxane II
description:
Roxane II continues Viviane Sassen's collaborative portrait of her muse Roxane Danset, extending a visual dialogue between photographer and subject that treats the body as a site of shadow, gesture, and mark-making rather than straightforward likeness.

The book gathers a sequence of images made following the pair's first collaboration, Roxane, using dynamic poses, cast shadows, and the imprint of skin against paper to blur the line between performer and performance. An introductory text by the Dutch artist and writer Maria Barnas, who also collaborated with Sassen on Umbra, frames the work as a shared self-portrait in which two identities become difficult to separate. Oodee published the book as a cloth hardcover.

Sassen, a Dutch photographer who trained as a fashion designer before turning to photography, works across fashion, fine art, and documentary registers, often returning to the human body as abstracted color and form; her other books include Roxane, Umbra, and Pikin Slee.
notes: Second collaboration with muse Roxane Danset, following Roxane (2012). Contributor name appears misspelled as "Maria Bernas" on some booksellers' listings; corrected here to Maria Barnas, the writer's published spelling. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Crime and Punishment
editor: Edited by Massimiliano Gioni and Gary Carrion-Murayari

title: Landscapes
description:
Landscapes is Lele Saveri's photobook of nude and botanical studies pushed through months of Risograph experimentation, treating the printing process itself as much a subject as the bodies and plants it depicts.

Saveri and designer Brian Lamotte spent months running the same photographs through a Risograph press, layering ink passes until the images broke down into grain, color shift and overprint. Rather than bind the unstable Risograph sheets directly, the pair scanned the results and reproduced them by offset, so the finished book carries the texture of the Riso experiments at the scale of a 120-page paperback. Dashwood Books published the softbound edition in 2015 on Finch Vellum paper, in a run of 500 copies, alongside a ten-copy box set that enclosed a set of the original Risograph prints.

Saveri, who moved from Rome to New York, is as well known for the platforms he built around other people's books as for his own: The 8-Ball Fair, the artist-run book fair he started in a Chinatown pool hall in 2012, and The Newsstand, a decommissioned MTA newsstand he leased as an exhibition space. Landscapes carries the same interest in printed matter as a physical, degradable medium that runs through those projects.
notes: Catalogued copy noted as "(original Risograph print)"; Dashwood's ten-copy special edition paired the offset-printed book with a set of the original Risograph prints used to make it. No ISBN was ever assigned to this self/small-press edition. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Peter Saville: Estate 1-127
contributors: Michael Bracewell (Essay), Wolfgang Tillmans (Contributor), Sarah Morris (Contributor), Sean Snyder (Contributor), Robert Longo (Contributor), Kelley Walker (Contributor)
description:
This monograph surveys the visual career of Peter Saville, the designer whose sleeve work for Factory Records reshaped the look of British record design from the late 1970s onward.

The book gathers 240 color images spanning Saville's early record covers through his later gallery-based projects, and pairs them with essays and personal responses from artists including Wolfgang Tillmans, Robert Longo, Sarah Morris and Sean Snyder. It was published to accompany a presentation with the Migros Museum für Gegenwartskunst, Zurich, and was named one of the Most Beautiful Swiss Books of 2007.

The volume situates Saville's commercial design work alongside contemporary art practice, tracking how his image-making for music and fashion has been read by artists working in other mediums.
tags: Art, Graphic Design, Contemporary Art, Exhibition Catalog
notes: Published by JRP|Editions (formerly JRP|Ringier) with the Migros Museum fur Gegenwartskunst, Zurich; named one of the Most Beautiful Swiss Books of 2007. The trade title carries the artist’s name; the catalogue record already had it. Cover image is the publisher's own product photograph. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Designed by Peter Saville
description:
Peter Saville's record sleeves for Factory Records recast graphic design as a form of authorship in its own right, and this monograph is the first sustained account of a career that reshaped how music, fashion and corporate identity look.

Edited by Emily King with an essay by Peter York, the book moves chronologically from Saville's earliest work for Factory — including the cover of Joy Division's Unknown Pleasures and New Order's ongoing sleeve designs — through his later work in fashion, advertising and civic branding, among it Manchester's own identity campaign. Reproductions of posters, sleeves and ephemera are set against interview transcripts and critical texts that track his shifting relationship to originality, appropriation and commercial constraint.

Saville remains one of the most influential graphic designers of his generation, and the book situates his practice within the wider history of British design culture, from the post-punk moment that made his reputation to the branding consultancies that later employed it.
notes: Bibliographic identity confirmed via AbeBooks and OpenLibrary; no publisher page reachable for this out-of-print 2003 title. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Passengers
description:
John Schabel's Passengers collects black-and-white photographs of airline travelers photographed unaware through the windows of departing planes, each face caught alone with itself in the last moments before takeoff.

Working with a long telephoto lens from the tarmac in the early 1990s, Schabel photographed passengers through the scratched, rain-streaked oval windows of parked aircraft, compressing distance until the glass itself becomes part of the image. The resulting portraits are soft, granular and voyeuristic: strangers caught mid-thought, unaware of the camera, their expressions ranging from boredom to apprehension. Sequenced without captions or names, the book reads as a single sustained meditation on air travel as a modern rite of passage, stripped of glamour and reduced to the isolation of the individual seat.

Schabel is an American photographer whose work has long focused on surveillance, distance and the unguarded moment. Passengers remains his best-known body of work, exhibited internationally and cited as an influence on subsequent photographers working with telephoto observation and the ethics of the candid portrait.
tags: Photography, Portraiture, Surveillance Index, Surveillance Index Edition One
notes: Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Tell Me When You Re Ready - Works From 1990-1995
Waffenruhe
description:
Waffenruhe (Ceasefire) is Michael Schmidt's stark portrait of a divided Berlin on the eve of reunification, and one of the most influential photobooks of the twentieth century.

First published in 1987 by the Berlin house Dirk Nishen Verlag, the book pairs Schmidt's high-contrast black-and-white photographs of the city's checkpoints, borderlands and anonymous residents with a text by the writer and theatre director Einar Schleef. Rather than document Berlin directly, Schmidt works through unexpected juxtaposition and abrupt sequencing to evoke a generation's sense of rupture and dystopia in the shadow of the Wall. The original edition sold out quickly and became difficult to find; this edition, published by Koenig Books in 2018, returns the book to print for the first time in three decades.

Schmidt (1945-2014) was a self-taught Berlin photographer whose books, including U-NI-TY, Berlin nach 45 and Lebensmittel, are central to postwar German photography. His work was the subject of solo exhibitions at the Museum of Modern Art, New York, and Haus der Kunst, Munich, and Waffenruhe remains the touchstone of his sustained engagement with Berlin's fractured identity.
notes: Catalogued title carried the parenthetical translation Waffenruhe (Ceasefire); Ceasefire is the accepted English translation of the title, not a separate edition title. This is the 2018 Koenig Books reprint of the 1987 Dirk Nishen Verlag first edition. Page count and dimensions could not be confirmed this session. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Private Views: A High-Rise Panorama of Manhattan
contributors: Essays: Sara Emilia Bernat, f-architecture, Irena Lehkoživová, Ava Lynam, Peter Noever, Jack Self, Michael Sorkin, Samuel Stein, Barbora Špičáková, Anthony Vidler, Sharon Zukin.
description:
All of us want to see Manhattan from above, but very few can do it from their own living room.

Private Views is here to satisfy our incessant curiosity about a hidden elite world that we can only observe from outside, or occasionally, from an overpriced viewing point crowded with tourists. While posing as an apartment-hunting Hungarian billionaire, Andi Schmied accessed and documented Manhattan's most exclusive high-rise properties. For the duration of the project, she inhabited a fictional persona: Gabriella, a mother of one whose husband is an antique dealer.

Dressing as Gabriella and acting as Gabriella, she prepared for the family's upcoming move to Manhattan. Complemented by essays, and fragments of the real estate conversations, the book guides its readers through the sunset from the Trump Tower and dawn over Central Park from the private ballroom of the tallest residential tower on the planet, showcasing samples of the world's most luxurious materials, such as the Calacatta Tucci marble used in bathrooms overlooking the Empire State Building.
tags: Art, New York City, Surveillance, Surveillance Index

title: Maneater
description:
Maneater collects five years of Aurel Schmidt's obsessively worked colored-pencil and graphite drawings, in which discarded fast food, cigarette butts, insects, and tangled vegetation accumulate into dense, corrosive images of the body under pressure.

The book brings together drawings shown across Schmidt's solo exhibitions at Deitch Projects in New York and Peres Projects in Los Angeles, alongside work exhibited at the DESTE Foundation in Athens, including the cigarette-burned faces of her Burnouts series. Text by curator Kathy Grayson accompanies the plates in this 160-page softcover.

Schmidt, born in Kelowna, Canada, in 1982, works in a self-taught, densely layered style that reworks the vanitas tradition through a punk and pop sensibility, rendering rot and decay with the patience usually reserved for still-life painting; Maneater remains her fullest survey in book form.
notes: Catalogued as "Schmit"; corrected to Aurel Schmidt, the artist's published spelling. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Beautiful Pig
description:
Beautiful Pig is Ben Schonberger's photobook study of American police culture, built from studio portraits, found ephemera and archival material rather than reportage from the street.

The book interleaves posed portraits, including an officer photographed wearing a tallit over his uniform and group portraits from a police academy class, with a grid of found Polaroid booking photographs annotated by hand with case notes, and objects pulled from an officer's personal archive: a cassette tape with its reels torn out, sticky notes recording what was on it, snapshots from awards dinners. Softcover and perfect bound, running past 200 pages at 8.25 x 10.75 inches, the book carries a foreword by Chad Alligood. Schonberger self-published a first edition, since out of print, followed by a second printing in 2014.

Schonberger's other project titles, including Detroit Shoreway and Hammer, share this working method: found archival material, ephemera and staged portraiture combined to examine an institution or place from within.
notes: Self-published; no ISBN was assigned. Second printing, 2014 (both the first edition and the second printing are out of print). Page count given as 200+ pages by the artist; exact count to be verified against the copy. Cover to be photographed. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Contacts
description:
this bookzine is based on Schorr's seminal book 'Jens F', published by Steidl/MACK.

The work is a study of Andrew Wyeth's series of paitings of a girl named Helga. Schorr began to photograph a young boy in many of the positions that Wyeth painted Helga to give someone another identity and photograph them through the transformation. During the process, Wyeth's book 'The Helga Pictures' became a sketchbook, filled with contact prints, annotations and so where the viewer sees only the finished and perfected photograph. 'Contacts' shows a deeper view into this process

title: 8 Women
description:
8 Women presents work which spans from the mid-nineties to the present.

Schorr's earliest works utilised appropriated adverts from fashion magazines to address issues of authorship and desire the works introduced a female gaze into the debate about female representation. Appropriation was Schorr's first medium and in some sense she returns to it, taking her own commissioned fashion images and folding them into a dialogue with other works. The works in 8 Women propose a variety of subjects, all of whom are involved in performance, be it as artists, models or musicians.

Schorr, who has been working in fashion for the last 10 years, created sets that doubled as her studio, teasing out images that could only be made with a subject that could travel between the object of desire and the enforcer of an identity crafted in that very moment. Working between out-takes and manipulations of tear sheets, Schorr questions who the women that desire to be looked at are, as well as what power exists in acknowledging that as a post-feminist position.
tags: Contemporary Art, Fashion Photography, Gender Studies, Photography, Fashion, Performance Art, Female Gaze

title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
Ernst Schwitters in Norway: Photographs 1930-1960 (Multilingual Edition)
Things Left Unsaid
description:
Paul Seawright turns his camera on the interiors of American and European television news studios, the spaces where footage of distant wars is edited into broadcast narrative.

The photographs record the sets, lighting rigs and control desks behind the news anchor's frame, drawing on Paul Virilio's writing on electronic warfare to examine how conflict is mediated and made presentable for a viewing public. The work was shown as Making News: Things Left Unsaid at the Centre Culturel Irlandais, Paris, in 2014, before traveling to The Model, Sligo, and the Ulster Museum in 2015, with an exhibition catalogue produced for the tour.

The project continues Seawright's long-running interest in the landscapes and infrastructure of conflict, following earlier bodies of work made in Belfast and Afghanistan that likewise withhold the image of violence itself in favor of its surrounding architecture.
notes: Published by Artist Photo Books, Dublin, in November 2014 in conjunction with the touring exhibition Making News: Things Left Unsaid, shown at the Centre Culturel Irlandais (Paris), The Model (Sligo) and the Ulster Museum. Text by Nicholas Allen. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Dark Room A–Z
description: Reflects on the methodologies, strategies, and points of interest behind a single, expansive body of work at a pivotal moment in his career.

title: Khichdi (Kitchari)
description:
Khichdi (Kitchari) is Nick Sethi's first major artist book, a decade-long project photographing India as both an outsider and a native son, and it announced him as one of the more idiosyncratic voices in contemporary documentary photography.

Named for the rice-and-lentil dish eaten across India regardless of region or household, the book gathers portraits, still lifes and street pictures made over ten years of travel through the country. Sethi, an American-born photographer of Indian heritage who did not visit India until age seventeen, used the camera to build connection with people and place; his images stay conscious of photography as a shared experience, folding his own presence and interests into scenes built around gender, technology, and the pull between inherited tradition and encroaching Western culture. The sequencing resists a single fixed viewpoint, echoing the dish's own lack of one official recipe.

Published by Dashwood Books and printed in New Delhi under Sethi's own direction, the book established his reputation beyond editorial work for magazines including Vice, and positioned him within a generation of photographers using personal, first-hand access to complicate inherited outsider images of South Asia.
notes: Publisher confirmed as Dashwood Books via a retailer's product record (vendor field); Dashwood's own site blocks automated requests, so no direct book page was reachable. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Pul Ke Niche
description:
Nick Sethi's Pul Ke Niche is a saturated, flash-driven photographic diary of the artist's travels through India, its title translating roughly as "under the bridge."

Shot on point-and-shoot cameras with hard on-camera flash, the book moves without hierarchy between street scenes, festival crowds, roadside stalls, animals and interiors, building a dense, saturated portrait of everyday life rather than a travelogue of monuments. Sethi's approach favors proximity and immersion over distance: subjects look directly into the lens, colors run hot and unfiltered, and the sequencing has the loose, accumulative rhythm of a diary rather than a planned essay. The book was produced through Dashwood Books, the New York photobook shop and publisher closely associated with Sethi's early work.

Sethi is an American photographer known for an immersive, high-contact documentary style developed largely in India. Pul Ke Niche preceded his later book Khichdi (Kitchari), also held in this collection, and the two form a sustained body of work returning to the same terrain over successive trips.
notes: No ISBN could be located for this self-published/small-run Dashwood title; Dashwood Books' own site 429s automated requests, so its listing could not be checked directly. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: No Time for Love
description:
A self-published zine in which the actress Chloe Sevigny turns a personal photo archive into a public one, pairing snapshots of past relationships with tabloid gossip clippings about herself.

No Time for Love collects photographs Sevigny took of the men she loved, in her words, "from my father to my first true love to my biggest crush," from photobooth strips to candid snapshots, alongside clippings from the New York Post's Page Six documenting her own public life. The men's faces are obscured with stickers, a gesture that turns romantic memoir into redaction. Published in Geneva by Innen in an edition of 1,000, the zine was released to coincide with the I Never Read art book fair in Basel in June 2015 and sold out shortly after.

Sevigny, an actress and longtime fixture of downtown New York's art and fashion scenes, has moved between film, fashion collaborations and self-published projects across her career. No Time for Love sits alongside that work as a diaristic, confessional object rather than a professional photography book, closer in spirit to a scrapbook than a monograph.
notes: Self-published zine, edition of 1,000, no ISBN assigned. Faces of the men pictured are obscured with stickers throughout. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: The People on the Street
description:
The People on the Street reverses Nigel Shafran's usual position behind the camera: between 2016 and 2017 he approached people sleeping rough in London and Paris and asked each of them to take his photograph.

The resulting pictures are presented unedited and in chronological order, each captioned only with the photographer's name and the location where it was taken. Shot against a homelessness crisis that saw the number of people sleeping rough in London double after 2010, the sequence repeatedly juxtaposes visible poverty with the commercial wealth of the surrounding streets. Shafran self-published the softcover book and directed all proceeds from its sale to homelessness charities.

Shafran has spent three decades photographing the overlooked textures of daily life, from still lifes of domestic clutter to the changing rooms of English department stores; here he turns that same patient, undramatic attention on himself, asking what changes when the photographer hands over control of the image.
notes: Self-published by Shafran; proceeds from sale went to homelessness charities. No ISBN found for this self-published edition. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Before and After Night Porter
description:
Before and After Night Porter gathers the black-and-white work of British photographer Chris Shaw (b. 1967), photographs shot in close-up, at unexpected angles and in high contrast, with a formal kinship to the Japanese Vivo and Provoke collectives of the 1960s.

The book brings together a selection of photographs from three of Shaw's projects: Life as a Night Porter (1995-2005), Sandy Hill Estate (1986-1989) and Weeds of Wallasey (2006-2011). Working in black and white when many of his contemporaries had turned to color, Shaw translated the blurred, disorienting language of Japanese photobooks such as Daido Moriyama's Farewell Photography and Yutaka Takanashi's Towards the City into a distinctly British context. Hardcover with dust jacket, 144 pages with 109 duotone illustrations, edited by Simon Baker and Inès de Bordas with an essay by Baker, published by Kehrer Verlag with the support of the Wilson Centre for Photography.

Shaw's photographs are held in major private and public collections, and this volume revisits and extends the body of work he began as a night porter at a Sunderland hotel in the 1990s, placing it alongside his earlier and later projects.
notes: Edited by Simon Baker and Inès de Bordas, with an essay by Baker; published with the support of the Wilson Centre for Photography. Kehrer Verlag's own product page dates the book to 2012; OpenLibrary lists 2013 and 160 pages against the publisher's 144 - the publisher's own listing is used here. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: 43-35 10th Street
editor: Daniel Shea, Walter Benn Michaels, Winfried Heininger
description:
43-35 10th Street is a book about architecture and its relationship to ideological and socioeconomic shifts.

The work began with a simple premise for Shea to observe the residential real estate boom in his neighborhood of New York City, Long Island City. This type of development boom, happening in cities globally, is a distinctly late capitalist solution to the perception of housing needs. Images of Long Island City in New York are juxtaposed with the government buildings in the famed Brazilian city of Brasilia, built ex-nihilo 50 years ago. Images of a dying California industrial town suggest a cycle of dissolution, real estate value, and entropy.
tags: Architectural photography, Artistic, Brasília (Distrito Federal, Brazil) -- Pictorial works, City planning -- Pictorial works, Documentary photography, Gentrification, Human ecology -- Pictorial works, Long Island City (New York, N.Y.) -- Pictorial works, Photography, Searles Valley (Calif.) -- Pictorial works

title: Blisner, IL: An Index of Work as Labour as Work
description:
Daniel Shea's Blisner, IL maps the aftermath of industrial collapse across southern Illinois, using a fictional composite town, Blisner, as a frame for photographs of real post-industrial landscapes and the people who remain in them.

The book is structured as an index, pairing photographs with text in a format the artist has described as both a new edition and a pseudo-sequel to an earlier, self-published version of the project. It was published as a 192-page hardcover by Fourteen-Nineteen, London, in 2014, with an accompanying essay by Walter Benn Michaels. A limited special edition, distributed through Loose Joints, later reissued the project once the first edition had gone out of print.

The project extends Shea's ongoing documentary interest in American industrial decline and the labor economies left behind by it, following his earlier photographic work on coal and steel regions of the Midwest.
notes: First edition published by Fourteen-Nineteen, London, 2014, with an essay by Walter Benn Michaels; described by the publisher as a new edition and pseudo-sequel to an earlier self-published Blisner, Ill. Once out of print, Loose Joints issued a separate limited special edition of the same title. This record reflects the standard 2014 hardcover. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Steven Shearer
publisher: Ikon Gallery / The Power Plant Contemporary Art Gallery
contributors: Nigel Prince (Essay), Helena Reckitt (Essay), Nancy Tousley (Essay)
description:
Steven Shearer is the catalogue for the Vancouver artist's first major touring survey, and it remains a key document of a practice built from the discarded imagery of adolescence and internet subculture.

Organized by the Contemporary Art Gallery, Vancouver, where the exhibition opened in 2004 before touring to Ikon Gallery, Birmingham and The Power Plant, Toronto, the show brought together Shearer's photorealistic graphite drawings and paintings alongside his large accumulations of found photographs: long-haired metal fans, skateboarders, and other vernacular self-portraits scavenged from the internet and print ephemera. This edition of the catalogue was published to accompany the Ikon Gallery and Power Plant venues, with essays by Nigel Prince, Helena Reckitt and Nancy Tousley that place Shearer's fascination with teenage male identity, boredom and heavy metal culture within a longer history of appropriation art.

Shearer represented Canada at the 2011 Venice Biennale, and this early survey catalogue documents the vocabulary (collected photographs, hand-lettered poetry, and meticulous drawing) that carried through the rest of his career.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Drawing, Exhibition Catalog
notes: This self-titled catalogue is distinct from the artist's later publication Steven Shearer: Exhume to Consume (National Gallery of Canada, 2011); do not conflate the two. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

description:
A compilation bringing together reprints of 28 out-of-print artist's notepads originally published by Sheshivari in his own publishing house, Boabooks, between 2008 and 2011.

These original notepads featured contributions (images and text) from various contemporary artists, including Olivier Mosset, Isabelle Cornaro, and Jérémie Gindre, among others. The book is primarily an art publication and a documentation of Sheshivari's curatorial and publishing work with Boabooks, allowing readers to view the development of the series as a whole.

title: Blind Date
edition_printrun: La Fábrica edition of the 2017 T&M Projects self-published original
description:
Lieko Shiga's Blind Date is a staged, dreamlike photographic series built around couples encountered and photographed in Bangkok, their bodies and motorcycles caught in theatrical arrangements of artificial light and motion.

Working outside her native Japan, Shiga approached her subjects as collaborators in constructed tableaux rather than documentary sitters, using flash, blur and staged gesture to push ordinary scenes of intimacy and transit toward something closer to fiction or ritual. The resulting images resist a single reading of place or narrative, instead building an atmosphere of charged, unresolved encounter that recurs across the sequence. First self-published in 2017 by T&M Projects, the book was reissued by the Madrid house La Fábrica, which carries the ISBN cited here; the two editions share the same body of work.

Shiga is a Japanese photographer known for a highly staged, performative approach that blurs documentary and fiction, developed most fully in her long-term project photographing the Tohoku coastal community of Kitakama before and after the 2011 tsunami. Blind Date shows the same theatrical instinct for light and gesture applied to a different, foreign context.
notes: This edition (La Fábrica, ISBN 9788410024496) reissues Shiga's 2017 self-published original from T&M Projects; edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Olele Olala
description:
Olele Olala is Kishin Shinoyama's document of Carnival in Rio de Janeiro, made on assignment for the Japanese edition of Playboy when the photographer was thirty years old.

Issued as a Playboy Special Edition by Shueisha in 1971, the book runs largely in color, its images sequenced by the writer Shōzō Tsurumoto into a photographic travelogue with a line of text accompanying nearly every picture, capturing the crowds, costumes, and staged theatricality of the Carnival street parades.

Shinoyama, one of postwar Japan's most prolific commercial and fine-art photographers, moved fluidly between fashion, celebrity portraiture, and reportage across a six-decade career; the Rio material was later restaged on film by director Nobuhiko Obayashi, who rephotographed Shinoyama's Carnival pictures on 16mm.
notes: Published in 1971 as a Playboy Special Edition; no ISBN exists for this pre-ISBN-era edition. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: I Wish I Never Saw the Sunshine.
description:
American conceptual artist Pacifico Silano’s practice is rooted in excavating the printed ephemera of gay culture to create new images that comment on loss, longing and queer melancholy.

In particular, Silano uses the gestures of framing, cropping and layering vintage gay erotica to comment on the HIV/AIDS crisis and its reverberations on queer lives, which included the loss of the artist's uncle at the height of the epidemic.

I Wish I Never Saw the Sunshine is Silano’s first artist’s book, and engages with an ambitious accordion-folded format that references Silano’s photo-based installations: two twenty-panel long sequences that can be read as both one continuous collage and a sequence of individual images. Included in the book is an interview with the artist by José Diaz, Chief Curator of The Andy Warhol Museum.

title: Tear Sheets
publisher: Silent Face Projects with Dashwood Books
description:
Tear Sheets takes its title from the torn and clipped magazine pages that are Pacifico Silano's raw material: found images from vintage gay pornographic and physique magazines, rephotographed, cropped and recomposed into new tableaux.

Working from an archive of found print media, Silano isolates gestures, colors and fragments of bodies from their original context, turning advertising and pornographic photography into images about desire, nostalgia and loss in gay culture, with the shadow of the AIDS crisis running beneath the surface of the source material. The book accompanies an exhibition of the same body of work and includes a text by curator and writer Marvin Heiferman. It was co-published by Silent Face Projects, the Brooklyn imprint, and Dashwood Books in 2016.

Silano, born in 1986, continues this method of appropriation and recomposition in later books such as I Wish I Never Saw the Sunshine and Shadow Cast, both published by Loose Joints, extending the same interrogation of vintage print media into new bodies of work.
notes: Co-published by Silent Face Projects (Brooklyn) and Dashwood Books; text by Marvin Heiferman. Published alongside an exhibition of the same work. OpenLibrary records the book as unpaginated; page count and dimensions to be verified against the copy. Cover to be photographed. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: A Summer
description: 99 flowers, a guide, a calendar, an index, and a conversation.

title: Libya: Inch by Inch, House by House, Alley by Alley
description:
Giovanna Silva's Inch by Inch, House by House, Alley by Alley photographs Libya in the years after the 2011 uprising and civil war, its title borrowed from the language of urban siege warfare.

The book belongs to a series of publications conceived by Silva and published by Mousse under the heading Narratives, each volume built around photographs of a country at war or in crisis. Silva, an architect as well as a photographer, brings an interest in the built environment to the work, tracking how conflict is written into streets, houses and city blocks rather than staged as spectacle.

The book sits within Silva's broader practice of photographing cities under political and architectural pressure, work that has appeared in Domus and San Rocco alongside her independent publications.
notes: Full title on the cover is Libya: Inch by Inch, House by House, Alley by Alley, part of Mousse Publishing's Narratives series on nations at war or in crisis. Format, page count and dimensions were not available from the sources checked. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: The Love Doll: Days 1-36
publisher: Baldwin Gallery / Salon 94 / Tomio Koyama Gallery / Wilkinson Gallery
description:
The Love Doll: Days 1-36 follows Laurie Simmons as she photographs a life-size Japanese love doll through the invented rhythm of an ordinary life, extending a body of work that has staged artificial figures as stand-ins for women since the late 1970s.

Simmons acquired the doll and photographed it over an extended period, dressing and posing it in domestic interiors — bathing, dressing, reading, waiting — so that a single character accumulates a fictional biography across the sequence of images. The pictures return to concerns present throughout Simmons' career: the uncanny space between the animate and the inanimate, and the way domestic femininity is staged, performed and manufactured. The book, edited by Lynne Tillman, was published as the catalogue for a run of gallery exhibitions in New York, London and Tokyo between 2011 and 2013.

The project extends Simmons' work from her 1970s ventriloquist-dummy and dollhouse photographs through her earlier series with Japanese love dolls, and anticipates her continued exploration of surrogate figures standing in for the female body.
notes: Self-published by the participating galleries and distributed by D.A.P.; exact first-printing year inferred from the accompanying exhibition run (2011-2013) rather than a dated colophon. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

editor: by Collier Schorr and Laurie Simmons

title: Paperwork And The Will Of Capital
The Color of a Flea’s Eye: The Picture Collection
description:
A tremendous feat of bookmaking, Taryn Simon's The Color of a Flea's Eye deploys prints, postcards and other ephemera to explore the organization of visual information through the New York Public Library's beloved archive Taryn Simon's The Color of a Flea's Eye presents a history of the New York Public Library's Picture Collection--a legendary trove of more than one million prints, photographs, postcards, posters and images from disused books and periodicals.

Since its inception in 1915, the Picture Collection has been a vital resource for writers, historians, artists, filmmakers, fashion designers and advertising age
