title: An American Index of the Hidden and Unfamiliar
Rear Views, a Star-forming Nebula, and the Office of Foreign Propaganda
Birds of the West Indies
description:
Taryn Simon's Birds of the West Indies traces the accidental origin of the name James Bond. Not the fictional spy, but the real ornithologist whose 1936 field guide of the same title Ian Fleming borrowed for his own creation.

Simon builds the book around three parallel sequences. One is portraits of the actresses who played "Bond girls" across the film franchise. Another catalogues code names the U.S. government has assigned to weapons systems and covert operations, many of them, coincidentally or not, also bird names. The third reproduces the original bird plates from the ornithologist James Bond's field guide. Read together, the sequences trace how a naming system meant to catalogue Caribbean bird species migrated into espionage fiction, then into the actual vocabulary of American military and intelligence programs. Hatje Cantz published the 440-page clothbound volume in 2013, with a contribution from curator Daniel Baumann. The project began as a companion video work shown at the Venice Biennale that year.

Simon was born in New York in 1975. She works across photography, text, and archival research to expose the systems, official and hidden, that structure how the state names, classifies, and remembers. Her other projects include An American Index of the Hidden and Unfamiliar and A Living Man Declared Dead and Other Chapters I-XVIII. Birds of the West Indies extends that method to the language of naming itself.

title: Collages
description:
A dedicated volume of Lorna Simpson's collages, gathering the works on paper in which the American conceptual artist cuts her source material from the pages of vintage Ebony and Jet magazines, crowning found portraits of Black women and men with ink-washed and watercolor forms.

Published by Chronicle Books in 2018 with an introduction by the poet and scholar Elizabeth Alexander, the book presents the collages plate by plate. Hair is the recurring site of invention: advertising heads from mid-century print culture sprout galaxies, geological strata, and abstracted coiffures, turning the archive of American image-making back on itself.

Simpson (b. 1960, Brooklyn) came to prominence in the 1980s with photo-text works interrogating race, gender, and representation the collages extend that inquiry into found material with the economy of gesture that defines her practice across photography, film, and painting.
tags: Collage, Photography, Found Photography, African American Art

title: VISTA
description:
Colin Snapp's VISTA is a photographic study of the American scenic overlook, the roadside platform built and framed for tourists to take in a view.

Rather than photographing landscape directly, Snapp turns his camera on the apparatus of looking itself: guardrails, viewing platforms, hands holding cameras and phones, and the vistas beyond them, already composed and captioned for consumption before the visitor arrives. The book, published as No. 5 in the Etudes Books series by Editions Bessard, is bound in cloth with the title, artist and ISBN printed directly on the cover rather than a dust jacket, in keeping with the series' spare, essayistic format. Sequenced without extended text, it builds a quiet argument about the American landscape as something mediated and pre-framed long before it is photographed.

Snapp is an American artist working across photography, film and sculpture whose work frequently returns to landscape, tourism and the built structures that shape how nature is seen. VISTA sits alongside his other photographic projects as a compact study within that larger, sustained interest in mediated land.
notes: Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: With And Without You
description:
A tribute to Jacob Aue Sobol's father, who died when the photographer was twenty and never saw the two decades of work that followed.

With And Without You brings together 129 images spanning Sobol's career: highlights from published projects including Sabine, Arrivals and Departures, By the River of Kings and I, Tokyo, set alongside pictures from the then-unpublished bodies of work Home, Road of Bones and America. The 224-page hardcover, published by Super Labo with text in English and Danish, functions less as a chronological survey than as a private reckoning conducted in public, gathering the images his father never got to see into a single volume.

Sobol, a Danish photographer and Magnum member, has built his career on close, physically immersive relationships with the people and places he photographs, from a Greenlandic fishing village in Sabine to Tokyo, Bangkok and rural Russia in later projects. With And Without You reframes that body of work around the personal loss that runs beneath it.
notes: This is the 2022 second edition, published by Super Labo; first-edition year could not be independently confirmed this session. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Let's Panic No. 3
contributors: Davide Sorrenti (Photographer), Jim Goldberg (Photographer), Larry Clark (Photographer), William Strobeck (Photographer), Drew Jarrett (Photographer)
description:
Let's Panic No. 3 is the third issue of the New York art-and-fashion biannual Let's Panic, built around an extensive portfolio of pictures by the photographer Davide Sorrenti.

Alongside Sorrenti's pictures, the issue carries Larry Clark's portraits of River Phoenix, Chloe Sevigny photographed by William Strobeck, and Drew Jarrett's pictures of Guinevere Van Seenus, within a large-format, saddle-stitched object built around a rotating roster of photographers, stylists, and writers rather than a single masthead voice.

Let's Panic drew on a loose community of New York and Los Angeles photographers, stylists, and artists working across fashion and fine art, among them Jim Goldberg, Mark Borthwick, and Yelena Yemchuk; this issue's Sorrenti portfolio has since become a reference point for later exhibitions of his archive.
notes: Catalogued author field merged two names, "Davide Sorrenti" and "Goldberg, Jim"; reassigned to NA VA since this is a various-contributors magazine issue, not a single-artist work. Sorrenti and Goldberg are two of roughly thirty contributors to this issue, alongside Larry Clark, William Strobeck, and Mark Borthwick; neither is the sole author or editor. Cover confirms this is Issue 03. Publication year and ISBN could not be confirmed; a trade ISBN appears attached to "Issue 03" in one bookseller listing but was not independently verified against this item, so it is omitted here. The issue number is taken from the two photographers named in the catalogue record, both of whom appear in No. 3, and from the cover; verify against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: A Pound of Pictures
binding: Embossed linen hardcover with front and back tip-in
edition_printrun: Three different papers, including a marbled Japanese stock and five randomised replica vernacular photographs
description:
A Pound of Pictures is a stream-of-consciousness celebration of the photographic medium, bringing together an entirely new collection of work by Alec Soth made between 2018 and 2021.

Depicting a sprawling array of subjects — from Buddhist statues and birdwatchers to sun-seekers and busts of Abe Lincoln — this book reflects on the photographic desire to pin down and crystallise experience, especially as it is represented and recollected by printed images.

Throughout this eclectic sequence are the recurring presences of iconography, of souvenirs and mementos, and of the image-makers that surround us day to day. Forming a winding, ruminative road trip, Soth's photographs are followed by his own notes and reflections in an extended afterword. Each book contains five randomised replica vernacular photographs loosely inserted within the pages.
tags: Contemporary Photography, Photography, American Photography, Documentary Photography, Road Trip

title: Gathered Leaves
binding: Boxed set (clamshell box, postcards, and miniature facsimile books)
description:
Gathered Leaves is not a single book but a mid-career retrospective in a box. MACK issued it as a set of postcards and miniature facsimiles, a way to hold and reshuffle Alec Soth's first four major bodies of work.

MACK published it in 2015 to accompany a touring exhibition curated by Kate Bush. The set surveys everything Soth had published since 2004: Sleeping by the Mississippi, Niagara, Broken Manual, and Songbook. Its title echoes Walt Whitman's Leaves of Grass; each project is treated as a leaf gathered from a longer, ongoing document of America. The box itself is embossed cardboard, in a clamshell form. Inside are twenty-nine large-format postcards reproducing images from across the four bodies of work, each with an essay by the writer and photographer Aaron Schuman printed on its reverse, alongside an introductory card by Bush. Four miniature facsimile books, one per project, sit alongside the postcards. A reader can move through each full sequence in miniature.

Soth was born in Minneapolis in 1969. He is a member of Magnum Photos and founder of the imprint Little Brown Mushroom. Gathered Leaves sits at the hinge of his career: a look back at the work that made his name, before he continued the line with Songbook and, later, A Pound of Pictures.
tags: Photography, Documentary Photography, American Photography, Retrospective
notes: Boxed set, 22.8 x 22.3 cm (box); no page count as it is not a paginated codex — 29 postcards plus 4 miniature facsimile books, one per body of work.

title: Songbook
description:
Songbook turns Alec Soth's eye from the solitary Americans of Sleeping by the Mississippi toward community life: meetings, dances, festivals and communal gatherings across the country, stripped of their news context and read instead as a search for connection.

From 2012 to 2014, Soth traveled state by state working as a community newspaper reporter, publishing his own self-produced paper, The LBM Dispatch, alongside assignments for the New York Times and others. From upstate New York to Silicon Valley he attended hundreds of local gatherings, and Songbook collects the resulting photographs as a fragmentary, often funny and often sad portrait of the tension between American individualism and the desire to belong. MACK published the 144-page hardcover in 2014.

Soth, born in Minneapolis in 1969, is a member of Magnum Photos and the founder of the publishing imprint Little Brown Mushroom. Songbook followed Sleeping by the Mississippi and Broken Manual as part of a body of work that returns repeatedly to the American road and the people who live along it.
notes: First edition; MACK has issued multiple printings since. AbeBooks and MACK's own listings date the first edition to 2014; OpenLibrary lists 2015. Page dimensions not confirmed against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Temporary Discomfort: Chapter I-V
description:
Jules Spinatsch's Temporary Discomfort documents the security apparatus mounted around five economic summits, working across landscape photography, photojournalism and surveillance imagery.

The book collects five chapters made in Davos, Genoa, New York, Evian and Geneva during World Economic Forum and G8 meetings under emergency lockdown, with the camera trained on the police and military presence rather than the protests or proceedings themselves. An essay by Martin Jaeggi situates the work within the conditions of contemporary documentary photography. The book was awarded the German Photobook Prize in the photo-book category on publication.

The project is characteristic of Spinatsch's broader practice of photographing systems of surveillance and control, using the summit lockdowns to examine how public space is reorganized around the threat of disorder.
tags: Photography, Documentary Photography, Surveillance, Photojournalism, Surveillance Index, Surveillance Index Edition One
notes: Collected single-volume hardcover edition covering all five chapters (Davos, Genoa, New York, Evian, Geneva); every source checked lists this as one ISBN and one hardcover printing rather than separate per-chapter volumes, so no distinct chapter number is recorded here. If the library's physical copy is a single-chapter booklet rather than the collected edition, this record should be corrected against it. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Semiautomatic Photography
edition_printrun: 1st, 290 black and white illustrations thread-sewn softcover
description:
How one tilts the camera, holds it with both hands in front of the waist.

How one looks through the viewfinder, gazes one-eyed into the world. How one hides it in stockings, behind the back, and how one lets it peep out from behind the corner of a building, as though it were a detective. Holding the Camera shows a pictorial genre from the now extinct era of analogue photography. Like the dinosaurs, supposedly the victims of a violent meteorite bombardment, also these images that were once distributed a million times over in instructions and advertisements, have been erased, deleted. «Nadine Olonetzky

title: We will never be so close again
edition_printrun: Recycled book, 10 black & white plates, 21 color plates

title: Devils & Angels Ritual Feasts in Europe
Whitewash
description:
Whitewash is Harit Srikhao's first monograph, and it turns a teenage memory of state violence into a body of staged, symbolically loaded photographs rather than a documentary account.

Srikhao was a student in Bangkok during the 2010 military crackdown on Red Shirt protesters, known as Black Saturday, and was unable to see through the government propaganda surrounding the event at the time. Years later he returned to that memory not through reportage but through elaborately staged tableaux that borrow from Thai religious iconography, fetish fantasy and popular ritual, restaging violence, nationalism and control as a kind of costumed performance. The resulting pictures use color, artifice and theatrical staging to question the shared idea of reality among Thai citizens and the use of images as tools of social control.

Published by Akina Books as a spiral-bound first edition, the book established Srikhao as one of the notable photographers to emerge from Thailand in the years following the protests. His method departs from straightforward photojournalism toward invented, symbolic restaging of political trauma.
tags: Photography, Documentary Photography, Southeast Asian Photography
notes: No ISBN issued. An AbeBooks listing cites a 2017 self-published edition ('Mt. Meru. Surgery'); the publisher's own colophon, reproduced by a retailer, gives Akina Books, 2018 as the first edition, which is used here. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Deadline
description:
277 photographs, reproductions and documents. In the highly anticipated second installment of the Deadline publications Will Steacy tells the story of an industry in crisis and a family legacy cut short.

Steacy’s latest book published by b.frank books reveals the harsh realities facing the newspaper industry today in a behind-the-scenes look at one newsroom’s grit and determination to get the news out despite shrinking advertising revenue, falling circulation, lay-offs, buy-outs, and bankruptcy. In his follow up to the critically acclaimed Deadline newspaper, this 192-page book features Steacy’s photographs of The Inquirer newsroom and printing plant, historical material from The Inquirer's archive and his own family's five-generation newsman history.

The accompanying essay by former Inquirer executive editor Gene Roberts, whose leadership won the paper 17 Pulitzer Prizes, explains how corporate media consolidation and the shift to budget cutting in an effort to maximize shareholder value were the first dominos in the newspaper industry’s subsequent downfall. Deadline opens a window into the realities of an industry in crisis and explains how and why we got here. Steacy’s in-depth examination of the media is particularly relevant in an election year in which the consequences of the de-newspaperization of America are on full display as facts and accountability have been trumped by voters' political ideology.

title: Luke Stephenson's 99x99s
description: “99x99s is a photographic road trip exploring the world of the 99 ice cream. Over 25 days and 3,500 miles I travelled deeper and deeper into the story of this British icon and the culture that made it.” “As I traveled from place to place I became fascinated by the human touches that make each cone unique and the stories which shroud the 99 in mystery.” —Luke Stephenson

title: John Stezaker: Rubell Family Collection
description:
Published by the Rubell Family Collection, Miami, in 2007, this catalog — edited by the museum's then-director Mark Coetzee — was among the first American surveys of the British collagist John Stezaker (b. 1949), drawn from the Rubells' holdings of his cut-and-paste appropriations of vintage film stills, postcards, and book plates.

The 128-page hardcover reproduces the work in color and black and white, with an essay by the critic Michael Bracewell. Stezaker's collages proceed by a single, exacting cut: film-star publicity stills spliced with postcard landscapes, faces interrupted by other faces, the seams of the source material left legible rather than smoothed away. The catalog situates that practice within an American collecting context years before Stezaker's wider institutional recognition.

Stezaker came to prominence among the British conceptualists of the 1970s and received the Deutsche Börse Photography Prize in 2012, following his 2011 Whitechapel Gallery retrospective. He is represented by The Approach, London, and Petzel Gallery, New York. This is the earliest of the four Stezaker titles in the library, alongside Silkscreens, Nude and Landscape, and One on One.

title: I Will Survive
description:
Hito Steyerl's I Will Survive follows a single 3D-scanned bullet as it moves through military supply chains, data servers and international arms fairs, using one object to trace how weapons, images and information now travel the same infrastructure.

Published by Spector Books to accompany the exhibition of the same name, the book gathers Steyerl's essayistic writing with stills and documentation from the video and installation work, extending her inquiry into surveillance, circulation and the political economy of digital images. Rather than treating the bullet as a symbol, Steyerl follows its literal supply chain, showing how the same networks that move munitions also move data, capital and images across borders. The result reads as both exhibition catalogue and standalone critical text.

Steyerl is a German artist, filmmaker and writer whose work on digital images, war and infrastructure, including How Not to Be Seen and Duty Free Art, has made her one of the most influential essayistic voices in contemporary art. I Will Survive continues that body of work, tying one physical object to the wider networks of violence and information it moves through.
notes: Cover sourced via twelve-books.com after earlier low-resolution candidates proved unusable. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Folklig Idrott
description:
Folklig Idrott (Folk-athletic games) gathers Maximilian Stejskal's mid-century photographs of traditional Swedish-Finnish rural sport, images made for an ethnographic study and republished decades later as a body of documentary photography in their own right.

Stejskal's black-and-white photographs recorded wrestling, stone-lifting, tug-of-war and other rural games practiced among Swedish-speaking communities in Finland, originally compiled for a 1954 folklore study published by the Society of Swedish Literature in Finland. In 2016, editors Marie-Isabel Vogel and Alain Rappaport returned to Stejskal's negatives, publishing this 120-page edition through Edition Patrick Frey that presents the photographs on their own terms, separated from the original academic apparatus and allowed to read as formally direct, unsentimental documents of bodies at work and at play.

Little is documented about Stejskal beyond this project; his photographs survive largely through the folklore archive they were made to serve. Their republication situates his field photography alongside Edition Patrick Frey's broader interest in vernacular and archival image-making, work produced outside any art context that later reads as such.
notes: Catalogued as 'Maximilian Still'; corrected to Maximilian Stejskal, the photographer named on the title page and in library records. Folklig Idrott translates as Folk-athletic games. This 2016 edition, edited by Marie-Isabel Vogel and Alain Rappaport, republishes photographs first compiled for a 1954 Swedish-language folklore study; the original 1954 volume was published by the Society of Swedish Literature in Finland. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: The Late Works
contributors: Dean Sobel (Author), Alex Katz (Contributor), Dorothea Rockburne (Contributor)
description:
An exclusive look at the late work of one of the most influential and enigmatic painters, whose late-career paintings are virtually unknown to the public and many are published here for the first time.

Clyfford Still (1904-1980) is a pioneer of Abstract Expressionism, along with Mark Rothko, Jackson Pollock, Lee Krasner, and Willem de Kooning. This revelatory book, accompanying a groundbreaking exhibition, investigates Clyfford Still's late work, both in painting and in drawing, made after his move to rural Maryland in 1961.

This marks a particularly fertile period for Still he made over 375 works on canvas and a staggering 1,100 works on paper in Maryland before his death in 1980 at the age of 75. Given Still's especially reclusive posture later in life and the fact that none of the artworks in Still's estate were exhibited or made available to anyone before the opening of the Clyfford Still Museum in 2011, a full-scale presentation of these forty paintings and thirty works on paper is especially meaningful.

title: Walking
description:
Walking gathers Thomas Struth's photographs of people in motion through public space, extending the artist's long study of how cities structure the bodies that move through them.

Published by Ivorypress in a perfect-bound paperback edition of 101 pages, the book sequences images of pedestrians, streets, and urban thresholds without the didactic framing of Struth's museum retrospectives, letting the act of walking itself carry the book's structure.

Struth, a member of the generation trained under Bernd and Hilla Becher at the Düsseldorf Academy, is best known for his large-scale photographs of city streets, museum interiors, and family portraits; Walking sits alongside smaller, more direct bodies of work that circle back to the street photography underlying his larger architectural series.
notes: Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Love & Hate & Other Mysteries: Found Altered Snapshots from the Collection of Thierry Struvay
description:
Love & Hate & Other Mysteries collects one hundred found snapshots that have been physically altered by the people who once owned them, faces and figures removed with scissors, pen or tears.

Drawn entirely from Thierry Struvay's collection of vernacular photography, the book reproduces 25 color and 75 black-and-white images in which a face has been cut out to fit a locket, a figure scratched away in anger, or a couple torn apart down the middle. An introduction by Glenn O'Brien frames the collection as a study of the private emotional histories left legible in damaged photographs. The book was published as a 144-page hardcover by August Editions in 2016.

The book belongs to a wider practice of found-photography collecting and publishing, treating the marks left on discarded snapshots as a form of authorship in their own right.
notes: Collection of found and altered vernacular snapshots assembled by Thierry Struvay, with an introduction by Glenn O'Brien; the images are not by a single photographer. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Pictures from Home
description:
Pictures from Home is Larry Sultan's decade-long portrait of his parents in their San Fernando Valley home, and it stands among the most influential photobooks made about family, memory and the American domestic interior.

Beginning in the early 1980s, Sultan repeatedly photographed his father Irving and mother Jean in the house where he grew up, staging scenes drawn from memory alongside pictures made in the ordinary course of their days. The book interweaves these color photographs with stills from his father's home movies, family snapshots, and transcribed conversations with his parents, building a layered, sometimes contradictory portrait that questions the truth claims of documentary photography itself. First published in 1992 to wide critical acclaim, the work was reissued by MACK in 2017 with a reworked design and expanded sequence.

Sultan, who taught for decades at California College of the Arts and died in 2009, is remembered as a central figure in the staged and suburban strands of American color photography; Pictures from Home remains the project most closely identified with his work, and its influence runs through later photographers working at the boundary of documentary and staged family portraiture.
notes: The book has several editions (Abrams 1992; MACK 2017 reissue). This record uses the confirmed MACK 2017 edition (167 pages); edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Tekerrür (Recurrence)
description:
Eighty anonymous identity photographs, rephotographed and enlarged until the one thing an ID portrait exists to do (fix a person to a name) stops working.

Süme and Öğütcen took a set of found passport-style portraits, reproduced and resized them, and sequenced them with a text that reads the results against the function they were made for. Scaled up and stripped of their documents, the faces de-subjectify: the gaze detaches from the sitter and becomes the book’s real subject, an image passed from hand to hand and rewritten by whoever holds it. The title, Tekerrür, means recurrence. It names both the repetition of the format across eighty near-identical frames and the way history and memory get written over the same pictures. The book is a slim softcover from Reccollective, its dark board blind-embossed with the title and the two names.

Süme is an Istanbul photographer and a founding member of the collectives reccollective and bandrolsüz; Tekerrür sits between 289kd (2009) and Vesika (2019), the later book returning to the same eighty gazes and extending the enquiry into photography, power and memory.
tags: Photography, Portraiture, Found Photography, Artist Book
notes: Cover credits both Selim Süme and Özgür Öğütcen in blind embossing; the second name was read directly off the copy. Published by Reccollective, Istanbul, the artist-run imprint behind Süme’s 289kd (2009) and Vesika (2019). No ISBN traced. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Radial Grammar
description:
Radial Grammar is Batia Suter's atlas of found photographs, arranging existing images into new visual sequences that let form and pattern, rather than the pictures' original captions or sources, govern meaning.

Working from an archive of appropriated photographs spanning scientific illustration, landscape and vernacular imagery, Suter builds pages of visual rhyme: recurring shapes, gestures and textures link unrelated pictures across time and origin. The 296-page book was published by Roma Publications to accompany Suter's 2018 exhibition at Le Bal, Paris, curated by Diane Dufour, and includes a separate accordion-folded supplement of illustrations bound into the volume. Texts appear in English and French.

Suter, a Swiss artist based in Amsterdam, has worked since the early 2000s with collage, appropriation and the sequencing of found images, treating photographs as raw material for essayistic argument rather than as records of firsthand observation. Radial Grammar extends the method of her earlier Parallel Encyclopedia projects into a single sustained visual grammar.
notes: Published on the occasion of Suter's exhibition at Le Bal, Paris, May 25-August 26, 2018. Includes a separate accordion-folded supplement of illustrations. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Parallel Encyclopedia #2
description:
Tiré du site Internet de Roma Publications: [vol. 2]: "Batia Suter's work intuitively situates found images in new contexts to provoke surprising reactions and significative possibilities. This volume follows on from the first Parallel Encyclopedia, published in 2007. Underlying themes of Suter's practice are the "iconification" and "immunogenicity" of old images, and the circumstances by which they become charged with new associative values. "In my work, I collect groups of images based on various themes and characteristics, and I investigate how they can manipulate each other, depending on where and how they are placed.

In the process of making this book, narrative lines unfolded before my eyes as I shifted images around.

title: Sender
description:
Sender reworks Peter Sutherland's photographic archive into a layered, disorienting stream of cropped scans, full-scale reproductions, and overlapping images of brands, logos, and signage.

Published by Printed Matter as a perfect-bound softcover, printed in color at 23 by 30 centimeters, the book includes a text by the writer Ross Simonini and was issued in a limited edition.

Sutherland works across photography, painting, and collage, often layering travel snapshots with mixed-media work printed on industrial mesh; Sender extends that same collage logic to the printed page, treating image saturation itself as subject matter.
notes: Printed Matter issued this title in a limited edition; this copy's numbering could not be confirmed and is not asserted here. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Night into Day / De Nuit en Jour
description:
American artist Sarah Sze (b. 1969) exhibited her first solo show at the Fondation Cartier pour l'art contemporain at the turn of the millennium; two decades later she returned to Jean Nouvel's building with two new sculptures made for the occasion, the subject of this catalogue.

The sculptures explore how the contemporary proliferation of images, via print and pixel, from deep space to the deep web, changes our relationship to time, memory and the physical presence of objects. Designed in close collaboration with the artist and issued with 48 different covers, the 208-page paperback documents the execution of Sze's installation and includes an essay by philosopher Bruno Latour, a conversation between Sze and Nouvel, and an essay by exhibition curator Leanne Sacramone. Published bilingually in French and English by the Fondation Cartier pour l'art contemporain, Paris, in 2020.

Sze works across sculpture, drawing and installation, building accumulations of everyday objects into structures that examine perception, scale and the passage of time; this catalogue documents her second engagement with the Fondation Cartier's exhibition spaces, twenty years after her first.
notes: Bilingual French/English catalogue, published with 48 different covers designed in collaboration with the artist; catalogued copy carries the French title, De Nuit en Jour. Contributors: Bruno Latour, Jean Nouvel, Leanne Sacramone. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: ecollage
description:
ecollage collects the collage work of Towa Tei, the Tokyo-based musician and producer best known as a founding member of Deee-Lite. He assembles cut fragments of vintage Japanese packaging, advertising, and print ephemera into layered, densely worked portraits.

The cover sets the tone: a woman's face and shoulders reconstructed from clipped magazine and product imagery, snack-food branding and pin-up photography fused into a single, slightly uncanny figure, titled in the same bright, mismatched lettering as the collages themselves. Tei has pursued this visual practice alongside his music since the 1990s.

Tei debuted with Deee-Lite in 1990, whose album World Clique established him internationally, before a long solo career spanning more than a dozen albums and the groups Sweet Robots Against the Machine and Metafive. His design and art-direction work runs parallel to the music: he was art director for Yellow Magic Orchestra's 40th-anniversary reissue and, with Tomoo Gokita, for Yukihiro Takahashi's Grand Espoir. ecollage sits at the intersection of the two practices, a visual counterpart to the sampling and recombination that define his music.

title: Season Three
description:
Season Three is the third in a series of books recording Juergen Teller's ongoing collaboration with designer Nicolas Ghesquiere for Louis Vuitton.

The 224-page paperback follows Ghesquiere's Fall-Winter 2015/16 collection through 118 color photographs, mixing press-kit images, street photography and still lifes with candid backstage and bathroom scenes and runway documentation. Rather than a conventional fashion lookbook, the book applies Teller's characteristic snapshot aesthetic to the full production cycle of a collection, from studio to runway to press circulation.

The book extends Teller's long-running practice of photographing fashion from inside its working process rather than as finished editorial imagery, a mode he has developed across decades of collaboration with designers and magazines.
notes: Third of three Louis Vuitton season books photographed by Juergen Teller with designer Nicolas Ghesquiere. Now out of print per the distributor listing. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Hairdos of Defiance
description:
Hairdos of Defiance gathers two decades of Ed Templeton's portraits of mohawked strangers, and it treats a single hairstyle as a lens onto punk identity, refusal and belonging across generations.

A former professional skateboarder turned photographer and painter, Templeton shot the portraits on film over roughly twenty years while traveling through the United States and Europe, from Disneyland to Detroit to Scotland, approaching his subjects directly on the street rather than staging them. The book sequences the pictures alongside an essay, On Mohawks, that traces the hairstyle from its origins in indigenous culture through its emergence as a punk identifier and later co-option by the mainstream, closing with its significance to Templeton's own life as an outsider kid growing up in suburbia. Deadbeat Club Press published the first edition, a small-format hardback, in 2018.

The book extends Templeton's long-running practice of documenting youth subculture — skateboarding, punk, suburban California — with the same unposed directness that runs through his other photobooks.
notes: Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Contemporary Suburbium
edition_printrun: Two-volume boxed set, issued in slipcase
description:
Contemporary Suburbium is a two-volume boxed set in which Ed Templeton and Deanna Templeton each present a separate photographic volume of Southern California suburban life, issued together in a shared slipcase.

Rather than a single co-authored sequence, the set gives each photographer their own book: Ed Templeton's volume works from his documentation of skateboarding, youth culture and the built suburban landscape of Orange County, while Deanna Templeton contributes her own parallel record of the same milieu, seen from a different vantage. Housed together, the two volumes read as complementary studies of one place and one community, shaped by a married couple who have spent decades photographing it from inside.

Ed Templeton is a photographer and professional skateboarder whose books, including Teenage Smokers and The Seconds Pass, document skate and suburban youth culture from within; Deanna Templeton's own photography, including The Swimming Pool and What She Said, focuses on adolescence, girlhood and Southern California life. Contemporary Suburbium brings their distinct bodies of work together under one shared title.
notes: Two-volume boxed set (issued in slipcase), one book by Ed Templeton and one by Deanna Templeton under a shared title; cover image shows the Ed Templeton volume with the Deanna Templeton volume visible behind it. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Wayward Cognitions
description:
Wayward Cognitions collects two decades of Ed Templeton's photographs of Orange County, California, an unsentimental record of skate culture, suburban sprawl and adolescence made by an artist who came up inside the world he photographs.

The 160-page monograph brings together Templeton's black-and-white and color images of teenagers, storefronts, parking lots and the built edges of Southern California, continuing the diaristic street photography that has run through his work since the early 1990s. It was published in 2014 by Um Yeah Arts with a text by Stijn Huijts.

Templeton, a former professional skateboarder and founder of the skate brand Toy Machine, has photographed skate and youth culture since the early 1990s, publishing widely and exhibiting internationally. His photography moves between snapshot immediacy and formal composition, treating the terrain skateboarding was built on as a lens on American adolescence more broadly.
notes: A special edition of this title exists under a separate identifier; this record describes the standard 2014 hardcover edition. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Showboat: Punk / Sex / Bodies
description:
Showboat: Punk / Sex / Bodies explores sex in punk and punk in sex, drawing on Toby Mott's archive of punk-era ephemera to complicate a movement often read as almost asexual.

Edited by Toby Mott from the Mott Collection, his holdings of punk, protest, and subcultural print material, the book gathers imagery around the body and sexuality within punk culture. Dashwood Books published the softcover in New York in 2016, in an edition of 1,500 copies.

Mott, a British artist and collector, has spent decades assembling primary punk and countercultural ephemera and publishing it in book form as the Mott Collection, of which Showboat is one volume among several exploring different facets of that archive.
notes: Catalogued title "Showboat Special Edition" corrected to the book's actual title, Showboat: Punk / Sex / Bodies; no evidence of a separate "Special Edition" SKU distinct from this standard edition was found. Published in an edition of 1,500 copies. Catalogued under “The Mott Collection”, the archive of punk and subcultural print that Toby Mott assembled and drew this book from. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Delicious Metropolis: The Desserts and Urban Scenes of Wayne Thiebaud (Fine Art Book, California Artist Gift Book, Book of Cityscapes and Sweets)
Miroslav Tichy - L'homme A La Mauvaise Camera
Edit Beijing
description:
Edit Beijing collects street photographs Guy Tillim made over a two-week residency in Beijing, working closer to his subjects than in the wide cityscapes of his earlier African work.

Tillim shot the series and, with designer Syb Kuiper, edited it down into a sequence that places photographs side by side as if forming a single continuous scene, though each is in fact a discrete image. "The more visible you are to people in the streets, the more invisible, in a certain sense, you become," Tillim has said of the shift toward standing in plain sight with a tripod-mounted camera rather than working from a distance. Editions Bessard published the hardback in 2017 in a limited edition of 500 copies, designed by Kuiper and issued in a slipcase.

Tillim, born in Johannesburg, is known for photographic surveys of African cities in transition, including Avenue Patrice Lumumba and Museum of the Revolution; Edit Beijing applies the same eye for architecture and public space to a different continent, at closer range.
notes: Editions Bessard's limited edition of 500 copies, designed by Syb Kuiper, was issued in a slipcase and included a signed C-print laid in; edition to be verified against the copy. Page count and dimensions not confirmed. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Saturated Light: Silver Works
description:
Saturated Light brings together, for the first time in one volume, almost thirty years of Wolfgang Tillmans's Silver works, abstract photographs built from marks that most photographic processes are designed to eliminate.

The 416-page hardcover documents the works themselves alongside their installation in institutions including Tate Britain (2003), the Venice Biennale (2009), K21 Dusseldorf (2013) and WIELS, Brussels (2020). An essay by art theorist Tom Holert examines the material and conceptual stakes of the series, while a conversation with photo engineer Klaus Pollmeier addresses the technical processes, intentional and accidental, behind the pictures. Tillmans describes the works on the cover itself as stained, impure, bright, unstable, exhausted, fugitive, smear, shimmer, as solid colours.

The Silver works sit apart from the rest of Tillmans's photographic practice, which otherwise centers on the depicted subject; here the subject is the photographic material and chemical process itself, a line of work he has pursued continuously since the early 1990s alongside his portrait, still-life and abstract picture-based work.
notes: The catalogue title Stained Ripe Impure Bright is the opening line of a longer text by the artist reproduced on the book's own cover (Stained Ripe Impure Bright / Diluted Unstable Exhausted Accumulated Saturated / Processed Fugitive Fixed Light / Bound Smear Shimmer Solid Colours). The book's published title is Saturated Light: Silver Works. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Wolfgang Tillmans
description:
The book that introduced Wolfgang Tillmans to a general audience, and the one that fixed the loose, unhierarchical way of looking he had been building in magazines since the late 1980s.

Published by Taschen in Cologne in June 1995, edited by Burkhard Riemschneider with a text by Simon Watney, its 176 pages run portraits of friends, pictures made in clubs and at Love Parade, still lifes of clothing and fruit, and landscapes, set beside one another at a level pitch rather than sorted into series. Tillmans had been publishing in i-D and elsewhere for several years, and the book carries that magazine sensibility over into an artist’s monograph: the images are sequenced for rhythm and adjacency, and the everyday is given the same weight as the staged.

Tillmans went on to win the Turner Prize in 2000, the first photographer and the first non-British artist to do so, and his later installations have pushed further into abstraction and camera-less work. This first Taschen volume remains the clearest record of the early practice, and the collection holds three of its companions from the same years: the Portikus Frankfurt catalogue, the Kunsthalle Zürich book, and Hatje Cantz’s Wer Liebe wagt, lebt morgen.
tags: Photography, Contemporary Art, Portraiture, Queer Culture
notes: The catalogue row read “Wolfgang Tillmans. Cologne”, which is a bibliography-style citation giving the place of publication rather than part of the title; the artist’s own bibliography lists it as “Wolfgang Tillmans. Edited by Burkhard Riemschneider. Text by Simon Watney. Taschen, Köln”, 1995. Sometimes catalogued under the series name Photo & Sexy Books. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Wolfgang Tillmans: Kunsthalle Zürich
edition_printrun: JRP Ringier Kunstverlag reprint of the catalogue for the exhibition at Kunsthalle Zürich, March 25 - May 21, 1995; exact reprint year unconfirmed
description:
Wolfgang Tillmans: Kunsthalle Zürich is the catalogue for the artist's 1995 exhibition at Kunsthalle Zürich, one of his earliest institutional surveys.

The 81-page volume, bound in gray-green boards with photo-illustrated covers, reproduces the photographs shown in the exhibition, which ran from March 25 to May 21, 1995, alongside texts by Bernhard Bürgi and Bettina Marbach in English, German and French. The show came early in Tillmans's career, at a moment when his mix of portraiture, still life, club and street photography, hung without hierarchy between large prints and magazine-scale images, was still an unfamiliar curatorial proposition for a museum context. This edition is a later reprint of the original 1995 Kunsthalle Zürich catalogue.

Tillmans is a German photographer whose work spans portraiture, abstraction, still life and installation, shown widely at institutions including Tate Britain, where he won the Turner Prize in 2000. The Kunsthalle Zürich exhibition and catalogue mark an early moment in a career that would go on to include dozens of major museum surveys.
notes: This ISBN is attached to a JRP Ringier Kunstverlag reprint of the original 1995 Kunsthalle Zürich exhibition catalogue; the year given here is the original publication/exhibition year, and the reprint's own year could not be confirmed. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Wolfgang Tillmans: Portikus Frankfurt
description:
A catalogue published for Wolfgang Tillmans' 1995 exhibition at Portikus, Frankfurt am Main, one of the early institutional shows that established the loose, wall-spanning installation approach central to his work.

Published to accompany the exhibition running September 2 to October 15, 1995, the catalogue reproduces Tillmans' photographs from the show alongside a conversation between the artist and curator Neville Wakefield, with text in German and English. Rather than presenting a single body of work in sequence, Tillmans' Portikus installation mixed subjects and scales in the manner that came to define his exhibition-making: club culture, still life, portraiture and abstraction shown together as a single field rather than a linear narrative.

Tillmans (born 1968) rose to prominence in the early 1990s with photographs of youth culture and club life for magazines including i-D, before moving into an installation practice that treats the exhibition wall itself as a compositional unit. He won the Turner Prize in 2000, the first photographer and the first non-British artist to do so, and this Portikus catalogue documents his work at an early stage of that trajectory.
notes: Catalogued as Wolfgang Tillmans. Frankfurt am Main; identified as the catalogue for Tillmans' 1995 solo exhibition at Portikus, Frankfurt, published under the title Wolfgang Tillmans, Portikus Frankfurt. No cover image could be located this session; cover to be photographed. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Wer Liebe wagt lebt morgen
contributors: Annelie Lütgens (Text), Helen Molesworth (Text), Collier Schorr (Text)
description:
Wer Liebe wagt lebt morgen is a Wolfgang Tillmans exhibition publication, gathering the photographer's images of everyday life, intimacy, and observation as printed and installed for the show.

Published in Ostfildern-Ruit, the book follows Tillmans's characteristic method of hanging photographs of widely differing subject and scale together, without a fixed hierarchy between a magazine tear sheet, a still life, and a portrait.

Tillmans, the first photographer and first non-British artist to win the Turner Prize, has spent three decades treating photography as a flexible, non-hierarchical medium, moving between club culture, still life, astronomical imagery, and abstraction; this volume is one of many exhibition-tied publications documenting that ongoing body of work.
notes: Catalogued title improperly included the publisher's location, "Ostfildern-Ruit," as part of the title; corrected here to the book's actual title. Published 1996; the year and the full form of the title are confirmed against the artist’s own bibliography, which lists it as “Wolfgang Tillmans: Wer Liebe wagt, lebt morgen / For when I’m weak I’m strong. Texts by Annelie Lütgens, Helen Molesworth, and Collier Schorr. Hatje Cantz, Ostfildern”. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Concorde
description:
Concorde is Wolfgang Tillmans' sustained study of a single subject: the Concorde supersonic jet, photographed taking off, landing, in flight, and sometimes reduced to a tiny, birdlike silhouette in the sky.

For the passengers who could afford it, Tillmans has said, flying Concorde was a glamorous but cramped and slightly boring routine, while watching it from the ground was a strange, free spectacle: a super-modern anachronism and an image of the desire to overcome time and distance through technology. The book carries no text beyond a short description on the inner front flap, letting the 62 color photographs stand on their own as both a portrait of technological beauty and a record of the environmental cost the aircraft represented. First published in 1997, this fifth printing is issued by Walther König, Köln, as a 128-page softcover.

Tillmans, born in Remscheid, Germany in 1968, works across photography, installation and print, moving fluidly between intimate portraiture and subjects like Concorde that isolate a single recurring form; the book remains one of his most enduring and frequently reprinted artist's books.
notes: Catalogued title included "- Cologne," referring to the publisher, Walther König, based in Köln (Cologne); this printing is the fifth, of a book first published in 1997. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Wolfgang Tillmans: Burg
description:
Wolfgang Tillmans' Burg is a 1998 monograph that gathers the German photographer's characteristically wide-ranging body of work into a single, deliberately unhierarchical sequence.

The book moves between portraits, still lifes, club and street photography, astronomical images, and near-abstract studies of light and material, edited and designed by Tillmans himself with an accompanying essay by critic David Deitcher. Published by Taschen in Cologne, it is a hardcover volume of 180 pages that continues Tillmans' practice of treating the photobook as its own curated space rather than a simple catalogue of prints.

Tillmans, who won the Turner Prize in 2000, has built his reputation on dissolving the boundary between documentary, fashion, and fine-art photography, and Burg sits alongside his other Taschen-era books as an early statement of that approach.
notes: Taschen, Cologne, 1998. Edited and designed by Wolfgang Tillmans, with an essay by David Deitcher. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: AC: Isa Genzken/Wolfgang Tillmans
description: Artists Isa Genzken and Wolfgang Tillman have collaborated regularly since meeting in the nineties at Daniel Buchholz gallery. This catalogue published on the occasion of the 2001 collaborative show 'Science Fiction/ Being content here and now', Museum Ludwig, Cologne features pictures from the show and a series of portraits and photographs from the artists studios in Berlin and London.

title: Abstract Pictures
description:
Abstract Pictures is a monograph that compiles Wolfgang Tillmans' non-representational, abstract photographic work over two decades.

The book showcases series like Blushes, Freischwimmer, and Lighter, exploring the possibilities of the photographic medium through techniques like camera-less exposures, darkroom manipulation, and sculptural paper forms. It contains essays by Dominic Eichler and excerpts from Tillmans' own notes, interviews, and lectures.

Designed by Tillmans and Karl Kolbitz, the book emphasizes the materiality of the photographic object itself, rather than its reproductive function. Includes unique, hand-assembled sections with layered images created during the printing process. The photograph itself—essentially divorced from its reproductive function—becomes the objet d'art. Received the German Photo Book Award in Silver, 2012. Available in English and German. Published in Ostfildern, Germany.

title: Conor Donlon
description:
In Conor Donlon, Wolfgang Tillmans (born 1968) chronicles East London’s art scene and nightlife of the early 2000s, as well as his friendship with collaborator and artist Conor Donlon.

The book sees Donlon’s appearance and style changing, as well as his backdrops: a 2003 demonstration against George W. Bush’s state visit a picnic at the park after an opening at Tillmans’s exhibition space Between Bridges the bright yellow walls of Tillmans and Donlon’s home long-gone LGBT clubs The Ghetto and The Joiners’ Arm and quieter moments spent talking in the studio and around town.

Tillmans’s photographs are at once intimate and emblematic of a flourishing arts era, where both artists’ work gained momentum. The Guardian’s culture editor Alex Needham introduces the work with an essay about Donlon’s initial role as Tillmans’s assistant, contextualizing the artists’ collaboration and the inception of London independent bookstore Donlon Books in 2008.

title: Wolfgang Tillmans: A Reader
description: This volume offers a panoramic collection of interviews and writings from an artist for whom language has always been a significant means of creative expression. Arranged chronologically, the assembled texts reflect Tillmans’ thinking on photography, music, politics, nightlife, astronomy, spirituality and activism. The sources are as varied as their content, with statements and conversations that originally appeared in exhibition catalogues rubbing up against social-media posts and song lyrics.

title: Chicha Dreams
description:
Chicha Dreams is the first book of the Peruvian photographer Nicolás Torres, compiling informal portraits made across three decades of photographing chicha parties in the shantytowns outside Lima.

Chicha is a hybrid of peasant folk music and psychedelic rock popular in Peru's working-class urban neighborhoods, carrying with it a syncretic, irreverent aesthetic and a way of life as much as a sound. Torres, who worked as a bricklayer in the poor neighborhood of Cajamarquilla outside Lima, bought a camera in the late 1970s and began photographing birthdays, weddings, concerts and chicha parties for the people around him; by the mid-1980s he had become the primary photographer for promoters organizing the parties, building an archive of nearly 60,000 negatives largely unseen outside his own community. Published by Dashwood Books in a first edition of 54 pages, the book gathers a selection of these late-night portraits with an introduction by the Peruvian art historian and curator Alfredo Villar, who discovered the archive while researching chicha culture.

Torres's work sits outside the conventions of both documentary and fine-art photography, made from within the community it depicts rather than as an outside observer's record, and Chicha Dreams was his introduction to an international audience for photography that had previously circulated only among the people it portrayed.
notes: First edition of 500 copies, published by Dashwood Books, 2014. No ISBN found through any source checked; likely never assigned one, as is common for small first editions from this publisher. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Une Genealogie Des Grandes Oreilles (French Edition)
description:
This book presents the iconographic research conducted by artist Lauren Tortil over the past three years on Big Ears: the military surveillance devices that call upon mediated listening.

This genealogy reaches beyond the principle of lineage. In 460 images, Lauren Tortil articulates her thoughts through material from various registers: paintings, film extracts, technical drawings, photographic archives, etc. The reading is accompanied by a booklet with three texts and pictures annotated by the artist. Exhausting, recontextualizing and shifting its subject beyond the initial military territory, this book reminds us that listening practices are deeply intra-connected to politics, science, medicine and art.

title: Dolce Via: Italy in the 1980s
description:
Charles H. Traub's Dolce Via: Italy in the 1980s is a color street-photography survey made across Italy in the early 1980s, from Milan south to Marsala, and it stands as one of the sharper American outsider views of Italian public life from that decade.

Working with a panoramic Widelux camera, Traub photographed everyday encounters on piazzas, beaches, and sidewalks, drawn to the saturated color and theatrical self-presentation of Italians going about ordinary business. The book collects these images with a foreword by critic Max Kozloff and an introduction by poet Luigi Ballerini, and was published by Damiani in 2014 as a 112-page hardcover.

Traub, an American photographer and longtime chair of the MFA photography program at the School of Visual Arts in New York, has published widely on street photography and social documentary; Dolce Via extends the vernacular, color-driven approach of his earlier American work to a European setting.
tags: Photography, Street Photography, Color Photography, Italy
notes: Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Rockocó: imágenes del pop-rock madrileño en los 80
description:
Rockocó collects the photocopied fanzine Miguel Trillo self-published from a market stall in Madrid in the early 1980s, a firsthand record of the city's post-Franco youth subcultures shot from inside the crowd rather than at a critical distance.

This 2017 La Fonoteca edition reprints all six original issues in facsimile — devoted in turn to mods, punks, technopop and Movida scenesters, rockers and teddy boys, and heavy metal fans — alongside a new seventh issue gathering Trillo's portraits of young Madrid musicians made between 2000 and 2016. Photocopied, stapled and sold by hand at concerts and record fairs, the originals worked as much as flyers as photobooks; the reprint preserves their scrappy, homemade format as a set of separate booklets rather than smoothing them into one bound volume.

Trillo has spent four decades photographing Spanish youth culture from the movida madrileña onward, and Rockocó sits alongside his better-known monographs, including La Primera Movida, as primary-source documentation of a scene he photographed as a participant rather than an outside observer.
notes: Facsimile reprint of Trillo's original photocopied fanzine (six issues, early 1980s) plus a new seventh issue of 2000-2016 portraits, per OpenLibrary's cataloguing of this edition. No cover image was located for this title; cover to be photographed. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Frido Troost An Educational Archive of 2863 Slides
description:
This publication is composed of all the slides Frido Troost (1960-2013) used for his classes at the Gerrit Rietveld Academie.

Troost, art historian by trade, was a pioneer in collecting photography of all sorts. In his store ‘Institute for Concrete Matter’ many types of photography were represented, varying from da-guerreotypes to albumin prints, stereo photos to family albums.

The images in this book come from all kinds of sources: paintings, advertisements, erotica, art objects, portraits, etc. They form a new collection that represents Frido Troosts associative way of looking. The slides are presented in blocks of nine, in the same construct as Frido Troost gave his classes, a non-hierarchal set up that invites the viewer to link the images freely. A controversial mix that covers a big part of the history of photography
tags: slides-(photography), Photography, pictorial-works, history, picture-books, Archive

title: Cy Twombly: In Beauty It Is Finished: Drawings, 1951–2008
publisher: Rizzoli International Publications, in association with Gagosian Gallery
description:
Cy Twombly: In Beauty It Is Finished surveys one of the least publicly seen strands of the artist's output: his drawings, made between 1951 and 2008.

The 125-page hardcover volume was published by Rizzoli in association with Gagosian Gallery to accompany a gallery exhibition of the same title, and gathers works on paper spanning Twombly's full career, from his early graphite and crayon studies through the looser, more gestural sheets of his later decades. The book is edited by Mark Francis, former Gagosian director and a longtime scholar of Twombly's work, with an essay by the art historian David Anfam situating the drawings within Twombly's broader practice.

Twombly (1928–2011) is best known for large-scale paintings that fuse gestural abstraction with classical and literary allusion; this catalogue makes the case that his works on paper, often treated as preparatory or secondary, form a parallel and equally sustained body of work.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Drawing, Exhibition Catalog
notes: Rizzoli, in association with Gagosian Gallery, 2018. Edited by Mark Francis with an essay by David Anfam. Exhibition dates and venue city not confirmed beyond the Gagosian Gallery imprint. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Real Nazis
description:
Real Nazis sets Hollywood film stills of actors playing Nazi officers directly against archival photographs of the real Third Reich officials and war criminals they were cast to resemble, and lets the reader try to tell the two apart.

The book presents the images in sequence without captions separating fiction from documentary record, so the visual likeness between cinematic villainy and historical fact does the argument's work. It follows the design and production of Piotr Uklanski's 1999 book The Nazis, extending that project's interrogation of how popular film has rehearsed and aestheticized fascist imagery.

Uklanski is a Polish-born conceptual artist whose work regularly recycles found and appropriated imagery, from film stills to folk craft, to probe collective memory and taste. Real Nazis was published by Edition Patrick Frey, the Zurich imprint that has issued several of his photographic and book-based projects.
notes: Follow-up to Uklanski's 1999 book The Nazis, reusing the same design and production. Language of the text is not confirmed against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

description: Although beauty contests did not find favor in the Soviet Union until the late 1980s by 1991 before the collapse of the Soviet Union the Soviet beauty queen had a become symbol of perestroika itself. These photographs were taken 1988 - 1990 in Leningrad at various beauty contests and at the Leningrad Beauty Institute, an academy preparing aspiring beauty queens for competition and acquired in St. Petersburg by The Archive of Modern Conflict.

title: Holding the Camera
edition_printrun: 290 black and white illustrations thread-sewn softcover
description:
How one tilts the camera, holds it with both hands in front of the waist.

How one looks through the viewfinder, gazes one-eyed into the world. How one hides it in stockings, behind the back, and how one lets it peep out from behind the corner of a building, as though it were a detective. Holding the Camera shows a pictorial genre from the now extinct era of analogue photography. Like the dinosaurs, supposedly the victims of a violent meteorite bombardment, also these images that were once distributed a million times over in instructions and advertisements, have been erased, deleted. «Nadine Olonetzky

title: Berlin 2013/1983
edition_printrun: Two volumes, bilingual English and German, text volume with 128 pages
contributors: containing essays by Sandra Bartoli, Kenneth Haynes, Anne Huffschmid, and Anh-Linh Ngo.
description:
The artist book Berlin 2013/1983 by the Canadian artists Daniel Young and Christian Giroux is an attempt to answer two interrelated research questions: what does one year of new building construction in a city look like, and how does this contemporary city compare to that of a generation earlier?

Berlin is an intriguing case study, not least because of the changing geo-politics altering the urban fabric of both East and West Berlin. With encyclopedic pretension, the artists attempted to document every building completed in Berlin in 2013 presented alongside buildings erected one generation (approximately 30 years) earlier.

title: Vacant Spaces NY
description:
A visual documentation of the post-recession and pandemic-era landscape of New York City, focusing on the potential of unused urban fabric.

The book catalogs empty storefronts and underutilized spaces using incomplete data to visualize the scale of urban vacancy. It presents case studies for converting commercial voids into housing or social services, explicitly addressing the housing crisis and retail density shifts. Features hand-applied stickers, ultra-thin calendared paper, and fluorescent spot color (Pantone 805).

title: Artists Who Make Books
description:
A vital survey of 32 internationally recognized artists who make books as part of their creative practice - features 500 images of these rarely seen works.

The 'artist's book' has long been an important form of expression, and Artists Who Make Books showcases 32 internationally recognized artists who have integrated book production into their larger creative practice. This volume features a selection of books — many rarely seen — by every artist included, an accompanying text providing further context, and over 500 illustrations of covers and interior spreads. Insightful interviews with Tauba Auerbach, Paul Chan, and Walther König, and in-depth essays by Benjamin H. D. Buchloh and Lynda Morris round out this illuminating survey.

title: What They Saw: Historical Photobooks by Women, 1843-1999
editor: Edited by Russet Lederman, Olga Yatskevich
contributors: Edited by Russet Lederman and Olga Yatskevich. Contributing Essayists: Mariama Attah, Jörg Colberg, Elizabeth Cronin, Deirdre Donohue, Anthony Hamber, Christine Hult-Lewis, Michiko Kasahara, Paula V. Kupfer, Jeffrey Ladd, Carole Naggar and Tony White
description:
Paris Photo–Aperture Foundation Catalogue of the Year Award 2021.

Kraszna-Krausz Photography Book Award 2022. Time Magazine 20 Best Photobooks of 2021. What They Saw: Historical Photobooks by Women, 1843–1999 explores photobooks created by women from photography's beginnings to the dawn of the 21st century. Edited by Russet Lederman and Olga Yatskevich (New York City: 10×10 Photobooks, 2021). Presenting a diverse geographic and ethnic selection, the What They Saw anthology interprets historical photobooks by women in the broadest sense possible: classic bound books, portfolios, personal albums, unpublished books, zines and scrapbooks. Some of the books documented are well-known publications such as Anna Atkins' Photographs of British Algae: Cyanotype Impressions (1843-1853), Germaine Krull's Métal (1928) and Diane Arbus: An Aperture Monograph (1972), while other books may be relatively unknown, such as Alice Seeley Harris' The Camera and the Congo Crime (c. 1906), Varvara Stepanova's Groznyi smekh. Okna Rosta (1932), Eslanda Cardozo Goode Robeson's African Journey (1945), Fina Gómez Revenga's Fotografías de Fina Gómez Revenga (1954), Eiko Yamazawa's Far and Near (1962) and Gretta Alegre Sarfaty's Auto-photos: Série transformações—1976: Diário de Uma Mulher—1977 (1978).

Also addressed in the publication are the glaring gaps and omissions in current photobook history, in particular the lack of access, support and funding for photobooks by non-Western women and women of color. Structured as a traveling reading room, publication and series of public events, the project launched in November 2021 with the release of this publication. The reading room is now touring internationally to allow the over 250 books in the project to be shared with a global community. Contributing Essayists: Mariama Attah, Jörg Colberg, Elizabeth Cronin, Deirdre Donohue, Anthony Hamber, Christine Hult- Lewis, Michiko Kasahara, Paula V. Kupfer, Jeffrey Ladd, Carole Naggar and Tony White. Contributing Book Description Researchers-Writers: Rose Bishop, María Beatriz H. Carrión, Jesse Dritz, Taylor Fisch, Lauren Graves, Anna Jacobson, Paula V. Kupfer, Ashley McNelis, Katherine Mitchell, Frankie Moutafis, Carole Naggar, Caroline M. Riley and Kelsey Sucena. What They Saw: Historical Photobooks by Women, 1843–1999 is a follow-up project to 10×10 Photobooks' How We See: Photobooks by Women, which showcased contemporary photobooks by women (2000-2018) and began in 2018 at the New York Public Library with a tour to five other venues.
