title: Ecal Photography
contributors: Text by Nathalie Herschdorfer, Milo Keller.
designer: Art Direction by Julien Gallico & Olga Prader
description: An art school is an image factory. New generations of artists are constantly emerging, joining the marathon of exhibitions and publications from the very first years of their creative lives. In this context, the art school has become a particularly attractive place for ambitious young artists.

title: Houseplants Covered With Snow
description:
Houseplants Covered With Snow is a small collage artist book by the Dutch artist Ruth Van Beek, built entirely from cut, folded, and reassembled photographs sourced from vintage horticultural books and magazines.

Van Beek works from a growing personal archive of found photographic material, mostly plant and specimen photography from the 1950s through the 1970s, which she cuts out, pastes, and folds into odd, quietly surreal compositions. The 45-page softcover book, 171 x 241 mm, was published by Dashwood Books in New York in 2014 and was issued alongside a companion volume, Houseplants, from the same body of work.

Van Beek's practice sits at the intersection of photography, collage, and sculpture; she treats the found photograph as raw material rather than document, and her books, including The Levitator and The Cast, have become a recognizable strand of contemporary Dutch photobook-making built on appropriation and reconstruction rather than original image-making.
notes: Catalogue title combines two Dashwood Books publications sold as a pair, Houseplants Covered With Snow and a companion volume, Houseplants. This record is filled against Houseplants Covered With Snow (2014, Dashwood Books, 45pp, 171 x 241 mm), the one independently confirmed via a separate library catalogue entry; the companion Houseplants could not be separately verified and is not described here. No ISBN found for this title in any source checked. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Paris Mortel
description:
Paris Mortel is Johan van der Keuken's early photobook of Paris, made while he was still in his twenties and years before he turned primarily to filmmaking.

Published in 1963 by C. de Boer Jr. in Hilversum, the book gathers black-and-white street photographs made in Paris, where van der Keuken had studied at the IDHEC film school; its title, using the French mortel rather than a Dutch equivalent, signals the somber, elegiac register of the images. A revised and expanded edition, retitled Paris mortel retouché and co-credited to Willem van Zoetendaal, was published by Van Zoetendaal Publishers in 2013, fifty years after the original.

Van der Keuken (1938-2001) is best known internationally as a documentary filmmaker, but he began as a photographer, publishing his first book, Wij zijn 17 (We Are 17), while still a teenager. Paris Mortel belongs to this early photographic period before his move into cinema, a medium in which he continued to work with still and moving images side by side for the rest of his career.
notes: Two van der Keuken titles share this name: the original 1963 C. de Boer Jr. (DEBO) edition and a substantially revised 2013 Van Zoetendaal Publishers reissue titled Paris mortel retouché, co-credited to Willem van Zoetendaal, with a different ISBN. This record follows the catalogued title and matches it to the 1963 original; no cover image was located for that edition. Edition to be verified against the copy. Cover to be photographed. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Soon
description:
By means of a dialogue between the text and the visual material from the videos, Steyn Bergs and Emma van der Put want to take a critical look at how images are mobilised to illustrate certain visions of the future, and how they contribute to the creation of such visions—which are never ‘neutral’—in the present.

On the basis of the videos made by Van der Put, this publication focuses on the specific working and politics of images in the Noordwijk and the Expo area in Brussels. Within these locations, developments that are currently taking place throughout Europe (from property speculation to migration flows) manifest themselves in a concrete and local manner. This book is released in context of the solo exhibition “Mall of Europe” by Emma van der Put at Mu.Zee, Ostend. With the generous support of Mu.Zee, Mondriaan Fund, Jaap Harten Fond

title: Can't Pay You to Disappear
description:
Thomas Vandenberghe's Can't Pay You to Disappear is a handmade photobook that unravels the life span of an intense relationship, where love, obsession and loss run together into a single, urgent narrative.

The book pairs fragments of dialogue, spoken between an unnamed couple, with images scanned directly from Vandenberghe's original darkroom prints, mostly reproduced at their original size so that the physical trace of his process, cropping, blur, torn and collaged prints, remains visible on the page. Published by AKINA Books in a first edition of 200 copies, it is bound with a French-fold stab-strip structure and silkscreened in two colours on white cloth, sold out shortly after release.

The book also marks a shift in Vandenberghe's photography, from early, minimal images toward physical intervention on the print itself, collage, tearing and repetition, a strategy he returned to in later, related work built around the same relationship.
notes: Self-published, handmade first edition of 200 copies from AKINA Books, sold out. No ISBN was assigned to this title. Cover to be photographed: the only reproduction traced carries a bookseller watermark. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Kiki / 12
description:
Kiki / 12 is one part of a twelve-issue fanzine project by fashion photographer Willy Vanderperre, each installment built around a single model rather than a season or a brand.

Published by IDEA in London in 2017, this issue is devoted to Kiki Willems: an unbound, loose-folded publication of 23 pages that pairs extreme close-up portraiture, including a signature detail shot of the model's ear, with more conventional studio images. Vanderperre shot each of the twelve /12 issues in the same stripped-down format, treating the fanzine as a way to picture models as individuals outside of a fashion campaign's usual framing. Each edition was printed in a run of 300 copies.

Vanderperre, long associated with Raf Simons and stylist Olivier Rizzo, is one of contemporary fashion photography's defining image-makers; the /12 series, alongside subjects including Julia Nobis, Abbey Lee, and Natasha Poly, sits apart from his commercial work as a sustained, self-directed portrait project.
notes: IDEA, London, 2017. One issue of Vanderperre's twelve-part /12 fanzine series, each devoted to a single model; this issue features Kiki Willems. First edition, unbound, loose-folded format, printed in an edition of 300. No ISBN found for this self-published fanzine. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Jonas / 12
description:
Jonas / 12 gathers intimate portraits and close-up studies of the model Jonas Gloer by fashion photographer Willy Vanderperre, stripping his subject away from the clothes and sets of a fashion shoot to the face alone.

The publication is one of twelve unbound amazines that make up IDEA's 12 series, each devoted to a single model and each issued loose, in a poly bag, rather than bound as a conventional book. Vanderperre drew the imagery from his fashion work with Gloer, whom he has photographed since the model was in his teens.

Vanderperre is a Belgian photographer known for his fashion work with Raf Simons, Prada, and Dior, and for a recurring cast of models he returns to across seasons and campaigns. Jonas / 12 sits alongside his other self-published and small-press projects, which move his fashion photography into a more private, sustained register.
notes: One of twelve unbound amazines in IDEA's 12 series, each dedicated to a single model; this volume features Jonas Gloer. Self-contained, no ISBN. Page count and dimensions not confirmed against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Photobook Phenomenon
editor: Vicenç Villatoro, Pepe De Mora, Moritz Neumüller, Lesley Martin
description:
Published to accompany the exhibition of the same name at Barcelona's Centre de Cultura Contemporània (CCCB), Photobook Phenomenon traces the rise of the photobook from an overlooked publishing format to one of the central forms through which contemporary photography circulates.

Edited by Vicenç Villatoro, Pepe De Mora, Moritz Neumüller, Lesley Martin and Martin Parr, the catalogue combines historical and critical essays with statements from photographers who work directly in the book form, including Laia Abril, Julián Barón, Alejandro Cartagena, Jana Romanova, Viviane Sassen, Thomas Sauvin, and Katja Stuke and Oliver Sieber, each discussing the creative process behind making a photobook. The exhibition itself explored ways of displaying and handling photobooks through interactive installations, letting visitors experience the object quality of the works rather than only reproductions of their pages.

Produced with Fundación Foto Colectania and published by RM Verlag, the book functions as both an exhibition record and a standalone survey of contemporary photobook culture, gathering curators, historians and practitioners around a format that has increasingly become the primary site of photographic authorship.
notes: Anthology of curatorial and photographer contributions on the photobook as a form; catalogued as NA VA per house convention since it is a multi-editor, multi-contributor volume rather than a single-author book. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Nudes: Curated by Julien Dossena
contributors: Julien Dossena (Curator), Coco Capitán (Photographs and text)
description:
Nudes is a fashion-photography publication commissioned as a deliberate response to Jean Clemmer's 1969 monograph Nues, a book of female nudes styled in Paco Rabanne's sculptural metal and plastic garments.

A Magazine Curated By's editor Dan Thawley asked Julien Dossena, Creative Director of the house of Paco Rabanne, to curate a contemporary answer to Clemmer's book. Dossena in turn commissioned the photographer Coco Capitán, who shot the series at Villa Noailles, the 1920s Robert Mallet-Stevens estate above Hyères, using contemporary and archive Paco Rabanne pieces and her own accompanying poems. The 100-page softcover, published in a limited edition of 1000 in 2016, also carries a dialogue between Dossena and Thawley on nudity and eroticism in fashion imagery.
notes: Catalogued as Various given the curated, multi-contributor authorship: photographs and text by Coco Capitan, curated by Julien Dossena. Publisher and page count from a direct fetch of amagazinecuratedby.com; a photo-eye citation for the same ISBN independently gives a different page count (94pp) and lists Paco Rabanne, Paris as publisher, which is not reflected here. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Nuogo kūno teorija
description:
Nuogo kūno teorija (Theory of a Naked Body) is a group exhibition catalogue examining how Lithuanian photographers pictured the nude body across three decades of the country's twentieth-century photography.

Edited by Donatas Stankevičius with text by Milda Kiaušaitė, the catalogue draws together black-and-white nude photographs by Lithuanian authors made from the 1960s through the early 1990s, organized around the charged relationship between photographer and model. The editor's note frames that dynamic as a tension between making an artistic image of a naked body and merely viewing one under photography's cover. Published in 2016 by Kaunas Photography Gallery in an edition of 500, the softcover volume is bilingual in Lithuanian and English and printed on Munken Lynx stock.

As a group survey rather than a single photographer's monograph, the catalogue positions individual Lithuanian nude studies within a shared, era-spanning inquiry into how the genre negotiated Soviet-era and post-Soviet attitudes toward the body.
notes: English translation of the Lithuanian title: Theory of a Naked Body. Bilingual exhibition catalogue on Lithuanian nude photography from the 1960s to the early 1990s, edited by Donatas Stankevičius with text by Milda Kiaušaitė. Edition of 500 copies. Cover to be photographed: the only reproduction traced carries a bookseller watermark. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Yes Yes Yes Alternative Press: '66-'77 from Provo to Punk
description:
Yes Yes Yes Alternative Press: '66-'77 from Provo to Punk is a survey catalogue documenting the international underground and alternative press of the late 1960s and 1970s, from the Dutch Provo movement through to the emergence of punk.

Edited and curated by Emanuele De Donno and Amedeo Martegani, the nearly 500-page volume reproduces underground newspapers, magazines and zines from across Europe and North America, chiefly in illustrations, with the periodicals' own titles listed along the spine. It includes interviews with editors, artists and writers involved in this publishing culture, translated by Myriam Laplante. The book was co-published by a+mbookstore, Milano, and VIAINDUSTRIAE publishing, Foligno, in collaboration with the COLLI publishing platform, Rome.

It was published as the catalogue for a linked set of exhibitions: Yes Yes Yes Alternative Press at the Palazzo Trinci, Foligno (April 26-May 18, 2014); Yes Yes Yes Alternative Press: From Provo to Punk at Collegio Tridente, Urbino (June 25-26, 2014); and Yes Yes Yes at COLLI independent art gallery, Rome (April 18-June 6, 2015). As a group survey with no single author, the volume is catalogued here as Various Artists.
tags: Art, Zines, Underground Press, Exhibition Catalog
notes: Group survey catalogue with no single author; catalogued as Various Artists. A German bookseller listing gives an alternate translated title, "Yes Yes Yes: Revolutionary Press in Italy 1966-1977, From Mondo Beat to Zut" -- the title and colophon used here follow the OpenLibrary/publisher record. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Prkýnka na maso jsme uřízli
description:
Prkýnka na maso jsme uřízli documents the first years of Czech skateboarding culture, up to 1990, through photographs and first-person accounts from people who were part of the scene.

The book combines archival and contemporary photography with interviews, including with actor Petr Forman and snowboarder Luděk Váša, to reconstruct the look and atmosphere of an underground youth culture with little existing documentation. It was published by the small Czech press Yinachi in 2013, supported by Budweiser Budvar's BU2R platform for urban culture.

Martina Overstreet and Michal Nanoru assembled the book as what reviewers describe as the first publication to capture this period of Czech skate culture in any depth, placing it alongside a small body of regional subculture documentary photobooks rather than within either author's wider individual output, which could not be independently confirmed this session.
notes: Title translates literally as We Sawed Off Little Meat-Cutting Boards, apparently Czech skateboarding slang for the decks themselves; exact idiom not independently confirmed. Written by Martina Overstreet with Michal Nanoru; both names identified via databazeknih.cz; edition, format, and pagination could not be confirmed and should be checked against the copy. Cover image is a small (250x326) scan; a higher-resolution scan was not found. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: SPBN: Self Publish, Be Naughty
description:
Self Publish, Be Naughty is an anthology assembled under the Self Publish, Be Happy imprint, edited by Bruno Ceschel, bringing together self-published photographic work from a wide roster of contributors.

As with other Self Publish, Be Happy projects, the book operates as a survey of independent and self-directed photographic practice rather than a single-author monograph, collecting images and contributions submitted directly by the photographers involved rather than commissioned or curated through a conventional publishing house.

Self Publish, Be Happy was founded by Bruno Ceschel in London to champion self-publishing as a mode of photographic practice, running workshops, an archive and a series of anthology publications of which this is one; the project has been influential in framing self-publishing as a legitimate and widely practiced strand of contemporary photography rather than a fallback to institutional publishing.
notes: Multi-contributor Self Publish, Be Happy anthology edited by Bruno Ceschel; the catalogue row recorded 75 contributors. Catalogued as NA VA per house convention. No ISBN or publication year could be confirmed through AbeBooks or OpenLibrary; the publisher's own site was unreachable at the time of research. Edition to be verified against the copy. Cover to be photographed. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: AKINA Publishers
contributors: Photographers: AM projects (Tiane Doan Na Champassak, Olivier Pin-Fat, Laura Rodari, Hiroshi Takizawa, Thomas Vandenberghe, Daisuke Yokota)
description: About the project: 1 month of shooting, 1 year in the making, 3AM is an experimental collective project unlike any others, a psychedelic experience brought to you by the long-term collaboration between AKINA and AM Projects. AM primarily means ‘After Midnight’, but it can also refer to ‘a.m’ (ante meridiem or before midday). AM projects is set up by independent photographers as a space to manifest themselves internationally as a likeminded group via jointly curated exhibitions and publications.

title: EROTISH (book + print)
edition_printrun: Edition of 100, signed and numbere, ills colour / b&w, paperback
description:
Her name is Julia, his name is Vincent. They met almost 10 years ago, and have been creating together for 5 years.

‘Erotish’ is an exercise in style, inspired by the aesthetics of the 1980s. Nostalgic for a time when “everything seemed positive, carefree, and where aesthetics were the priority”, the photographers play with retro codes, a few clothes in satin, naked bodies on motorcycles, a subtle blurry effect… But far from producing a vulgar sexy collection, or merely copy and pasting a certain aesthetic, the duo reclaims to modernize this aesthetic. (Cyrielle Gendron for Photo fr)

title: Homo Viksraitis
description:
Homo Viksraitis is a 2017 paperback photobook by the Lithuanian photographer Rimaldas Viksraitis, issued by Dashwood Books, the New York bookshop and small press.

Little bibliographic detail on the book's contents is available from the sources checked; it was published as a limited first edition in softcover. It is a separate title from Viksraitis's best-known book, Grimaces of the Weary Village, Photographs 1976-2006, selected by Martin Parr, and should not be confused with it.

Viksraitis (b. 1954) has worked since the 1970s photographing rural life in Lithuania's Sasnava region, and Martin Parr's championing of his work through the Grimaces of the Weary Village project brought him international recognition, including an infinity award from the International Center of Photography in 2009.
notes: Catalogue entry read 'Rimaldas Virsraitis / Homo Viksraitis'; confirmed the photographer's name is Rimaldas Viksraitis and that Homo Viksraitis is a real, separate title from Grimaces of the Weary Village, not a corruption of it. Page count and dimensions could not be confirmed from any source checked. Cover to be photographed: no usable cover image could be retrieved. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: A Black Hole Is Everything a Star Longs to Be
description:
A beautifully designed panorama of Kara Walker’s works on paper―all reproduced for the first time This gorgeous 600-page volume, with a printed cloth-over-paper binding, provides an exciting opportunity to delve into the creative process of Kara Walker, one of the most celebrated artists working in the United States today.

Primarily recognized for her monumental installations, Walker also works with ink, graphite and collage to create pieces that demonstrate her continued engagement with her own identity as an artist, an African American, a woman and a mother. More than 700 works on paper created between 1992 and 2020―which are reproduced in print for the first time from the artist’s own strictly guarded private archive―are collected in this volume, thus capturing Walker’s career with an unprecedented level of intimacy. Since the early 1990s, the foundation of her artistic production has been drawing and working on paper in various ways. Walker’s completed large-format pieces are presented among typewritten notes on index cards and dream journal entries sketches and studies for pieces appear alongside collages.

The result is a volume that allows readers to become eyewitnesses to the genesis of Walker’s art and the transformative power of the figures and narratives she has created over the course of her career. Now based in New York, Kara Walker was born in Stockton, California, in 1969. She received her Master of Fine Arts from the Rhode Island School of Design in 1994 soon afterwards, Walker rose to prominence for her large, provocative silhouettes installed directly onto the walls of exhibition spaces. Walker’s work confronts history, race relations and sexuality in a decidedly non-conciliatory manner, urging the public to reconsider established narratives surrounding the experiences of African Americans in particular.

title: The Ecstasy of St. Kara: Kara Walker, New Work
contributors: Ari Marcopoulos (Photographer), John Lansdowne, Tracy K. Smith
description:
Kara Walker's work astutely examines race, gender, and identity.

Walker's newest series of large-scale drawings stem from her consideration of monuments and notions of permanence and impermanence following her massive public art project, A Subtlety, in Brooklyn. Influenced in part by the artist's recent residency at the American Academy in Rome, this series of drawings is an extensive examination of how Walker envisions the rise and fall of society. Richly illustrated, this publication includes plates of each work, as well as intimate photographs of the artist at work taken by her partner, acclaimed artist and filmmaker Ari Marcopoulos.

An introduction by Reto Thüring and Beau Rutland contextualizes the importance of this latest evolution within Walker's oeuvre John Lansdowne addresses the topic of Christian iconography and its relationship to Walker's new drawings and Pulitzer Prize–winning poet Tracy K. Smith contributes a new poem. In addition, a text by Walker considers her work within the recent political climate. Published for the Cleveland Museum of Art exhibition (09/10/16–12/31/16).
tags: Art, Black Artists, Exhibition Catalogues, Contemporary Art, Drawing

title: Made Glorious Summer
description:
Made Glorious Summer takes its title from the opening line of Shakespeare's Richard III — "Now is the winter of our discontent / Made glorious summer" — and gathers a body of Nick Waplington's photographs under that note of uneasy seasonal turn.

Published by the Tokyo imprint Powershovel Books in a numbered edition of 500, the paperback continues Waplington's long-running documentary interest in everyday English life; its cover image, a lone hooded figure walking a coastal path at dusk past a wind-bent tree, sets the book's tone of solitary, overcast English landscape rather than the crowd scenes of his earlier work.

Waplington (born London, 1965) first drew wide attention with Living Room (1991), an intimate document of a working-class Nottingham family's daily life, and has since moved between documentary photography, fashion collaborations (including work with designer Alexander McQueen), and small-press editions; Made Glorious Summer belongs to the run of independently published, Japan-printed books through which much of his later photography has appeared.
notes: Identified via three matching AbeBooks listings (title, author and ISBN agree); Powershovel Books' own site is defunct so no publisher page or year could be confirmed. Issued as a numbered edition of 500 copies. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Anaglypta 1980-2020
description:
“1979…Fuel strikes, rubbish piling up in the street it felt like the end of times, the end of my childhood at least.

As we danced to the sound of joy division and the clash in my bedroom during the six week period that schools were closed I saw this collapse as only a positive thing, concerts and skate parks for me instead of studying, I loved it. As the year turned the new decade, 1980 I was 14 years old and i somehow got hold of my first camera. It gave me a place in the do it yourself movement of the post punk generation. I could take pictures wherever I went and share them with friends and try to get a few into local fanzines. That was the goal, fanzine photographer back then in 1980 aged 14. As the years progressed and punk gave way to electro, hip hop and then house music all night long I carried the camera with me always.

Without thinking about the long term consequences of this I slowly but surely started to build an archive of the time, my time. The music I loved became a gateway to art and politics and eventually lead me to art school. From there the need to find something to belong to became an obsession and then a life. Always the camera, always the people…so this book is part one a crisscrossing non linear journey through those 40 years using the images I have taken ‘on the go’ mixed with a number of smaller projects that have never seen the light of day. Plus projects for art forum and gallery only based work. . I hope you enjoy the adventure in pictures as much as I did making them. Oh and Anaglypta…its whatever you want it to be.” Nick Waplington.

title: Warhol : le grand monde d'Andy Warhol
From A to B and Back Again
contributors: Jessica Beck (Contributor), Okwui Enwezor (Contributor), Trevor Fairbrother (Contributor), Hendrik Folkerts (Contributor), Branden W. Joseph (Contributor), Barbara Kruger (Contributor), Glenn Ligon (Contributor), Michael Sanchez (Contributor), Lynne Tillman (Contributor)
description:
A unique 360‐degree view of an incomparable 20th-century American artist One of the most emulated and significant figures in modern art, Andy Warhol (1928–1987) rose to fame in the 1960s with his iconic Pop pieces.

Warhol expanded the boundaries by which art is defined and created groundbreaking work in a diverse array of media that includes paintings, sculptures, prints, photographs, films, and installations. This ambitious book is the first to examine Warhol’s work in its entirety. It builds on a wealth of new research and materials that have come to light in recent decades and offers a rare and much-needed comprehensive look at the full scope of Warhol’s production—from his commercial illustrations of the 1950s through his monumental paintings of the 1980s.

Donna De Salvo explores how Warhol’s work engages with notions of public and private, the redefinition of media, and the role of abstraction, while a series of incisive and eye-opening essays by eminent scholars and contemporary artists touch on a broad range of topics, such as Warhol’s response to the AIDS epidemic, his international influence, and how his work relates to constructs of self-image seen in social media today.

title: Andy Warhol. Polaroids
description:
Andy Warhol was a relentless chronicler of life and its encounters.

Carrying a Polaroid camera from the late 1950s until his death in 1987, he amassed a huge collection of instant pictures of friends, lovers, patrons, the famous, the obscure, the scenic, the fashionable, and himself. Created in collaboration with the Andy Warhol Foundation, this book features hundreds of these instant photos.

Portraits of celebrities such as Mick Jagger, Alfred Hitchcock, Jack Nicholson, Yves Saint Laurent, Pelé, Debbie Harry are included alongside images of Warhol’s entourage and high life, landscapes, and still lifes from Cabbage Patch dolls to the iconic soup cans. Often raw and impromptu, the Polaroids document Warhol’s era like Instagram captures our own, offering a unique record of the life, world, and vision behind the Pop Art maestro and modernist giant.
tags: Art, Art Book, New York City, photograhy, polaroids

title: War Sand
description:
Donald Weber's War Sand approaches the D-Day invasion of Normandy through a single, unexpected forensic lens: a grain of sand.

Working with colleagues, Weber examined the sand of the Normandy beaches where the invasion was fought, gathering physical evidence of the battle that remains embedded in the coastline decades on, fragments of shrapnel and war matériel visible under magnification. The 371-page volume interleaves these forensic images with scientific data, wartime spy-craft references, film stills, dioramas, drone photography, private postwar memoirs and seaside photographs, building an immersive account of collective memory rather than a conventional documentary narrative. It includes an essay by Larry Frolick and a fold-out map, and was published by Polygon in 2018 following an earlier, smaller self-published edition.

Weber is a photographer known for long-term, research-driven projects on conflict, power and memory, including Interrogations and Bastard Eden, Our Chernobyl. War Sand extends that method to a historical subject, asking what a landscape retains of an event and how photography can make that retention visible.
notes: Printed Matter also lists an earlier, self-published edition of this project (D. Weber, Amsterdam, 2017, signed, edition of 875); the record here follows the 2018 Polygon paperback edition matching this ISBN. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Function
contributors: Isabella Burley (Text), Elise Gallant (Contributor), Jack (Contributor), Lydia Lunch (Contributor), Emma Roach (Contributor), Jamie Andrew Reid (Art Direction)
description:
Function is Harley Weir's contribution to Baron, a numbered series of hardback books produced by the London art-direction studio of the same name, each handed to a different image-maker with an open brief.

Across 166 pages, Weir builds a visual essay around the body's biological conditions, reproduction, birth, and the nipple's conflicting roles as erogenous zone and feeding organ, treating each as a site where the body's functions collide with how they are policed and consumed. The book, art-directed by Jamie Andrew Reid, brings together photography with text and contributions from Isabella Burley, Lydia Lunch, Elise Gallant, Jack, and Emma Roach, and was printed in a first edition of 1,000 copies.

Weir, a British photographer known for blurring documentary and fashion image-making, has published a run of similarly self-directed photobooks including Homes and Paintings with Loose Joints; Function sits alongside those as one of the more overtly political entries in her bibliography.
notes: Baron, London, 2018 (Baron issue 5). Art direction by Jamie Andrew Reid; texts and contributions by Isabella Burley, Lydia Lunch, Elise Gallant, Jack, and Emma Roach. First edition of 1,000 copies. No ISBN found; publication year taken from a secondary source rather than the book's own colophon. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: 艾未未: 纽约1983-1993
contributors: San ying tang she ying yi shu zhong xin, Chambers Fine Art (Gallery)
notes: Photographs of New York City's Lower East Side, 1983 to 1993.

title: On the Table
description:
On the Table surveys the full span of Ai Weiwei's career, from his early conceptual work in 1980s New York, shaped by Warhol, Duchamp, and Johns, to his present standing as one of the best-known and most influential contemporary Chinese artists.

The book is illustrated throughout with a mix of previously unseen work and key pieces from across thirty-five years of practice, including his Study of Perspective series and his sunflower-seed installations, set alongside documentation of the activism for which he has become widely known. It includes a text by Rosa Pera and an interview with the artist by Lluís Homs, and was published by the Madrid house La Fábrica in 2015.

Ai Weiwei works across sculpture, installation, architecture, film, and social media, and has used each in turn to criticize the Chinese government's record on human rights and free expression. On the Table joins a substantial body of monographs and exhibition catalogues surveying an output that spans conceptual objects to large-scale public installations.
notes: Career-spanning monograph with text by Rosa Pera and an interview by Lluís Homs, published by La Fábrica in 2015. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: The Powder
description:
The Powder is Jocko Weyland's artist's book on the golden era of American ski culture, built around growing up skiing in Colorado in the late 1970s and early 1980s.

Assembled from found and archival imagery, the book sets skiing before its absorption into big commercial resorts and before snowboarding reshaped the sport, recovering a period when the culture around skiing was scrappier, weirder and closer to the counterculture aesthetics of the decade than to the branded resort imagery that came to define the sport later. Published by Dashwood Books in a first edition of 500 copies and designed by Hans Seeger, the book pairs skiing imagery with the loose, collage-like sequencing characteristic of Weyland's other publications.

Weyland, born in Helsinki in 1967, is a writer, artist and curator whose books include The Answer Is Never: A Skateboarder's History of the World (Grove Press, 2002) and, also with Dashwood, Danny's Lot, Geomancy and Egg Strike on Orchard. He founded the serial publication Elk in 2003 and later served as Chief Curator at MOCA Tucson; his recurring interest in vernacular American subcultures — skateboarding in The Answer Is Never, skiing in The Powder — runs through both his writing and his artist's books.
notes: Catalogued author field carried a (ed) annotation; Weyland is credited on the book itself as author, so the role is recorded as Author here. First edition of 500 copies, designed by Hans Seeger, published by Dashwood Books, 2011. No ISBN, page count or trim size found through any source checked. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Peer to Peer
description:
Peer to Peer is Hannah Whitaker's study of how photographs can behave like a network, iterating and cross-referencing one another rather than standing as single, isolated images.

The book alternates a full-page photograph with a following spread of up to four smaller images that relate back to it, using repeated marks made through in-camera masking to give the sequence a linear, almost textual logic. The cover spells out the book's title and author in an invented, illegible alphabet, inverting the photographs' own logic by asking to be looked at rather than read. Published by MOREL Books in London in 2015 as a 100-page hardcover in an edition of 1000, it includes an accompanying text insert by the poet Aaron Kunin.

Whitaker, a Brooklyn-based photographer known for constructed, in-camera studio work that treats the photographic apparatus itself as subject matter, has exhibited widely and published with MOREL Books and other independent presses; Peer to Peer is among her more systematic explorations of photographic seriality.
notes: Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Michael Williams by Eric Crosby, Michael Williams, et al.
description:
Over the last 10 years, Los Angeles–based Michael Williams (born 1978) has created paintings known for their layered imagery, eye-popping color and use of airbrushing and inkjet printing.

His large-scale works begin as drawings either on paper or on the computer screen before they are printed or transferred to canvas and then embellished with oil paint. Williams’ narrative content reveals a dark sense of humor about everyday life, often exploring the role of the painter as observer. Wickedly funny allegories merge with abstract painting as free-form amoebic shapes frequently fill the entirety of his canvases.

The resulting paintings offer a dense and absorbing terrain of color and form. Michael Williams is published to accompany the artist’s first US solo museum exhibition, at Carnegie Museum of Art, where he presents a new body of his large-scale paintings as well as drawings that mix collage and free-associative mark-making

title: Michael Williams: Things You Shouldn't Understand
Michael Williams
description:
Michael Williams surveys the recent evolution of the New York-based painter's practice, from large gestural oil paintings toward similarly scaled canvases printed with a billboard-sized inkjet printer.

Despite this shift in materials, Williams's paintings retain a warmth and personal quality, drawing on a dense catalogue of imagery built through drawing and a mining of the artist's inner psyche; the pictures are often comic, occasionally pointed about the present state of humankind, without settling into an accusatory tone. Refusing to side definitively with representation or abstraction, Williams instead pursues his own line of complex image-making. Published by JRP|Editions in 2015 as a hardcover of 64 pages with 45 color plates, the book was issued to accompany Williams's solo exhibition at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts, and includes essays by writer George Pendle and curator Dan Nadel.

Williams (born 1978) works between Los Angeles and New York; this monograph, edited by Lionel Bovier, captures a pivotal moment in his practice as he moved from painting by hand toward the hybrid drawing-to-print process that has since become central to his work. The Hudson Street Library separately holds Williams's 2017 Carnegie Museum of Art catalogue, from his first US solo museum exhibition.
notes: The catalogued title field was a pasted bookseller listing ("Michael Williams by Dan Nadel, George Pendle, et al. Aug 25, 2015"); the actual published title is simply Michael Williams, with Nadel and Pendle as essay contributors. This is a distinct title from the library's other Michael Williams catalogue (Carnegie Museum of Art, 2017, ISBN 9780880390583). Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Michael Williams: Traditional Cornish Cottages
description:
Michael Williams' Traditional Cornish Cottages is an artist's book that layers hand-drawn portraiture with the flattened imagery of the internet.

Throughout the 112-page volume, drawings of faces and figures are repeatedly interrupted by a uniform, cropped image of a browser window open on a lifestyle or commerce website, as though the screen itself were intruding on the drawn page. These sequences alternate with runs of entirely black and entirely white pages, producing a flickering effect Williams has compared to rapidly clicking back through a browsing history. Despite its topographic-sounding title, the book has no connection to Cornwall or vernacular architecture; the title reads as one more found, incongruous fragment of online language. Published by Karma, New York, in a softcover edition of 750.

It is the fifth artist's book Williams has made with Karma, part of an ongoing series of print projects that run alongside his paintings. Williams (born 1978) is known for large-scale, airbrushed and inkjet-transferred paintings mixing collage, cartooning and abstraction; his books extend that interest in appropriated, mass-produced imagery into a graphic, black-and-white register.
notes: This is the painter Michael Williams (born 1978, represented by David Kordansky Gallery), not the Cornish topographer of the same name; the title is a found, incongruous phrase and the book has no connection to Cornwall. Karma and David Kordansky Gallery list a 2017 publication date; some retailers list a February 2018 release date for the same edition. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Michael Williams: How to Ruin an Omelet
description:
Michael Williams' How to Ruin an Omelet gathers a body of drawings made in dry marker, a medium the American painter has used as a loose, fast counterpart to his large abstract-figurative canvases.

The 64-page paperback, published by Karma in New York, reproduces drawings built from Williams' recurring cast of cartoonish, absurdist imagery, cracked eggs, distorted faces, and everyday objects rendered with a deadpan humor that undercuts their painterly complexity. Library of Congress cataloging places the drawings around 2016, and the book functions as a compact survey of a medium Williams treats as sketchbook and finished work at once.

Williams (b. 1978) is known for paintings that combine airbrush, digital printing, and hand-drawn marks into dense, layered compositions; Karma, which represents him, has published several volumes of his work, of which this drawing-focused book is among the more intimate.
notes: Karma, New York, 2017. Collects dry-marker drawings by painter Michael Williams (born 1978); Library of Congress cataloging dates the drawings to around 2016. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Archäologie, Beaux Arts, Ethnography, Théâtre-Vérité, Couleur Européenne, Couleur Soviétique, Couleur Chinoise, Varietes
description:
This catalogue accompanied an exhibition by the conceptual photographer Christopher Williams at the Contemporary Art Gallery in Vancouver, running January 13 to March 6, 2005.

Its unusually long title strings together the names of several bodies of work shown together, in a mix of English and French, a structure characteristic of Williams's practice of grouping images by category, source, or production process rather than by subject alone. The catalogue was curated by Claudia Beck and includes an essay by John Miller, and runs 45 pages.

Williams is a Los Angeles based artist whose photographs, often shot to commercial or archival specifications, examine the systems of image production, from advertising to state photography, that shape how photographs are made to look neutral. His exhibitions and catalogues, of which this is one, typically foreground the conditions of the photograph's making as much as its ostensible subject.
tags: Art, Photography, Contemporary Art, Exhibition Catalog
notes: Exhibition catalog for Christopher Williams's show at the Contemporary Art Gallery, Vancouver, January 13 to March 6, 2005, curated by Claudia Beck with an essay by John Miller. Diacritics in the title were stripped in the library's catalogue record (Archaologie Beaux Arts Ethnography Theatre-Verite) and have been restored here from bookseller and library listings; the final word appears as Varietes, without an accent, on the cover and in source listings alike. Booksellers list this record's page count as either 33 or 45; 45 is used here, from a library catalogue entry for this ISBN, and should be checked against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: The Man in the Crowd: The Uneasy Streets of Garry Winogrand
Chloe Wise
publisher: Division Gallery (Canada) and Galerie Sebastien Bertrand (Switzerland)
description:
Canadian artist Chloe Wise’s practice spans diverse media, including painting, sculpture, video and installation.

Foregrounding an interest in the history of portraiture, Wise examines the multiple channels that lead to the construction of a Self, paying particular attention to the interweaving of consumption and image making. With a wry sense of humour, she nods to canonical tableaux, like Manet’s Déjeuner Sur L’Herbe, exploring the shared projected desires built around food and the female body.

Meticulously hand painted casts of food serve as the base for the artist’s sculptural practice where strange assemblies, now frozen in sculpted plastic, toy with the presence and absence of unchangeability and perishability, fiction and reality. Advertising, fashion, taboo, multi-national brands—Wise looks to the consumptive habits built around these structures with parody and derision, underlying how the body is framed and becomes excessive in its manipulation of these sites.

title: 24 Tennis Court Drawings
description:
This book highlights a suite of twenty-four drawings by Jonas Wood depicting the color-saturated courts of various tennis tournaments as viewed by the artist on television in his studio.

Completed between 2016 and 2018, the works were first presented at Shane Campbell Gallery in Chicago and will be gifted to the Los Angeles County Museum of Art in 2025. The bilingual (English/Japanese) catalogue features a conversation with Wood that provides insight into the artist's process, as well as photographs of works in progress at the studio in Los Angeles.

title: Jonas Wood
contributors: Ian Alteveer (Essay), Helen Molesworth (Essay), Mark Grotjahn (Contributor)
description:
The first monograph devoted to Jonas Wood surveys the paintings that established him as one of the most closely watched figures in contemporary American painting.

Working from his own photographs, drawings and collages, Wood builds interiors, studio views, potted plants, and sports imagery into flattened, densely patterned compositions that compress perspective the way a collage does rather than a window onto space. The book, published in Phaidon's Contemporary Artists Series, brings together essays by curators Ian Alteveer and Helen Molesworth alongside a conversation with the painter Mark Grotjahn, situating Wood's paintings within the studio practice and working process behind them.

Wood emerged in the Los Angeles gallery scene in the 2000s and has since shown widely, including major presentations organized around the Karma and David Kordansky galleries and museum surveys; his wife, the ceramicist Shio Kusaka, is a frequent presence and subject in his domestic imagery. This survey remains the primary monographic reference on his work to date.
notes: Multiple self-titled Jonas Wood exhibition catalogs exist from Karma, Anton Kern Gallery and David Kordansky Gallery; this record is the Phaidon Contemporary Artists Series survey monograph (2019), the primary trade edition of the artist's most widely distributed self-titled book. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Westtexaspsychosculpture
description: This artist's book comprises photographs taken between 2008 and 2017 in the Marfa, West Texas area where Wool maintains a studio. The collection features 'found situations' including backyard debris, improvised storage, stray animals, and unusual structures that 'appear almost like sculpture for the split second of the open lens.' Signed by the artist.

title: East Broadway Breakdown
description: Black-and-white photographs taken in New York's Lower East Side. Designed by Hans Werner Holzwarth and Christopher Wool. A special edition version was also produced, limited to 160 copies, each including a different signed and numbered black-and-white photograph from the series. Signed by the artist.

title: can your monkey do the dog
description: Collaborative work between Josh Smith and Christopher Wool. The artists created together a series of pieces using digital imaging, with each artist alternately reworking the other's images. Signed by the artist.

title: Yard
description: This artist's book comprises photographs Christopher Wool made between 2008 and 2017 in the surroundings of Marfa in West Texas. Pictures of found situations: of backyard debris and improvised storage solutions, stray animals and strange constructions that once must have made sense but now appear undecipherable. Things set adrift and excerpts from the landscape that appear almost like sculpture for the split second of the open lens. Signed by the artist.

title: Road
description:
On first view, the photographic superimpositions in black and brown offer nothing to hold onto.

Their unruly surfaces lead into the depth, into fragments of motifs: backyards, dumped car tires, huge cable drums, dead tree stumps, rusty bed frames, or the wall of a shack with strange objects leaning against it. If, on second view, the eye manages to separate the different layers of reality meshed here, in the end the decipherable photographic images collapse again into painterly textures.

Swamp is the fourth artist's book from a series Wool has published with Holzwarth Publications: Road and Westtexaspsychosculpture collected photos of bumpy roads or sculpture-like found objects in Texan surroundings then, in Yard from 2018, the artist clearly superimposed two different realities. Now Swamp is another step in the process, developing new pictures through processing and reproduction, for which the original photographic gaze acts as just the basic layer. Signed by the artist.

title: Psychopts
description: Collaborative work between writer/musician Richard Hell and artist Christopher Wool. Paperback format with BW illustrations. Signed by the artist.

title: See Stop Run
description:
Published on the occasion of Christopher Wool: See Stop Run at 101 Greenwich Street, New York.

Organized by the artist with curator Anne Pontégnie, the survey exhibition was presented on the unoccupied nineteenth floor of a building in Manhattan's Financial District in spring and summer 2024 and drew more than 12,500 visitors. Featuring seventy-five works by Wool from the past decade, it employed the vacant 18,000-square-foot space, and the cityscape beyond, to contextualize and extend the artist's aesthetic.

Taking the form of an expanded artist's book, the catalogue gathers nearly three hundred candid and evocative color and black-and-white photographs of the installation taken by dozens of artists, friends, and Instagram users to reflect on the ways in which exhibitions are now documented and their contents reproduced and disseminated. It also includes an extensive interview between Wool and Pontégnie that situates the project within the artist's three-decades-long use of photography and installation. Distributed by D.A.P./Distributed Art Publishers, New York. Printed by Trifolio, Verona, Italy. Signed by the artist.

title: Bad Rabbit
description: The artist explores pieces of fencing wire discovered in Marfa, Texas, through black-and-white digitally treated photographs. These found objects served as inspiration for sculptural works cast in bronze and steel. According to the New York Times, the book "sharply elucidates the now considerable arc of Wool's engagement with photography for its own sake and for catalyzing the rest of his work." Signed by the artist.

title: Selected Works 1970-2015
contributors: WINER, Helene, HAINLEY, Bruce, SILLARS, Laurence
description:
The first major publication of B. Wurtz’s work, B. Wurtz: Selected Works 1970–2015 is published on the occasion of a comprehensive survey exhibition at the Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art, Gateshead, UK in 2015 and La Casa Encendida, Madrid.

For more than 40 years, B. Wurtz has collected common, domestic objects—carrier bags, aluminium roasting trays, buttons, shoelaces—and repurposed them into meticulously formal constructions that are balanced, fragile, yet sometimes discordant. His raw material is the stuff we constantly use and constantly overlook things that connect to life in its most everyday sense.

Bringing elegance to the mundane and revealing a beauty in materials that would otherwise be so easily disposed of, Wurtz’s sculpture maintains an adherence to classical forms and a play with art history, all the while responding to three fundamental needs outlined early in the artist’s career: sleeping, eating and keeping warm.

title: Gengetsu
description:
Takemi Yabuki's Gengetsu is a portrait project built on withholding: each subject, a stranger approached on the street and asked to pose, appears with part of their face or body cut from view.

Yabuki has described the method as a study of visibility and invisibility, of how much a photograph should be allowed to reveal. "You can see too much in photography," he has written of the series. "It is dangerous to be exposed to too much. This is just the right amount of expression to show reality." The book, published by Super Labo in 2015 as a 110-page hardcover with 52 images, was issued as a signed and numbered edition of 500 and was shown as an exhibition at Ai Kowada Gallery, Tokyo, the same year.

Yabuki (b. 1982) works primarily as a commercial photographer; Gengetsu, reviewed by curator Fumiko Nakamura of the Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art as an image that seems to "jump out" of the book despite showing only a figure covered in black spots, is among his best-known independent series.
notes: Signed and numbered, from an edition of 500. Published alongside the Gengetsu exhibition at Ai Kowada Gallery, Tokyo. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Berlin / Deep in Thought
description:
Berlin / Deep in Thought is Toshitsugu Yamawaki's black-and-white meditation on the city of Berlin, made as a study of the accumulated historical and political weight held in a single place.

Published by the artist's own imprint, Studio a la page, in 2014, the 492-page hardcover was issued in a numbered edition of 200 copies. In his artist's statement Yamawaki describes photographing Berlin's streets as an encounter with layered time, past, present and future seeming to exist together in the same moment, and describes the book as a collection of prints alongside his own analysis and considerations of that feeling, with the double title framing the city as a subject for contemplating what persists across its history.

Yamawaki (born Tokyo, 1956) worked as an art director in advertising before turning to photography and painting full-time in 2000; he later won second prize at the Kassel PhotoBookFestival's Photobook Award for his book Dual I & II. Berlin / Deep in Thought continues that body of work's interest in extended, book-length visual essays produced through his own studio.
notes: No ISBN was assigned to this self-published edition. Page count, dimensions and edition size come from josefchladek.com's catalogue record; dimensions are marked approximate there. Cover image is a Le Plac'Art Photo bookshop listing photograph and carries their site watermark. Numbered edition of 200 copies. Cover to be photographed: the only reproduction traced carries a bookseller watermark. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Dimension of Vision
edition_printrun: First edition, 2011; issued with variant covers printed by the photographer
description:
Dimension of Vision is Toshitsugu Yamawaki's first photobook, a 120-page collection built from roughly 2,000 images the artist shot between 2008 and 2011.

The book compiles 109 photographs, reworked in the months after the Great East Japan Earthquake of March 11, 2011, into three episodes: "Abstract," high-contrast black-and-white images of water surfaces and sparks; "Translation," color photographs made near U.S. military bases in Fussa and Yokosuka, Japan, as well as in New York and Barcelona; and "Calm," closing with a single black-and-white photograph of the sea, taken in Ibaraki on March 11, 2011. Yamawaki has described the title's sense of "dimension" as a return to first principles of how an image is read, stripping elements back to draw out latent meaning. Self-published through his own Studio A La Page, Tokyo, in 2011, softbound, with variant covers printed by the photographer; text in Japanese.

Yamawaki, born in Tokyo in 1956, worked as an advertising art director before founding Studio A La Page and turning to photography around 2000. His later book Dual I & II (2013) won second prize at the Kassel PHOTOBOOKFESTIVAL Photobook Award.
notes: Self-published first edition, 2011, with variant covers printed by the photographer; no ISBN was assigned to this title. Cover to be photographed: the only reproduction traced carries a bookseller watermark. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: 1 Wall Photography 02/ Indication
description: Publication from Daisuke Yokota's solo show, Grand Prix winner in the photography category at the 2nd "1 Wall" open call exhibition. On display are dream-like works depicting forest landscapes that seem to conceal something within.

title: Vertigo
description:
Daisuke Yokota's Vertigo is a photobook built around a bodily sensation rather than a place or subject: the disorientation of being off balance.

Across 96 hardcover pages, more than ninety black-and-white photographs, including two foldouts, move through close-up and aerial views processed with the grain, chemical staining, and re-photography Yokota is known for, evoking reversed sleep cycles, jet lag, and fragmented memory rather than depicting them directly. Edited by Yokota with Kohei Oyama and designed by Goshi Uhira, the book was published in Tokyo in 2014 as the first title from the imprint Newfave, in an edition of 500 copies, and was shortlisted for the Paris Photo–Aperture Foundation PhotoBook of the Year award.

Yokota (b. 1983) works across an unusually large and fast-moving bibliography of self-published and small-press books, most made by physically degrading his negatives and prints; Vertigo is an early example of that process applied to a single, sustained physical sensation rather than a specific place, as in later books like Site or Matter.
notes: Newfave, Tokyo, 2014, first title from the imprint. Edited by Daisuke Yokota with Kohei Oyama, designed by Goshi Uhira. Edition of 500 copies. Shortlisted for the Paris Photo-Aperture Foundation PhotoBook of the Year award. No ISBN found; cover to be photographed, as the only image traced carries a watermark. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

Small Paintings 1993-2004
description:
Small Paintings 1993-2004 gathers a decade of Lisa Yuskavage's smaller-format paintings, in which candy-colored light and cartoonishly exaggerated female bodies push figurative painting toward the territory of pin-up and pornographic imagery, then unsettle it from within.

The book reproduces the paintings largely without the mediating context of a gallery installation, letting the recurring cast of nude and semi-nude figures accumulate across the decade covered. It includes an essay and explanatory diagrams by the filmmaker Tamara Jenkins, and was published by Harry N. Abrams in New York in 2004.

Yuskavage is an American painter whose work, since the early 1990s, has used exaggerated, doll-like female figures to interrogate desire, shame, and the history of painting's own objectification of women. Small Paintings 1993-2004 sits within a substantial body of monographs and exhibition catalogues devoted to her painting.
tags: Art, Painting, Contemporary Art, Women Artists
notes: Essay and diagrams by Tamara Jenkins. Whether this volume was published to accompany a specific exhibition could not be confirmed this session; dimensions are not confirmed and should be checked against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: Lisa Yuskavage
contributors: Ariel Levy (Essay), Barry Schwabsky (Essay), Lena Dunham (Essay), Jason Schmidt (Photographer)
description:
Published in Phaidon's Contemporary Artists Series, this monograph presents the fullest survey to date of Lisa Yuskavage's paintings, tracking the arc of a body of work that has unsettled and reshaped expectations of figurative painting since the 1990s.

Yuskavage's paintings render female figures in lurid, theatrical color and exaggerated proportion, staging scenes that move between parody, tenderness and discomfort in equal measure. The book gathers reproductions of paintings across her career alongside essays by the journalist Ariel Levy, the critic Barry Schwabsky and the writer and filmmaker Lena Dunham, with studio photography by Jason Schmidt documenting Yuskavage's working process.

Yuskavage studied at Tyler School of Art and Yale, and emerged alongside painters like John Currin in the 1990s revival of figurative painting that treated art-historical technique as a vehicle for provocation. She has shown extensively with David Zwirner and been the subject of museum surveys internationally; this volume joins the Institute of Contemporary Art, Philadelphia's 2000 exhibition catalogue and Abrams's 2004 Small Paintings 1993-2004 as one of several monographic treatments of her work, positioned as the current standard trade survey.
notes: Multiple self-titled Lisa Yuskavage monographs exist, including the Institute of Contemporary Art, Philadelphia's 2000 exhibition catalogue (Claudia Gould, Katy Siegel) and Abrams's 2004 Small Paintings 1993-2004, catalogued separately in this collection. This record identifies the Phaidon Contemporary Artists Series edition (essays by Ariel Levy, Barry Schwabsky and Lena Dunham, photography by Jason Schmidt) as the distinct publication held under this entry. Edition to be verified against the copy. Summer archiving 2026; catalogued 2026-08-28.

title: NYC RIP
description:
In 1980, Miron Zownir emigrated to the USA, where he lived for the next fifteen years first in New York, then in Los Angeles, and Pittsburgh.

In New York, back then arguably the world's most fascinating and permissive metropolis, Zownir's peculiar approach to cover the city's multiple layered day-to-day lunacy was quickly recognised by the local scene as the TEUTONIC PHENOMENOGRAPHER (Village Voice).

Shot in moody, expressionistic b/w, Zownir's pictures from that period give a penetrating insight to inner-city sub-cultural spheres, which, in their original local context, have since perished in the boom of the 90s. His lens captured the untamed lust at the gay-parties, just shortly before Aids massively claimed its victims the futile protest of artists and offbeat performers

title: Rythm Mastr: This Is How It Begins
description:
"Rythm Mastr" is a comic series created by Kerry James Marshall, developed from 1999 to the present in response to the historical absence of black characters in comics.

Set in the community surrounding Marshall's Chicago studio, the narrative is rooted in reality but incorporates elements of fantasy, created using India ink drawings. The series debuted at the 1999/2000 Carnegie International, published as single illustrated panels in the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's magazine for eight weeks. Marshall papered the Carnegie Museum's display windows with 20 segments printed on newsprint and installed it in the museum's Treasure Room to explore how value is assigned to objects. Copies were distributed to the public for a nominal fee to ensure wide access. The story features an old man named Rythm Mastr and his young protégé, Farell. Meeting in a museum of ancient Egyptian art, Rythm Mastr teaches Farell traditional African drumming that brings ancient African and Egyptian statues to life. These animated statues possess superhuman powers derived from the seven gods of the Yoruba pantheon. The narrative addresses contemporary issues, including the spike in violence in 1990s Chicago and the demolition of high-rise public housing on the city's South Side. Over the years, the series has evolved through various formats. In 2003, it was featured as a daily comic strip in "One True Thing: Meditations on a Black Aesthetics" at MCA Chicago.

In 2008, it was presented at the Wexner Center at Ohio State University with puppets inspired by traditional Japanese Bunraku puppetry, including live performances with jazz drummer Kahil El'Zabar. The series appeared in Issue 14 of Esopus magazine in 2010. From 2015 to 2017, it was included in light-box displays in "Mastry," Marshall's 30-year retrospective, and inspired "Above the Line," a hand-painted mural on New York's High Line from 2015 to 2016. Marshall's work was influenced by The Black Panther comic he encountered at ten years old. His goal was to create black superheroes in a context where they matter, with a Homeric epic structure achieving cultural impact similar to Star Wars. His long-term ambition is to diversify the art historical canon with more images of black people in museums. Marshall envisions the series as a graphic novel and feature animated film. This comprehensive volume, edited by Michele Robecchi (Rizzoli Electa, 2025), represents the most complete documentation of the character, its genesis, and evolution over two decades, featuring Marshall's sophisticated debates about history, philosophy, and politics in vernacular Black English, creating an empowering blend of science fiction and Afrofuturism.

title: Stay away from nothing
contributors: James Hoff (Managing Editor), Joseph Logan (Designer), Allison Dubinsky (Copy Editor), Andrew Durbin (Afterword)
description:
This publication explores the relationship between artists Paul Thek and Peter Hujar through correspondence and photography spanning 1956-1975.

The collection includes over fifty letters and postcards, along with drawings and ephemera, documenting their travels, creative work, and personal connection across locations including Coral Gables, Philadelphia, Rome, Italy, and Fire Island. Peter Hujar's photographs capture Thek in various settings, including iconic images from the Palermo catacombs and studio portraits during the creation of "The Tomb," alongside previously unpublished candid shots.
tags: 1960s-1970s, American Artists, Artist Correspondence, New York Art, Photography, Queer Culture, Art

title: Goya: The Disasters of War
description:
"The Disasters of War", eighty invented and etched plates by Francisco de Goya.

In 1808, at the end of the first siege of Saragossa by Napoleon's troops, Francisco de Goya was invited with a number of other artists to visit the devastated city and arouse the people's patriotic fervour through a series of propaganda pictures and prints. Far from the glorification that had been entrusted to him, what Goya depicted was a universal condemnation of violence. Terribly contemporary, these images continue to assail us more than two hundred years later. To the horrors he saw in Saragossa, Goya added scenes of the famine he witnessed in Madrid and a series of symbolic prints on the post-war period that he entitled "Emphatic Caprices", in which he showed the loss of the constitutional ideals with the return of absolutism. The three blocks - War, Famine and Emphatic Caprices - constitute The Disasters of War, a work which Goya completed in 1820 but whose publication was delayed owing to its critical nature until 1863, 35 years after his death.

Appearing beneath each figure is a legend or caption, short text - sometimes just one word - which Goya included with expressive precision. The set, numbered by the artist himself, cries out to us with a moving narrative that was unusual for the time in making the denunciation of war its principal theme. The Aragonese artist can thus also be regarded as a pioneer of protest art. The Disasters of War, then, is a book of images for reading. Profoundly humanist, this reading is especially fitting in the context of today's flow of information, marked by the impact of the visual message and of brief texts. It begins with a prelude, "Sad forebodings of what is to befall", and culminates in an open ending: "Truth is dead" "Will she rise again?" That question leaves the door open to hope. Based on the original 1863 edition, this clothbound book faithfully reproduces the first edition of the complete set of 80 works: 1-47 WAR, 48-64 FAMINE, 65-80 EMPHATIC CAPRICES.
tags: Etchings, Historical, La Fábrica, Political Art, Spanish Art, War, disaster, Printmaking

title: Leo Villareal: Coding Light
contributors: Molly Donovan, Annie Dell'Aria, Sarah Sze
description:
An expansive monograph of work by acclaimed contemporary artist Leo Villareal, known for his monumental installations employing light and computer technology.

Transforming pixels using the zeroes and ones of binary code into dazzling displays of light, Mexican-American artist Leo Villareal creates abstract installations that are icons of public art. Employing artist-created code and custom software, his innovative practice explores chance, rules, and the underlying structure of systems.

Features more than 30 works ranging in scale – from exhibitions and immersive architectural commissions like Cosmos at Cornell University, to urban-scale artworks such as his seminal work, Illuminated River, which joins nine central-London bridges along the River Thames in London. Includes 350 illustrations spanning over two decades of the artist's career.
tags: Art Book, Contemporary Art, Digital Art, Installation Art, Light Art, Monacelli, Public Art, Art

title: David Wojnarowicz: Arthur Rimbaud in New York
contributors: Nicholas Martin, Craig Dworkin, Marguerite Van Cook, Phillip Aarons
description:
In 1978 and 1979, David Wojnarowicz took a series of photographs of a man wearing a paper mask bearing the visage of Arthur Rimbaud, the French poet equally known for his fervid verse and dramatic life.

Rimbaud was the instantiation, and perhaps the inventor, of the idea of the young gay hustler of genius. This volume features an introductory essay by Antonio Sergio Bessa contextualizing the series within a foundation of other works across literature, photography and performance. Nicholas Martin explores Wojnarowicz's practice in the context of the rise of the punk movement in downtown Manhattan in the late 1970s. Craig Dworkin explores Rimbaud's years as a runaway youth in Paris during the Commune. Includes an interview with photographer Allen Frame. Features 150 color images.

title: David Bowie Is (Museum of Contemporary Art, Chicago: Exhibition Catalogues)   (2 copies)
description:
This companion piece to an exhibition at London's Victoria and Albert Museum explores the iconography, fashion, and music of pop icon David Bowie.

Drawn to rock'n'roll as a rebellion against his suburban London upbringing, Bowie's career has been one of constant reinvention and innovation. As a musician and composer, his influences are wide ranging: he borrows as much from contemporaries such as The Rolling Stones and German synthesizer bands Neu! and Kraftwerk as from composers Kurt Weill and frequent collaborator Brian Eno. He is also heavily influenced by broader culture, notably adopting the cut up method often employed by William Burroughs, while being strongly influenced by the video work of Andy Warhol.

Beyond music, however, Bowie cultivated a constantly shifting sense of style, most famously as his glam rock, alien alter-ego Ziggy Stardust. His various costumes were Dadaist in impulse and Surrealist in conception and execution. Particularly striking, however, was the cobweb body-suit he wore for The 1980 Floor Show, which features two glitter covered mannequin hands that seem to be fondling his chest as a kind of camp provocation. Indeed, as Camille Paglia notes, Bowie came to embody the shaman and prophet who crossed into forbidden sexual terrain. (Apr.)

title: Dust & Grooves: Adventures in Record Collecting
description:
Compelling photographic essays from photographer Eilon Paz are paired with in-depth and insightful interviews to illustrate what motivates these collectors to keep digging for more records.

The reader gets an up close and personal look at a variety of well-known vinyl champions, including Gilles Peterson and King Britt, as well as a glimpse into the collections of known and unknown DJs, producers, record dealers, and everyday enthusiasts. Driven by his love for vinyl records, Paz takes us on a five-year journey unearthing the very soul of the vinyl community.
tags: Music, Photography, Pop Culture, Punk, Rock

title: Factory Records: The Complete Graphic Album by Matthew Robertson
description:
A creative juggernaut of the post-punk era, Factory Records was the catalyst behind the U.K. music explosion of the late '70s through the '90s with groups like Joy Division (soon to be the subject of an Anton Corbijn movie), New Order, and Happy Mondays leading the New Wave.

At Factory, musicians and designers commingled creatively, with innovators such as Peter Saville, Den Kelly, Mark Farrow, 8VO, and Barbara Kruger elevating album covers to a new art form. The label broke further ground when it opened its own disco, the legendary Hacienda.

Factory Records is the ultimate and only collection of Factory's complete graphic output, including every single piece it produced: extremely rare record sleeves, club flyers, and posters all gathered together for the first time. A must for collectors and enthusiasts, Matthew Robertson's meticulous compilation of underground ephemera is poised to introduce a new generation of music and design fans to the creative genius of Factory.
tags: Music, Photography, Pop Culture, Punk, Rock

description: Raw, brazen and totally intense, Fucked Up + Photocopied is a collection of frenetic flyers produced for the American punk scene between 1977 and 1985. Many were created by the musicians themselves and demonstrate the emphasis within the punk scene on individuality and the manic urge of its members to create things new.
