title: Joy Division by Kevin Cummins, Bernard Sumner   (Three Copies, one inscribed, one signed, one new)
description:
The definitive look at one of the most iconic rock bands of all time.

Joy Division pioneered a genre of music and defined the look and sound of the post-punk era, and thirty years after the suicide of their lead singer Ian Curtis, they remain one of the most influential rock bands to have come out of England. Between their infamous live performances and two studio albums in the late 1970s, Joy Division set the Manchester scene alight, established Factory Records as the most influential label in pop music, and recorded some of the most enduring songs of the era.

Kevin Cummins began his career just as the band formed, and for the few short years of their career was given closer access to them than any other photographer. Joy Division collects more than two hundred of his images of the band—sensitive photographs that capture their quiet introspection offstage, their close relationships as bandmates, and Curtis’s legendary energy in live performances—and supplements the iconic images with concert tickets, unreleased record sleeves, fan club badges, Factory Records flyers, and other rare ephemera. This book is the most definitive and heavily illustrated celebration of the band ever produced.
tags: Music, Photography, Pop Culture, Punk, Rock

title: Karlheinz Weinberger - Vol 1 Halbstarke P
description:
In 1958, Zürich photographer Karlheinz Weinberger first captured the likeness of Halbstarke (rebel) Jimmy Oechslin, an artistic moment which marks the genesis of this collection of images focused on young Swiss teenagers.

That particular photographic encounter triggered Weinbergers life-long fascination with outsiders and nonconformists in the otherwise staid environment of Switzerland. The photographs presented in this first of several volumes about his work offer a rare glimpse into a bygone world that seems almost cute and quaint from a contemporary perspective, but make no mistake: just dressing in jeans and hanging chains around ones neck was a statement as loud as blasting music by Buddy Holly on a quiet Swiss Sunday afternoon.
tags: Music, Photography, Pop Culture, Punk, Rock

title: New Order by Kevin Cummins    (signed)
description:
A definitive collection of photographs of the legendary and influential band New Order.

New Order remains one of the most popular bands of the last half century. Founded in the dying years of punk and disco, and combining elements of post-punk, new wave, and electronic dance music, New Order was responsible for some of the biggest hits of the era and is one of few bands to have achieved mainstream success while retaining cult status. Having been the most trusted photographer of Joy Division in the 1970s, Kevin Cummins was uniquely placed to document the rise and fall of New Order, from their formation in 1980 to their split in 1993.

From underground beginnings as the flagship group of Factory Records in Manchester to grandstand tours around Europe and America, Cummins captured the band in every light, from the intimacy of the studio to the frenetic energy of live performance. Collected here for the first time are more than a hundred photographs reflecting over a decade of New Order. Prefaced by a selection of rarely seen ephemera, conversations with the band members, and an introduction from Douglas Coupland, this is a stunning celebration of a band whose influence on music and fashion is still palpable today.
tags: Music, Photography, Pop Culture, Punk, Rock

title: No Wave: Post-Punk. Underground. New York. 1976-1980
description:
Art and music come together in this oral account of Manhattan's mid-1970s No Wave music scene.

Moore, a founding member of the band Sonic Youth, and Coley, a music writer and editor, identify the likes of Teenage Jesus and the Jerks, DNA, Contortions and Mars as the core bands that built No Wave. Shedding light on the personal relationships of these close-knit bands, the surprisingly reserved volume-graced with exquisite black-and-white photos with occasional splashes of poster-art color-also looks at how the devastated state of the city influenced their sound and performances: As everything's collapsing... the music became the rebellion, says Teenage Jesus's Lydia Lunch in her scowling, astute foreword.

Music sometimes described as a car crash gets heartfelt and intelligent commentary from the likes of DNA's Ikue Mori: it wasn't about technique it was more about new ideas and inspiration. The authors' personal interviews with the movement's other pioneers elicit raw, honest hindsight along with revealing photographs, this volume takes readers straight into the heart of this zeitgeist.
tags: Music, New York City, Photography, Pop Culture, Punk, Rock

title: Oh So Pretty: Punk in Print 1976-19801980
description:
Oh So Pretty: Punk in Print 1976-80 is an unrivalled collection of visually striking ephemera from Britain’s punk subculture.

It presents 500 artefacts - 'zines,' gig posters, flyers, and badges - from well-known and obscure musical acts, designers, venues, and related political groups. While punk was first and foremost a music phenomenon, it reflected a DIY spirit and instantly recognizable aesthetic that was as raw and strident and irrepressible as the music. As disposable as the items in this book once were, together they tell a story about music, history, class, and art, and document a seismic shift in society and visual culture.
tags: Art Book, Music, Photography, Pop Culture, Punk, Rock

title: Panic Attack!: Art in the Punk Years
description:
Punk is most commonly associated with music, fashion and graphics, but its rebellious and iconoclastic spirit also found expression in the visual arts.

Panic Attack! reveals the vibrant art scene that exploded in Britain and the United States between 1974 and 1984, when visual artists shared some of the radical attitudes and aesthetics of punk and post-punk musicians and designers.Featuring essays by both British and American commentators, a detailed chronology of the art and music scenes of the time and stunning reproductions of works by over thirty leading artists, Panic Attack! is an account of one of the most exciting periods in modern art.
tags: Music, Photography, Pop Culture, Punk, Rock

title: Patti Smith 1969-1976
description:
Before Patti Smith became a rock star, she loved to pose as one for her friend, the photographer Judy Linn.

These 100 grainy, gritty, black and white photographs show Smith working, playing, primping in the clutter of her apartment surrounded by erstwhile lovers, the artist Robert Mapplethorpe and playwright Sam Shepard. They brim with bright light and the obvious affection between photographer and subject. Linn, a photography professor at Vassar College whose work is now collected in the Whitney Museum and elsewhere, recalls a summer spent poring over Alfred Stieglitz's work, including the portraits of his wife Georgia O'Keefe (I thought I could memorize it and crack its grammar).

She describes learning from the visual logic and illogical brilliance of her own photos, and it's easy to see why. The photographs vary in quality, but at their best they capture Mapplethorpe and Smith's youth and earnestness, their wildness and vulnerability. Take the nudes of Smith, where a dark necktie and belt bisect and play against her long, pale body. Here is Smith's acclaimed 2010 memoir, Just Kids, come to life: the shrines to Bob Dylan, the dressup. The photos strike the same wistful note as Smith writes in her afterword: once upon a time, we were young and beautiful and anyone we imagined we could be. (Mar.)
tags: Music, Photography, Pop Culture, Punk, Rock

title: Punk 365 (365 Series)
description:
Thirty-plus years ago a dark rumble of noise gurgled up from the Lower East Side of New York City, made its way across the Atlantic to Great Britain, zigzagged back over the pond to the West Coast, and exploded.

Its name—Punk. InPunk 365, the most provocative photography documenting the performances, the looks, and the attitude has been gathered together, revealing reverberations that continue to shake up the status quo. Here we see it all: Pre-punk pioneers, the Stooges, the New York Dolls, the MC5. New York’s harbingers of change, the Ramones, Patti Smith, Richard Hell & the Voidoids. London’s anarchists, the Sex Pistols, the Clash, the Slits.

The West Coast’s anti-Beach Boys, X, the Germs . . .the list goes on. By the mid-1980s, from the Replacements to Bad Brains, the sound transmogrified into everything from garage punk to hardcore. Punk 365 has them all, including more than 300 different artists by the most talented photographers who captured the scene, including Bob Gruen, Roberta Bayley, Jill Furmanovsky, Stephanie Chernikowski, Godlis, Janette Beckman, and more.

title: Punk: Chaos to Couture
description: Nothing on King's Road in 1977--or the Bowery in 1975, for that matter--could compete with the clothes in this book for aggressivness, poetry, and sheer devotion to hardware. But Punk also captures the discomfort of admiring DIY fashion deracinated from social context: Locked so far away from the beating heart of punk, the clothes, no matter how dramatic, are soulless. --Sarah Leonard

title: Rock Seen - Bob Gruen
description:
For 40 years, Bob Gruen’s name has been synonymous with rock and roll.

From taking early photos on tour with Ike and Tina Turner, to capturing the early CBGB/Max’s Kansas City scene to covering current stadium rockers such as Green Day, Gruen has always been at the right place at the right time—and he’s always gotten the shot.

In this lavish monograph, Gruen has curated his favorite photographs from his career, with intimate captions and behind-the-scenes anecdotes. Featuring such illustrious acts as the Clash, Led Zeppelin, the Rolling Stones, Sex Pistols, Ramones, and more, and including an introduction by the legendary Debbie Harry of Blondie, this collection is a must-have for all fans of rock and roll.

title: Showboat: Punk/Sex/Bodies
description:
Showboat: Punk/Sex/Bodies explores sex in punk and punk in sex.

Punk is often thought of as an almost asexual movement, in part because of its charged aversion to romance (see Johnny Rotten’s notorious description of love as “2 minutes and 52 seconds of squelching noises”). Yet, its raw street sound triggered an exuberant, primal physical release among its youthful followers. For many punks, sex was used as a necessary shock tactic against the orthodoxies that held sway in conservative 1970s Britain. The status of punk as a radical subculture meant that it could freely explore sex without mainstream censorship and this ability to openly express sex and sexuality provided punk with so much of its essential rawness and immediacy.

Beginning in 1972 and spanning right up to the present day, Showboat provides a chronological survey of the relationship between punk and sex as seen through original posters, flyers, record covers, photographs and ephemera drawn from the editor’s punk archive, The Mott Collection. Alongside written contributions from Julie Burchill, Paul Cook, Vivien Goldman, Eve Libertine, Bruce LaBruce, Amos Poe, Richard Prince and Will Self among many others. Designed by Jamie Andrew Reid

title: Slash: A Punk Magazine from Los Angeles: 1977-1980
description:
The legendary punk and new wave alternative weekly magazine Slash was founded in Los Angeles in 1977 by Steve Samiof, and published a total of 29 print issues before its demise in 1980 (though it had a second life as the punk label Slash Records, which was eventually bought by Warner Bros. Records in 1999).

In its brief run, Slash defined the punk subculture in Los Angeles and beyond with the comic strip Jimbo by Gary Panter and photographs by Melanie Nissen, the cofounding publisher and longtime photo editor. Writing by Jeffrey Lee Pierce, Chris D., Pleasant Gehman and Claude “Kickboy Face” Bessy explored reggae, blues and rockabilly in addition to punk and new wave.Slash diagnosed the nascent punk scene’s challenge to the music industry and established its own oppositional voice in the editorial of its very first issue, staking a position against disco, Elvis and concept albums, and declaring: “Enough is enough, partner! About time we squeezed the pus out and sent the filthy rich old farts of rock ’n’ roll to retirement homes in Florida where they belong.”Slash: A Punk Magazine From Los Angeles, 1977–80 pays homage to the magazine’s legacy with facsimile reproductions of every cover from the publication’s run and reprints of some of the magazine’s best articles and interviews.

These are interspersed with new essays, reportage and oral histories from Exene Cervenka, KK Barrett, Gary Panter, Vivien Goldman, Richard Meltzer, Cali Thornhill DeWitt, Chris D., Bryan Ray Turcotte, Chris Morris, Ann Summa and Allan MacDowell, among others, telling the story of this critical chapter in the history of American media.

title: The Beautiful & The Damned: Punk Photographs by Ann Summa
description:
When photographer Ann Summa arrived in Los Angeles in 1978, the city's punk scene was still fresh, diverse, smart, utterly original-and fertile territory for a young photographer.

The Beautiful & the Damned is a collection of her portraits of the musicians, artists and fans who made Los Angeles such a crucial part of the history of punk. Taken between 1978 and 1984, the images mostly revolve around L.A.'s first punk generation, and include portraits of the Germs, the Screamers, X, the Cramps and the Gun Club, among many others. From there, the book expands its scope to accommodate the cross-pollination that took place between L.A.'s punk scene and the fine art community, (at the time, the audience for avant-garde artists such as the Kipper Kids, Johanna Went and Laurie Anderson was primarily drawn from the underground music scene), and the two other cities central to the birth of punk, London and New York.

Photographed during their first U.S. tours are U.K. groups the Clash, Magazine, the Fall, the Slits, Bow Wow Wow and the Pretenders, among others. Visiting dignitaries from New York include Television, James Chance, Lydia Lunch and Talking Heads. Also included are portraits of artists who served as an inspiration to L.A. punks-Captain Beefheart, Iggy Pop and David Bowie, among others-plus candid shots of unidentified audience members. Edited and with an introduction by Kristine McKenna, The Beautiful & The Damned includes 95 previously unpublished images.

title: The Hollow of the Hand by PJ Harvey
description: Between 2011 and 2014 PJ Harvey and Seamus Murphy set out on a series of journeys together to Kosovo, Afghanistan, and Washington, D.C.. Harvey collected words, Murphy collected pictures, and together they created an extraordinary chronicle of our life and times. The Hollow of the Hand marks the first publication of Harvey's powerful poetry, in conversation with Murphy's indelible images. It is a landmark project and will be published internationally in autumn 2015.

title: Touch Me I'm Sick
description:
Poised at the epicenter of an explosive underground scene, photographer Charles Peterson witnessed the birth of a brash new era of music that grabbed the world by its throat and refused to let go.

Grunge, the bastard child of 60s garage and 70s punk, revived the original, gritty spirit of rock and roll: rebellion ain’t pretty, but it sure is fun. Featuring ninety-two photographs—eighty of them never-before-published—spanning sixteen years, Touch Me I’m Sick, Peterson’s third monograph, documents the raw power of live performances by the soon-to-be-famous artists and their dedicated fans. Yet Peterson’s photographs don’t rely on the cult of celebrity to tell this compelling tale of angst, anxiety, and acoustics. Rather, they capture the cathartic ritual between musician and fan played out in seedy clubs reeking of sweat and stale beer. Bored, alienated youth with nothing better to do than bash their instruments and mosh their bodies in a barrage of sound, song, and furious energy are captured through Peterson’s signature style of wide-angle intimacy, swirling lights, and strange sense of grace.

Peterson creates timeless, artistic imagery out of this swiftly passing frenzy, and shatters the godhead of the rock star, revealing the band and audience as co-conspirators in rock’s latest, greatest revival. Featuring photographs of Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Sleater-Kinney, Mudhoney, Sonic Youth, L7, Hole, and Black Flag, among others, as well as excerpts from Your Flesh, Flipside, Melody Maker, B-Sides, Swellsville, and Chemical Imbalance, Touch Me I’m Sick is the perfect mix of art and journalism for music purists and connoisseurs. “And you know what? I think other photographers secretly want to be like Charles and Charles secretly wants to be like other photographers. And it’s a hard call—would you rather have that street cred, punk rock hipness, and respect from all the cool bands, or industry suave that gets major magazine editors and record exec dorks to fly you all over the world for photo shoots and pay you outrageous amounts of money?”

description:
The ultimate compendium of counterculture press in the United States and the Netherlands during the heady decades of the 1960s and 70s, this volume is the definition of sex, drugs, and rock n roll.

From underground pornography, free love, anti-establishment anarchism, and Provo, to anti-war protests, spiritual empowerment, the Black Panthers, and womens liberation, its all here. Page after page of magazine covers, articles, advertisements, and clippings encapsulate the era when academia revolted, gays marched in the streets, and hippies wondered if Jesus got high, too. title: You Should Have Heard Just What I Seen
description:
Throughout the heady years of New York's 1960s and 70s music scenes, James Hamilton was on hand to observe and photograph some of the most significant bands, musicians and performances of the twentieth century.

Serving as staff photographer for the Village Voice and Crawdaddy!, Hamilton photographed such musicians as James Brown, Captain Beefheart, Ornette Coleman, Creedence Clearwater Revival, Crosby, Stills, Nash and Young, the Grateful Dead, John Fahey, Mick Jagger, Jethro Tull, Elvin Jones, the Kinks, Madonna, Charlie Mingus, Joni Mitchell, the Ramones, Gil Scott-Heron, Patti Smith, Sun Ra, Tom Verlaine and Stevie Wonder. In You Should Have Heard Just What I Seen, Hamilton opens up his archives for the first time, revealing across 300 pages a trove of previously unpublished black-and-white photographs--portraits, snapshots, sketches, contact sheets--of some of the most recognizable faces in music.

Influential for several generations of budding photographers raised on his photographs, the work of James Hamilton is at last collected in this revelatory volume. As a young man in the late 1960s, James Hamilton met the legendary photographers Diane Arbus and Eugene Smith, and was inspired by them to document the changing skyline of New York City. As staff photographer for Harper's Bazaar and the Village Voice, Hamilton recorded the fashion shows, events, protests and riots, happenings, concerts, poetry readings and art openings of that era, and throughout the 1970s, his photographs of musicians and celebrities began to appear in the pages of Crawdaddy! magazine. Later Hamilton joined The New York Observer and began working with filmmakers George Romero, Francis Ford Coppola, Wes Anderson, Bill Paxton and Noah Baumbach as on-set photographer.
tags: Music, Photography, Pop Culture, Punk, Rock

title: Sarah Sze: Paintings
contributors: Mark Godfrey, Tina Pang, Madeleine Grynsztejn
description:
The first and only monograph to give a comprehensive examination of acclaimed American artist Sarah Sze's painting practice.

Since the late 1990s, Sarah Sze has developed a signature visual language that challenges the static nature of art with a dynamic body of work spanning sculpture, painting, drawing, printmaking, video and installation. In recent years, Sze has returned to painting, the medium in which she was first trained. Comprising constellations of painted and collaged elements, her expansive abstract landscapes explore a visual world that is constantly evolving, degrading, and generating new ways of seeing.

Her paintings are held in the permanent collections of prominent institutions and museums worldwide. The book includes two essays by Mark Godfrey and Tina Pang that explore Sze's influences and her working process, plus an interview between the artist and Madeleine Grynsztejn, that expands on the theoretical underpinnings of her painting practice. With each copy numbered and hand signed by the artist, this exquisitely illustrated luxury volume, packaged in a cloth-wrapped slipcase, was created in close collaboration with Sze.
tags: Abstract Art, Art Book, Contemporary Art, Painting, Phaidon

title: Nicole Wittenberg
contributors: Suzanne Hudson, Devon Zimmerman, David Salle, Jarrett Earnest
description:
This inaugural monograph surveys the work of American painter Nicole Wittenberg across two decades.

The artist is recognized for vibrant and energetic mark making, creating compositions that synthesize studies and life drawings into larger canvas works. Her subject matter spans landscapes, portraits, and erotic imagery. The publication features essays by Suzanne Hudson (art historian), Devon Zimmerman (curator), David Salle (contemporary painter), and Jarrett Earnest (writer, in extended conversation with the artist). Presented in cloth case with floral composition details, this book coincides with solo exhibitions at Ogunquit Museum of American Art and Center for Maine Contemporary Art. Features 250 illustrations. Nicole Wittenberg was born in San Francisco, CA, and received her BFA from the San Francisco Art Institute in 2003.

She received the American Academy of Arts and Letters' coveted John Koch Award for Best Young Figurative Painter in 2012. From 2011–14 she served as a teacher at the New York Studio School of Drawing, Painting, and Sculpture, and the Bruce High Quality Foundation University, and in 2017 she was a professor in the Critical Theory Department at the School of Visual Arts in New York. Wittenberg's works are included in prominent collections, including the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York The Albertina, Vienna the Museum of Fine Arts Boston Aishti Foundation, Beirut and others. She has enjoyed recent solo exhibitions at Massimo de Carlo, Milan (2024) Fernberger Gallery, Los Angeles (2024) Journal Gallery, New York (2023) Nina Johnson Gallery, Miami (2023) and Acquavella Galleries, Palm Beach (2022). She is based in New York and Maine.
tags: American Art, Contemporary Art, Monacelli, Painting

title: Lorna Simpson
description: Monograph on artist Lorna Simpson by Okwui Enwezor, published by Abrams.

title: Folksongs
description: An artist's book and monograph showcasing Prince's conceptual work across multiple mediums. Features new body of paintings alongside studio photos and documentation of various sculptures and installations from his Upstate series. Works incorporate collage, impasto, and oil stick techniques with close-up shots of eyeballs, sutured skin and mouths with a cigarette. Includes recent sculptures made from shredded denim and car tires.
tags: Art, Conceptual Art, Contemporary Art, Photography

title: The Fug
description:
Published for Prince’s 2011 exhibition at Almine Rech Brussels, this substantial catalogue presents a montage of Prince’s engagement with peripheral aspects of American culture.

The publication features "Thirteen Different Ways of Looking at Richard Prince," an essay by John McWhinnie that gives critical context for Prince’s appropriation strategies and his excavation of vernacular imagery. The book accompanied the exhibition "The Fug," shown at Almine Rech Brussels from September 10 to November 5, 2011.

Prince, born in 1949 in the Panama Canal Zone, creates art exploring "peripheral aspects of American culture, both high and low." His work addresses subjects like jokes, vehicles, literature, and celebrity while "taking aim at the vulgar, revealing culture’s indiscretions—misogyny, consumerism, exhibitionism and idealized desire."
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Exhibition Catalog, Appropriation Art, Counterculture, Punk, Americana

title: William Klein / Atsushi Fujiwara / Utagawa Hiroshige
description: Theme: Tokyo, a hybrid of Klein's raw, graphic street work and Japanese imagery (old and new). Contents: 1 numbered photographic print by Atsushi Fujiwara (18×24 cm), 1 portfolio of 10 images by William Klein (Tokyo 1961), 1 numbered pigment print (Digigraphie) after Hiroshige, 1 additional numbered silkscreen produced in collaboration with Aesop.

title: Maisie Cousins / Leslie David / Nadia Lee Cohen
description: Theme: Hyper-color, sensual, surreal feminine imagery. Part photography, part graphic art. Contents: 1 numbered photographic print by Maisie Cousins (18×24 cm), 1 numbered pigment print by Leslie David (18×24 cm), 1 portfolio of 10 images by Nadia Lee Cohen.

title: Immersion (70 Years Magnum Photos)
description: Special edition with Magnum Photos, celebrating 70 years of the agency, focusing on its 12 women photographers. Main credited photographers for the prints: Susan Meiselas and Alessandra Sanguinetti. Theme: Immersion. A curated look at Magnum's women photographers introspective documentary and poetic reportage. Contents: 1 numbered photographic print by Alessandra Sanguinetti, 1 numbered photographic print by Susan Meiselas, Immersion portfolio: 12 images by 12 Magnum women photographers.

title: Femmes du monde (Women of the World)
description: Special edition for Femmes du monde, the 10-year anniversary exhibition of Galerie Polka in Paris. Multi-artist box featuring Sebastião Salgado, Marc Riboud, Jacob Aue Sobol. Theme: Portraits and stories of women around the world from several major documentary photographers.

title: William Klein (Polka collaboration)
description: Produced with Galerie Polka. Theme: 100% Klein – continuing Wombat's focus on his energetic, graphic photography. Contents: 2 numbered photographic prints (18×24 cm) by Klein, 1 portfolio of 10 images by Klein. Signed special edition limited to 100 copies.

title: Ransom Ashley - VIRGINS
description: Theme: Coming-of-age, queerness and identity in the American South / Bible Belt cinematic, melancholic portraits of youth. Contents: 2 numbered photographic prints by Ransom Ashley, 1 portfolio of 10 images by Ashley. Prints on Hahnemühle fine art paper, made by Processus lab box is numbered, stamp-dated, hand-assembled. Signed edition: 50 copies.

title: René Burri - Imaginary Pyramids
description: Theme: Imaginary Pyramids, focusing on iconic pyramid imagery (e.g. Giza, Egypt) and Burri's architectural/structural sense of composition. Produced with Magnum Photos for Les Rencontres d'Arles 2018. Contents: A numbered photographic print (18×24 cm), A short portfolio (booklet of about 12 pages / images) around the pyramids theme.

title: Jack Davison
description: Theme: Experimental portraiture and still life. A mix of enigmatic, graphic images, a bit of everything from his early body of work. Contents: 1 numbered photographic print (approx. 24×30 cm) on Hahnemühle, printed by Processus, Portfolio of 17 images, printed on different papers, supports and sizes, giving a very tactile, varied set. Hand-assembled and numbered.

title: JR - MOMENTUM at MEP
description: Special edition produced for JR's exhibition MOMENTUM at the Maison Européenne de la Photographie (MEP), Paris. Contents: Standard Wombat structure: at least one numbered photographic print plus an unpublished portfolio (a set of images from JR's show).

title: Stanley Kubrick - Boxing
description: Collaboration with the Museum of the City of New York (MCNY). Theme: Early Kubrick boxing photographs – prizefighters, locker rooms, the world around the ring, before he became a film director (1949-1950). Contents: 1 numbered photographic print (e.g. Rocky Graziano showering, 1950), A portfolio of 12 photographs printed on fine paper, reproducing the series. All prints on Hahnemühle fine art paper, Processus lab, box numbered, stamp-dated.

title: Betina du Toit
description: Theme: Female portraiture where women are shown as fragile, sensual and strong, without artifice – unusual beauty. Contents: Lorna, Iceland, 2018 – 1 numbered photographic print (24×30 cm) on Hahnemühle, printed by Processus, No. 39 portfolio: 10–12 images + texts on Fedrigoni collection papers.

title: Gregory Halpern
description: Collaboration with Magnum Photos. Theme: Dreamy, atmospheric color work – landscapes, portraits and ambiguous scenes, including deserts, forests, oceans and uncanny figures. Contents: 1 numbered photographic print (Untitled, 2016), 24×30 cm on Hahnemühle, printed by Processus under Halpern's supervision, Portfolio No. 40: 12 photographs on Fedrigoni collection paper, in the box, Numbered certificate of authenticity. Hand-assembled and numbered.

title: Harley Weir & Cressida Brotherstone
description: Box aims to offer a visual response to art therapy and its power to heal – fusing Weir's images with therapeutic/psychological motifs. Contents: 1 numbered photographic print by Harley Weir (24×30 cm), 1 original portfolio combining photographic prints, drawings and texts on Fedrigoni papers. Standard Wombat build: numbered, dated, hand-assembled. Separate signed edition.

title: Elizaveta Porodina
description: Theme: A surreal, cinematic, almost sci-fi parallel world – strong color, experimental lighting and fantasy-like staging. The Wombat Artist Box 42 is an invitation into a parallel world created with Elizaveta Porodina. Contents: 1 numbered photographic print by Porodina, 1 portfolio of 10 prints, plus a text and a mirrored paper element in the box. Signed edition available all copies on Hahnemühle / high-end papers, numbered, hand-assembled.

title: Zhong Lin
description: Theme: Intense, surreal female portraits water, flowers and skin oscillating between serenity and suffocation (e.g. the woman submerged with bubbles, floral mask around the face). Contents: 1 numbered photographic print (signed in the signed edition), 1 original portfolio of 10 prints. Box is signed (for the signed edition), numbered, dated and hand-assembled standard edition is unsigned but still numbered. Signed edition: 100 signed copies.

title: Cristina de Middel
description: Collaboration with Magnum Photos. Theme (series Boa Noite Povo etc.): Explores extremes of human life, belief in mythology and political feeling through staged and symbolic images of nature, made in Bahia, Brazil, often in the jungle of the Mata Atlântica. Contents: 1 numbered photographic print by de Middel, 1 portfolio (around 10 images) titled along the lines of Boa Noite Povo. Printed on Hahnemühle fine art paper under the artist's supervision, box numbered and hand-assembled.

title: Kourtney Roy - Monster Inside
description:
Series title: Monster Inside, a previously unpublished series unveiled through the Wombat box.

Theme: Roy's trademark blend of kitsch color and psychological unease – uncanny, stylised self-performance and staged scenes that introduce the uncanny into familiar landscapes, and melancholy into colourful compositions. Contents: 1 numbered photographic print by Kourtney Roy (24×30 cm), Portfolio of 10 images from the Monster Inside series. Box numbered and hand-assembled signed edition includes a signed print. Signed special edition: 100 copies.

title: Apartamento Issue 3
description:
Spring/Summer 2009, the third issue of Apartamento, with JD Samson at home in New York, Jean Touitou in Paris, the Berlin design duo Bless, and a travel supplement shot by Ari Marcopoulos, Jason Nocito and Jocko Weyland.

Luiza Sá visits JD Samson in New York City. Michael Bullock and Yasmine Dubois-Ziai photograph Alexandra Singh's Tudor village inside a warehouse, Marco Velardi meets Jean Touitou at the Ateliers de la Petite Enfance in Paris, and Andrea Lissoni writes on Bless in Berlin. Hanna Nilsson and Sofia Østerhus contribute a plant portrait from Bromma, Kris Latocha a geology of design, and Ana Dominguez and Omar Sosa a study of marble and granite. Ezra Koenig writes "Under the bridge", David Armstrong opens his Candyland, Audrey Fondecave-Tsujimura reports from Nakameguro, Juan Ignacio Moralejo visits Juan Tessi and Alexandre Fehr meets Paulo César Pereio. Karley Sciortino closes with "Slaves". The everyday-life travel supplement adds Geoff McFetridge, Lele Saveri and Giorgio Di Salvo.

Apartamento was started in Barcelona in 2008 by Nacho Alegre, Omar Sosa and Marco Velardi as an everyday life interiors magazine, photographing homes as they are lived in rather than styled for the camera. This issue is from its second year, when the format was still settling.

title: Apartamento Issue 4
description:
Autumn/Winter 2009-10, with Chloë Sevigny's New York City, Enzo Mari on the essence of beauty in Milan, Philip Crangi's studio and bachelor pad, and Ari Marcopoulos inside Sonic Youth's house.

The issue opens with New York City by Chloe Sevigny and Thea Slotover in Stella Sabin's room. Michael Bullock photographs the jeweller Philip Crangi in New York City, Tim Small talks to Enzo Mari in Milan, Simon Castets visits Cyril Duval's control tower in Tokyo, Juan Ignacio Moralejo meets Gustavo Di Mario in Buenos Aires and Misha Janette finds Sonya Park at home in Tokyo. Nacho Alegre photographs Grillo Demo, Jocko Weyland reports on China apartments, Nick Currie writes on post-materialism in Berlin and Emily King on Mark & Garrick. Marlene Marino contributes "Post-sex and relaxation", Elsa Fischer a collage feature, Bertjan Pot the free potato wallpaper, and Porzia Bergamasco family tales made in Italy. The materials study this time is drinking glasses.

Enzo Mari's interview is one of the magazine's early statements of intent: a designer talking about how things should be made and used rather than how they should look. Apartamento returned to him in issue 12, through Murray Moss's collection of his work.

title: Apartamento Issue 5
description:
Spring/Summer 2010, from Walter Pfeiffer's home in Zurich to Justin Bond's East Village and the Koryo Hotel in Pyongyang, with an everyday-life travel supplement folded in.

Jacob Åström photographs the Koryo Hotel in Pyongyang and Marco Velardi visits Walter Pfeiffer in Zurich. Tokyo appears twice, with Yoko Amakawa on Narukiyo, an unconscious collector, and Cameron Allan McKean on Midori Araki. Juan Ignacio Moralejo photographs Leandro Erlich and Luna Paiva in Buenos Aires, Michael Bullock meets Justin Bond in New York City and Katherine Clary follows Alex Wiederin home. Thea Slotover cooks in Claudia's kitchen, Lovefoxxx writes on sunlight, Marlene Marino contributes "Classical New York City" and Mateo Kries the alchemy of the everyday. Daniel Riera photographs the Rambla del Raval, Retts Wood the Boat Club, and Imaad Wasif goes inside the secret world of the voidist. The materials study is wood, and the travel supplement covers 24 hours in Vancouver, the Japanese mountains and a Phoenix photo journal.

Apartamento was founded in Barcelona in 2008 by Nacho Alegre, Omar Sosa and Marco Velardi. By its fifth issue the pattern of the magazine was fixed: long interviews with people photographed in their own homes, a recurring study of one material, and a supplement on some part of everyday life.

title: Apartamento Issue 6
description:
Autumn/Winter 2010-2011, with Gosha Rubchinskiy in Moscow, Tomi Ungerer in Cork, Carl Johan De Geer in Stockholm, and Kinder, a children's supplement curated by Benjamin Sommerhalder with a colouring book by James Jarvis and activity pages by Miranda July.

Jonathan Olivares opens with "Today's home" from New York City. Alexander Elzesser meets Gosha Rubchinskiy, youth prophet of the suburbs, in Moscow; Thea Slotover visits 6a Architects' Steph MacDonald and Tom Emerson on Orde Hall Street in London; Michael Bullock photographs Leon Ransmeier's Wall Street shack; Juan Ignacio Moralejo meets Felisa Pinto in Buenos Aires and Helena Nilsson Strängberg the romanticist modernist Carl Johan De Geer in Stockholm. Bert Krus visits Frank Bruggeman's cactus misfits in Rotterdam, Marlene Marino photographs Paz de la Huerta, Charlie Koolhaas contributes "City21Millenium", Anders Edström "Todai Moto Kurashi" and Francesc Pons a piece on Leopoldo Pomés. Victoire and Ramdane Touhami write "africamento", Emily King covers Les Nouïes and Maria Vittoria Backhaus the Island of Calvary. Materials: inox and minerals.

Kinder was the first of Apartamento's supplements made for children, with Tomi Ungerer interviewed by Daniel Morgenthaler and Miranda July drawing the activity pages.

title: Apartamento Issue 7
description:
Spring/Summer 2011, with Kenny Scharf in Los Angeles, Bruce Benderson's technicolor two-bedroom in New York, Juana Molina in Buenos Aires, and an everyday-life food supplement featuring Alice Waters and Jim Haynes.

Paula Yacomuzzi opens with "Crisis vs. Creativity" from Barcelona. Anja Aronowsky Cronberg meets Zoe Bedeaux, the sourceress, in London; Jenna Sutela visits the textile designer Vuokko Eskolin-Nurmesniemi in Helsinki; Helena Nilsson Strängberg photographs Liselotte Watkins in Milan; Francesco Spampinato talks to Kenny Scharf; Juan Ignacio Moralejo finds Juana Molina at home in Buenos Aires; Michael Bullock visits Bruce Benderson in New York City; and Maria Cristina Didero tells the story of Aldo Ballo and Marirosa Toscani Ballo in Milan. Gemma Holt writes on Rosanjin, Blunk and clay, Nicolas Trembley on fat lava, Nick Currie on a new box, and Ola Rindal photographs a home overlooking the park. The food supplement carries Eva Hagberg on Alice Waters, Anja Aronowsky Cronberg's "Join me for supper!", Miguel Figueroa on Gloria Pinette and Anaïs Melero, and essays by Chiara Merino and Claire Frisbie. The materials study is bricks.

The food supplement marked the magazine's growing interest in the kitchen as the centre of a home, a thread that runs through later issues in interviews with Margot and Fergus Henderson, Jessica Koslow, Ruth Rogers, Claudia Roden and Rachel Roddy.

title: Apartamento Issue 8
description:
Autumn/Winter 2011-12, with Nathalie Du Pasquier arranging things in Milan, Faye Toogood's world in a suitcase, Marcelo Krasilcic on the Lower East Side, and La Monte Young's Dream House.

David Torcasso visits Beda Achermann's walk-in sketchbook in Zurich. Michael Bullock photographs Marcelo Krasilcic in New York City, Marco Velardi meets Faye Toogood in London, Helena Nilsson Strängberg talks to Nathalie Du Pasquier in Milan, Juan Ignacio Moralejo visits Pilar Benitez Vibart in Buenos Aires and Adrian Gaut photographs Elizabeth Beer and Brian Janusiak's useful accumulation in New York City. Philippe Parreno writes on things we make together, Julie Cirelli on La Monte Young's Dream House, Cosimo Bizzarri on Selam, Ivano and the treehouse, and Paula Yacomuzzi on Javier Mariscal. Victoria Camblin, Thea Slotover, Ken Miller, Jose Arnaud-Bello, David John and Makoto Orui contribute shorter pieces, Olaf Breuning circus animals, Marlene Marino "Busy in Brooklyn" and Mike Meiré "Are we there yet?". Aya Sekine photographs possessions. The materials studies are bread and, from Adrià Cañameras and Ana Dominguez, aubergines.

The issue's Featuring list also names Michael Stipe and Patrick Parrish, both of whom went on to write for the magazine themselves: Stipe interviewed Kim Hastreiter in issue 19, and Parrish wrote on Jim Walrod in issue 10 and Murray Moss in issue 12.

title: Apartamento Issue 9
description:
Spring/Summer 2012, with Wolfgang Tillmans, Tierney Gearon's family matters in Los Angeles, Yrjö Kukkapuro in Helsinki, Reg Mombassa in Sydney, and a fiction supplement by Jocko Weyland and Amanda Maxwell.

Ida Kukkapuro writes about one family and one room in Helsinki, and Adam Saletti visits Conor Donlon above his shop in London. James Ross-Edwards meets Reg Mombassa in Sydney, Alice Cavanagh photographs Tierney Gearon in Los Angeles, Max Lamb visits the Harrisons, potter and weaver, in Cornwall, Evangelia Koutsovoulou talks to the modern Hellenist Nanos Valaoritis in Athens, Michael Bullock sees Mexico City in two dimensions with José León Cerrillo and Jonathan Openshaw finds Duncan Fallowell book-cornered in London. Chris Johanson and Jo Jackson describe the way they live with it all in Portland, with an introduction by Sean Kinnerly. Jocko Weyland writes on commerce on the Agora, Jeff Rian on being lucky enough to like where you live, Jonathan Olivares on today's walls, and Karley Sciortino on roommates. Leah Singer photographs a tree stump, Tomás Nervi a solar stupor in Paris, Marlene Marino a nook in the sky. The materials study is candles.

The Featuring list also names Li Edelkoort, Jean Abou, Gonzalo Milà, Jordi Labanda, Ramdane Touhami, BOPBAA, India Salvor Menuez, Henry Roy and Max Lamb. Lamb's visit to the Harrisons is one of the few times the magazine has sent a designer to write about other makers.

title: Apartamento Issue 10
description:
Autumn/Winter 2012-13, the tenth issue, opening with Ai Weiwei on living and running through Tauba Auerbach's Soho apartment, Devonté Hynes, Esther Mahlangu in Weltevreden and Jim Walrod, the most famous interior designer you have never heard of.

Luiza Sá visits Tauba Auerbach in New York City, Karley Sciortino meets Devonté Hynes, Cosimo Bizzarri finds Ken Garland at 71 Albert Street in Camden Town, Evangelia Koutsovoulou talks to Yorgos Lanthimos by phone and Helena Nilsson Strängberg visits the ceramic legend Lisa Larson in Stockholm. Felisa Pinto and Juan Moralejo see Juan Stoppani in Buenos Aires, Patrick Parrish writes on Jim Walrod in New York, Matthew Freemantle meets Esther Mahlangu, queen of Ndebele art, Jocko Weyland spends a day in the strife with Edward Colver in Los Angeles, Michael Bullock photographs David Toro and Solomon Chase of DIS, and Emanuele Fontanesi visits Christophe Lemaire and Sarah-Linh Tran in Paris. Arquitectura-G browse Marlene Acayaba's book on the houses of São Paulo, Witold Rybczynski offers thoughts about home, Elein Fleiss writes on life, Nicholas Lander on the restaurateur and Alix Browne on her architect. The materials study is tape, and the issue carries a portfolio by Aurora Altisent and comics by Artus De Lavilleón and Andy Rementer with Margherita Urbani.

This is the first issue with an essay by Arquitectura-G, the Barcelona architecture practice whose piece on a single building recurs in most of the issues that followed.

title: Apartamento Issue 11
description:
Spring/Summer 2013, with François Halard learning to see in Arles, Michael Stipe sad to leave New York, Apichatpong Weerasethakul through the trees in Mae Rim, and Bob Gill across the pond and back.

Nacho Alegre photographs François Halard in Arles. Leon Ransmeier talks to Bob Gill in New York City, Rujana Rebernjak to Santi Caleca in Milan, Francesco Spampinato to Michael Smith in Austin, Mo Veld to Maurice Scheltens and Liesbeth Abbenes in Amsterdam, Jeff Rian to Dike Blair in New York and Helena Nilsson Strängberg to Anton Henning in Manker. Jeremy Liebman visits Apichatpong Weerasethakul in Mae Rim, and Michael Stipe writes on leaving New York City himself. Daniel Morgenthaler chairs a conversation in Zurich under the title "Time for your shelf". Ute Woltron writes on the elegance of lightness, Arquitectura-G on a tailor-made world, Ramdane Touhami welcomes readers to his home, Karley Sciortino meets a dominatrix, Jonathan Olivares reads customer reviews, Tenko Nakajima lives in a waffle and Marlene Marino contributes "L'ami de mon amie". The materials study is clay, and Mirko Borsche and Gian Gisiger illustrate a selection of proverbs.

The Featuring list also names Ricardo Bofill, Elfie Semotan, Tony Cederteg, Adrià Cañameras, Lovis Caputo, Lars Müller, Alexander Schärer and Henry Roy. Andy Rementer and Margherita Urbani's comic continues from issue 10.

title: Apartamento Issue 12
description:
Autumn/Winter 2013-14, with Genesis P-Orridge interviewed by Devendra Banhart, Omar Souleyman on tour in Sète, Trix and Robert Haussmann in Zurich, and Murray Moss's collection of Enzo Mari.

Alia Farid Abdal meets Omar Souleyman, an émigré on tour. Marlene Marino photographs Rose McGowan in Los Angeles, Nathalie du Pasquier visits the painter Chung Eun Mo in Torre Orsina, Michael Bullock finds Times Square on the Bowery with Scott Ewalt, Daniel Morgenthaler talks to Trix and Robert Haussmann in Zurich and Amelia Stein visits Ken Done in Sydney. Marisa Brickman meets Scott Sternberg in Los Angeles, Helena Nilsson Strängberg the painter Christoph Ruckhäberle in Leipzig, Emanuele Fontanesi the designers Aurélien Arbet and Jérémie Egry between New York and Paris, and Cameron Allan McKean the graphic designer Atsuki Kikuchi in Tokyo. Patrick Parrish writes on Murray Moss collecting Enzo Mari, Jonathan Olivares contributes "Acartamento", Arquitectura-G almost eight hectares, Maria Gerhardt a bunker in Copenhagen and Kasia Bobula a living museum. The materials study is magnets.

The Featuring list also names Sara Sachs and Frederik Jacobi, Smiljan Radic, Piero Gandini, Jolanthe Kugler and Francesco Zanot. Andy Rementer and Margherita Urbani's comic runs again.

title: Apartamento Issue 13
description:
Spring/Summer 2014, with Wes Anderson, Jack Pierson between New York and Twentynine Palms, Peter Shire as the mayor of Los Angeles, and The Girards, a supplement on the legacy of Alexander Girard.

Helena Nilsson Strängberg meets Rafael Horzon, anything but an artist, in Berlin. Jonathan Olivares follows Joel Chen round the world and home to Los Angeles, Jessica Piersanti visits Jean-Charles de Castelbajac in Paris, Michael Bullock sends Bernhard Willhelm to Hollywood, Evangelia Koutsovoulou talks life and cookbooks with Anissa Helou in London, Amelia Stein photographs Jack Pierson for the ages and Matt Paweski and Ryan Conder visit Peter Shire. Marco Velardi, Nacho Alegre and Omar Sosa put together The Girards, and Luciano Consigli contributes the portfolio "Humor Furniture Graphic". Mirella Clemencigh writes "I could hardly show you how to get there", Cameron Allan McKean "A train is rolling", Haydée Touitou "Un homme d'intérieur", Arquitectura-G a pre-classical house, Alix Browne "Shop till you drop" and Marlene Marino "Delta of Venus". The materials study is sugar, and the issue opens with a piece on shopping rituals.

The Featuring list also names Wes Anderson, Faye Toogood, Marie Honda, Richard McConkey, Adel Husni Bey, Arturo Rhodes, Fabiola Alondra, Oscar Tusquets Blanca and the comic duo Andy Rementer and Margherita Urbani. Jack Pierson's own books are held elsewhere in this library.

title: Apartamento Issue 14
description:
Autumn/Winter 2014-15, with Peter Halley remaining in light, Raymond Pettibon interviewed by Leah Singer, Jeremiah Goodman's insider view, and Jocko Weyland at Kentuck Knob.

Jocko Weyland opens at Kentuck Knob and contributes a short story. Haydée Touitou meets Michael Lindsay-Hogg in Paris, Adrian Walter visits Koudlam in Grenoble, Alex Tieghi-Walker goes around the world in several thousand objects with Terry Ellis in London, Ida Kukkapuro talks to the glass designer Oiva Toikka in Helsinki and Daniel Morgenthaler finds Lora Lamm living in a palimpsest in Zurich. Jim Walrod interviews Peter Halley in New York City, Pilar Viladas visits the illustrator Jeremiah Goodman, Wes Del Val meets Christiaan Houtenbos, Anne Waak photographs Birgitta Homburger and Florian Lambl in Berlin, and Leah Singer interviews Raymond Pettibon. Adam Yarinsky writes on preserving experience, Michael Anastassiades on hearing, seeing and doing, JW Anderson on life through objects, Elena Quarestani on the house that ages with no fear, and Marlene Marino photographs the ladies of Apartment #17. Goodman also contributes a portfolio of painted interiors. The materials study is ice.

Jeremiah Goodman painted interiors on commission for more than sixty years, and the portfolio here gathers a selection of them.

title: Apartamento Issue 15
description:
Spring/Summer 2015, with Vince Aletti among men in New York, Ryan McGinley's adventures, Ruth and Marvin Sackner's Miami collection, and an Ibiza special on Armin Heinemann and Paula's Ibiza.

Paul Schiek photographs Vince Aletti in New York City. Dean Kissick finds Matthew Stone in a pickle in London, Jim Walrod meets Gene Krell, a man of many hats, in Tokyo, Nacho Alegre visits Linus Bill living in a bakery in Biel, Matthew Freemantle the weaver Marguerite Stephens in Johannesburg, Leah Singer the Sackners in Miami, Alexander Kori Girard Todd Oldham's house of style in New York and Daniel Morgenthaler the photographer Shirana Shahbazi in Zurich. Hillary Navin follows Ryan McGinley, and Nacho Alegre travels to Ibiza for Armin Heinemann and his boutique. Amelia Stein writes on seats of power, Jeff Rian on connections, Alix Browne "All together now", Koen Sels "A telling mess", Arquitectura-G on how César loved to dance, and Haydée Touitou on the importance of MTV Cribs. Marlene Marino photographs Donald Cumming and Georgia Ford. Artus de Lavilléon and Jessica Piersanti contribute a special edition of their fanzine Deadpan, featuring Gaspar Noé. The materials study is brass and copper.

The Featuring list also names Guy Rombouts and César Manrique.

title: Apartamento Issue 16
description:
Autumn/Winter 2015, built around Donald Judd: a trip to Las Casas, his Texan ranch, with Flavin and Rainer Judd, and a collection of his everyday-life objects, alongside AA Bronson in Berlin, Denise Scott Brown in Philadelphia and Gary Panter on being weird.

Alix Browne visits Flavin and Rainer Judd at Las Casas to talk about growing up Judd. Michael Bullock meets AA Bronson in Berlin, Jim Walrod finds Matt Connors in New York City, Amelia Stein talks space and work with Denise Scott Brown, Leah Singer visits Gary Panter, Albert Moya photographs the sculptor Xavier Corberó in Barcelona and Yorgo Tloupas visits the house of Philolaos at Saint-Rémy-lès-Chevreuse, where everything the artist did not like he designed himself. Arquitectura-G open with the Hellscraper in Madrid. David Douglas Duncan's photographs of the private world of Pablo Picasso are reprinted, Jean-Philippe Delhomme paints a portrait of a house, Guillermo Santomà writes that to create is to destroy, Anna von Löw considers curation, Jorge de Cascante contributes "Sea, swallow me" and Marlene Marino "Heaven in hell's despair". The materials study is paper.

The Featuring list also names Arielle Holmes and Fernando Higueras. Judd's furniture and his ideas about how a space should be arranged sit close to what Apartamento has always been about, which is why the magazine gave him most of an issue.

title: Apartamento Issue 17
description:
Spring/Summer 2016, with Martha Stewart, Klaus Biesenbach, Petra Collins, Liam Gillick, Kathy Ryan's furniture romance and Wolfgang Tillmans's pictures of The Spectrum on Montrose Avenue.

Laura Regensdorf interviews Martha Stewart. Helena Nilsson Strängberg visits Johann and Lena König, Jim Walrod meets Petra Collins, Paul Schiek talks to Kathy Ryan, Michael Bullock to Klaus Biesenbach, Dean Kissick to Jason Schwartzman and Brady Cunningham, Leon Ransmeier to Liam Gillick and Haydée Touitou to Victoire de Castellane and Thomas Lenthal. Arquitectura-G visit Antonioni's Costa Paradiso, Luis Cerveró writes on the painter Abdul Mati Klarwein, Benoît Wolfrom on Javier Perés's African art, Robbie Whitehead on Raphaël Zarka in Paris, and Karley Sciortino interviews herself. Michael Bullock's piece on The Spectrum, the New York City queer party space, runs with Tillmans's photographs. A conversation on modern craft and Kathy Ryan's "Furniture Romance" round out the issue. The materials study is foam.

Petra Collins and Karley Sciortino both appear here as subjects after Sciortino had written for the magazine for years, from "Slaves" in issue 3 to "The dominatrix" in issue 11.

title: Apartamento Issue 18
description:
Autumn/Winter 2016-17, with a trip to Andrea Zittel's A-Z West in Joshua Tree, Kembra Pfahler, Margaret Howell, Fernando Arrabal, JB Blunk, and Jean-Philippe Delhomme's paintings from the Peloponnese coast.

Alix Browne visits Andrea Zittel in Joshua Tree, California. Michael Bullock meets Kembra Pfahler, Hugo Macdonald talks to Margaret Howell, Jordi Labanda to the publisher Luis Venegas, Dean Kissick to the cook Jessica Koslow, Jim Walrod to the painter Duncan Hannah in New York City, Alexander Kori Girard writes on JB Blunk, Haydée Touitou meets Sébastien Meyer and Arnaud Vaillant, Leah Singer visits Jeanne Greenberg Rohatyn, Pau Guinart talks to Fernando Arrabal and Kat Herriman to Chloe Wise in New York City. Molly Goddard is photographed at home. Arquitectura-G write on the house as a city, James Ross-Edwards on Jules the house guest, and "Making Meaning" is a conversation with Susan Sellers, Andrew Zuckerman and Sam Grawe. Delhomme's series is called "The kamara". The materials study is potatoes.

Jean-Philippe Delhomme's painted contributions run through this period of the magazine, from the portrait of a house in issue 16 to the rental opportunities in issue 20 and "The Forgotten Painter" in issue 23.

title: Apartamento Issue 19
description:
Spring/Summer 2017, with Alessandro Mendini in Milan, Richard Hell and Kim Hastreiter in New York, Leonard Koren at Point Reyes, Bernard Rudofsky's "La Casa", and a portfolio of Robby Müller Polaroids.

Gianluigi Ricuperati talks to Alessandro Mendini in Milan and Mariah Nielson to Leonard Koren at Point Reyes. Hugo Macdonald meets Penny Martin in London, Jim Walrod visits Richard Hell in New York City, Marta Riezu the artist Antoni Miralda in Barcelona, Leah Singer the illustrator Barbara Nessim, Joe Magliaro Naoki Takizawa in Tokyo, Michael Stipe Kim Hastreiter, Flavin Judd the set decorator Ford Wheeler, Michael Bullock Flawless Sabrina, and Marco Velardi Cristopher Nying in Stockholm. Arquitectura-G take on "La Casa" by Bernard Rudofsky. A feature on Instagram stories and a conversation with Carlota Guerrero, Paloma Lanna and Soraya Rosales sit alongside Haydée Touitou's selection of Robby Müller's Polaroids. The materials study is plastic bags.

Robby Müller, the cinematographer of Paris, Texas and Down by Law, made Polaroids for decades between films; this portfolio came out a year before his death, when the pictures were only beginning to be shown.

title: Apartamento Issue 20
description:
Autumn/Winter 2017-18, with Lawrence Weiner, Alec Soth in Minneapolis, Gay Talese, Kyoichi Tsuzuki and his Tokyo Style, Margot and Fergus Henderson in London, and Maureen Paley interviewed by Vince Aletti.

Hugo Macdonald visits Margot and Fergus Henderson. Jae Seok Kim meets the graphic designer Na Kim in Seoul, Alice Cavanagh Julien Dossena in Paris, Vince Aletti Maureen Paley in Hove, Luis Cerveró the painter Maria Pratts in Barcelona, Paul Schiek Alec Soth in Minneapolis, Leah Singer Lawrence Weiner in New York City, Jim Walrod the director Jerry Schatzberg and Sabrina Tarasoff the Nest founder Joseph Holtzman in Valatie. Cameron Allan McKean interviews Kyoichi Tsuzuki, and a selection from Tsuzuki's Tokyo Style follows. Arquitectura-G write on a device for contemplation in the Matarraña, a feature asks whether we are living in a domestic dystopia, Jean-Philippe Delhomme paints a series of unique rental opportunities, Jocko Weyland contributes the short story "Human-shaped hole" and Andy Rementer and Margherita Urbani the comic "When and where?". The materials study is toilet paper.

Tsuzuki's Tokyo Style (1993), photographs of the small, crammed apartments of ordinary Tokyo, is one of the books Apartamento's own approach descends from, so the pairing of interview and reprint here reads as an acknowledgement.

title: Apartamento Issue 21
description:
Spring/Summer 2018, with Nicolas Party in Brussels, Peter Berlin in San Francisco, Henry Taylor in Los Angeles, Juan Grimm's garden at Los Vilos, and a grandson's account of living with Nicola L.

Alix Browne visits Katie Stout in New York City. Sinisa Mackovic meets Nicolas Party in Brussels, Nacho Alegre the designer Sabine Marcelis in Rotterdam, Takuhito Kawashima the painter Henry Taylor in Los Angeles, Laila Gohar the chef Danny Bowien in New York City, Erik Hartin the photographer Lina Scheynius in London, Matt Connors the artist Peter McGough in New York City, Paul Gorman the painter Duggie Fields in London, Jae Seok Kim Hong Seung-Hye in Seoul, Maria Cristina Didero Lapo Binazzi in Florence, Jean-Philippe Delhomme the illustrator Pierre Le-Tan in Paris, Emilio Marín the landscape architect Juan Grimm at Los Vilos and Michael Bullock Peter Berlin in San Francisco. Oliver Lanzenberg writes on living with Nicola L. Arquitectura-G visit a house in Ghent under the title "Endless set of possibilities", and "Space Jam" is a conversation with Pablo Díaz-Reixa, Oriol Riverola and Luis Cerveró. The materials study is rubber.

The Featuring list also names Mr Portsmouth and Sylvia Whitman of Shakespeare and Company. Peter McGough's interview by a fellow painter, Matt Connors, is typical of how the magazine matches subjects with writers who already know them.

title: Apartamento Issue 22
description:
Autumn/Winter 2018-19, with Fernando Botero in Pietrasanta, Françoise Mouly and Ingo Maurer in New York, BV Doshi in Ahmedabad, Sheila Heti in Toronto, and Alberto Ponis's Sardinia.

Leah Singer visits Sheila Heti in Toronto, with watercolours by Leanne Shapton. Hugo Macdonald talks to Ruth Rogers, Madeleine Willis to the gallerist Yvon Lambert in Paris, Maisie Skidmore to the photographer Campbell Addy in London, Michael Bullock to the painter Jonathan Lyndon Chase in Philadelphia, Jocelyn Silver to Nick Murphy in New York City, Gabriel Fowler to Françoise Mouly, Ji-Un Nah to Oh Hyuk in Seoul, Komal Sharma to the architect BV Doshi in Ahmedabad, Robbie Whitehead to the director Ruben Östlund in Gothenburg, Haydée Touitou to the publishers Mélanie Scarciglia and Christophe Boutin in Paris, Kim Hastreiter to the lighting designer Ingo Maurer, Pere Pedrals to the cartoonist Nazario Luque in Barcelona and Jessica Piersanti to Fernando Botero in Pietrasanta. August Becker writes on the painter Gertrude Abercrombie. Arquitectura-G's "The Crystal and the Flame" covers Ponis's houses at Palau, and Nazario contributes the comic "Helena: A Shadow in the Plaza Real". The materials study is bones.

Doshi had won the Pritzker Prize earlier in 2018; the magazine returned to him with an obituary by Khushnu Hoof in issue 31.

title: Apartamento Issue 23
description:
Spring/Summer 2019, with Telfar Clemens in New York, Tadanori Yokoo and Samiro Yunoki in Tokyo, Laurie Spiegel, Kazuo Shinohara's House in Uehara, and a conversation on spaces of desire between Kembra Pfahler, Robert Yang and Joel Sanders.

Maisie Skidmore visits the photographer Coco Capitán in London and Harry Lester the winemaker Patrick Bouju at Saint-Georges-sur-Allier. Leah Singer talks to the composer Laurie Spiegel, Andrew Romano to the sculptor Ricky Swallow in Los Angeles, Michael Bullock to Telfar Clemens in New York City, Leti Sala to Paloma Lanna in Barcelona, Takuhito Kawashima to the ceramicist Takuro Kuwata in Toki City and to Tadanori Yokoo in Tokyo, Adam Iezzi to Jessica Ogden at Ocho Rios, Alexander Kori Girard to the textile designer Samiro Yunoki in Tokyo, Isaiah Yehros to the sculptor Nobuo Sekine in Los Angeles and Kim Hastreiter to Thomas Lauderdale in Portland. Arquitectura-G write on Shinohara's House in Uehara, and Jean-Philippe Delhomme contributes the story "The Forgotten Painter". The materials study is charcoal.

The Featuring list also names Carlos Somorrostro. Shinohara returned in issue 32, with Seng Kuan on the House with an Earthen Floor.

title: Apartamento Issue 24
description:
Autumn/Winter 2019-20, with Xavier Dolan in Montreal, Marine Serre in Paris, Kenneth Ize in Lagos, Lykke Li, Ron Nagle interviewed by Peter Shire, Cecilia Chiang, and Mark Lebon's story about a house told by Carmen Hall and Frank Lebon.

Leah Singer visits Jessi Reaves in New York City. Andrew Zebulon and Kristen Wentrcek meet Serban Ionescu, Durga Chew-Bose talks to Xavier Dolan, Helen Jennings to Kenneth Ize, Mish Barber-Way to Lykke Li in Los Angeles, Fabio Cherstich writes on the painter Patrick Angus, Jessica Piersanti visits Marine Serre, Fanny Singer the restaurateur Cecilia Chiang in San Francisco, Guillermo Santomà the architect Oscar Tusquets in Barcelona, Paul Gorman Ben Kelly and Clare Cumberlidge between London and Pett Level, Kim Hastreiter the jeweller Ted Muehling, Enrique Giner de los Ríos the composer Michael Nyman in Mexico City, Michael Bullock 321 Gallery in New York City, Peter Shire the ceramicist Ron Nagle in San Francisco, Gudrun Willcocks the architect Peter Stutchbury in Sydney, Robbie Whitehead Rafram Chaddad at Le Kram in Tunis and Evangelia Koutsovoulou the painter Alekos Fassianos in Athens. "Living in the present" is a conversation between Jack Self, Stephanie Macdonald and Vinca Petersen. The materials study is wire.

Rafram Chaddad, interviewed here at home, went on to write for the magazine: on Charles Perry in issue 26, Claudia Roden in issue 29 and, in issue 32, a guide to Libyan prison.

title: Apartamento Issue 25
description:
Spring/Summer 2020, with Simone Fattal and Etel Adnan, Barbara Stauffacher Solomon in San Francisco, Thaddeus Mosley in Pittsburgh, Rirkrit Tiravanija, Ray Johnson's Pink House, and Vinca Petersen's portfolio of 1990s rave culture.

The issue opens with "A question of taste", a conversation about food. Robbie Whitehead interviews Vinca Petersen alongside her portfolio "No System". Sarah Souli visits the composer Lena Platonos in Athens, Brendan Dugan the sculptor Thaddeus Mosley in Pittsburgh, Pere Pedrals the artist Amèlia Riera in Barcelona, Hugo Macdonald the set designer Gary Card in London, Alix Browne Andy Coolquitt in Austin, Matylda Krzykowski Barbara Stauffacher Solomon in San Francisco, Jina Khayyer Simone Fattal and Etel Adnan, Enrique Giner de los Ríos Lucas Cantú and Carlos H Matos in Mexico City, Leah Singer the filmmaker Michael Snow in Toronto, Michael Bullock Nick Cave and Bob Faust, Lola Kramer Rirkrit Tiravanija between Chiang Mai and New York City and Haydée Touitou the winemaker Gabrio Bini on Pantelleria. Arquitectura-G write on Sam Chermayeff, Iris Humm contributes the photo album "Immediate family", and Frances Beatty tells Hannah Martin the story of Ray Johnson's Pink House on Long Island. The materials study is pills.

Etel Adnan was 95 when this interview ran, photographed at home with Simone Fattal, her partner of many decades.

title: Apartamento Issue 26
description:
Autumn/Winter 2020-21, with Martine Rose in London, Thomas Demand in Biesenthal, Carlo Rovelli in Verona, Ottessa Moshfegh in Pasadena, Willi Smith's life on Lispenard Street, and Luigi Ghirri's interiors selected by Matt Connors and Adele Ghirri.

Maisie Skidmore visits Martine Rose. Emanuele Quinz talks to the physicist Carlo Rovelli, Oliver Mol to Ottessa Moshfegh, María Inés Plaza Lazo to Thomas Demand, Karl Sjölund to the composer Kali Malone in Stockholm, Francesca Balena and Maria Cristina Didero to Andrea Branzi in Milan, Estelle Hanania to the illustrator Bernadette Després at Givraines and Ruth Gebreyesus to the chef Tunde Wey in New Orleans. Arquitectura-G write on the architect Anne Holtrop, Rafram Chaddad on Charles Perry, Jocko Weyland on the painter Olivier Mosset and Camille Okhio on the designer Willi Smith. A conversation takes up the Indigenous Australian concept of Country, and Yelena Moskovich contributes the short story "Funny body". The materials study is glass.

The Featuring list also names James Wines, Manuel Núñez Yanowsky and Park Seo-Bo. Ottessa Moshfegh returned in the next issue with a story of her own, "The imitations".

title: Apartamento Issue 27
description:
Spring/Summer 2021, with Louise Bourgeois's New York home, Tabboo!, Pedro Friedeberg and Mario García Torres in Mexico City, Larry Stanton on Fire Island, and the first chapter of Zebadiah Keneally's graphic novel "All the things I know".

Anne Hanavan and Michael Bullock visit Tabboo! in New York City. Yining He talks to the photographer Luo Yang, Carlota Pérez-Jofre to Mario García Torres, Nicholas Lewis to David Numwami in Brussels, Suleman Sheikh Anaya to Pedro Friedeberg, Madeleine Willis to the winemakers Anders Frederik Steen and Anne Bruun Blauert at Valvignères, Leah Singer walks through Louise Bourgeois's house, Jocko Weyland meets the jeweller Alex Streeter in Tucson, Michael Bullock the designer Victor Barragán, Matt Connors the painter Roger Herman in Los Angeles, Marta Sironi the artist Lucia Pescador in Milan, Andrew Zuckerman Alexandra Cunningham Cameron and Seth Cameron, Carmen Hall Sabrina Fuentes in London, and Arthur Lambert and Fabio Cherstich remember Larry Stanton, the artist as a young man. Arquitectura-G write on Leopold Banchini, and Ottessa Moshfegh contributes the short story "The imitations". The materials study is chalk.

Larry Stanton died in 1984. Lambert, who knew him, and Cherstich later edited a monograph on his work; the Fire Island piece here comes out of that research.

title: Apartamento Issue 28
description:
Autumn/Winter 2021-22, with Soisy and the Sphinx, the homes of Niki de Saint Phalle, alongside Paa Joe in Accra, Fritz Haeg at Albion, Luigi Serafini in Rome, Joan E. Biren's portraits of lesbians, and an essay by Paul B. Preciado on living with Matta.

Leah Singer visits Saint Phalle's houses at Soisy-sur-École and Pescia Fiorentina, and Gemma Janes meets Nathalie de Saint Phalle in Naples. Adjoa Armah and Elaine Yj Lee talk to the coffin-maker Paa Joe, Susana Vargas Cervantes to Joan E. Biren in Washington DC, Michael Cukr to the painter Katherine Bernhardt in St. Louis, Fabio Cherstich to Luigi Serafini, Michael Bullock to Fritz Haeg, Jazmine Hughes to Topaz Jones in New York City, Emanuele Quinz to Gianni Pettena in Fiesole, Francis Upritchard to Lisa Walker and Karl Fritsch in Wellington, Natalia Torija Nieto to Jose Dávila in Guadalajara, Zdenka Badovinac to Roman Uranjek in Ljubljana and Brendan Embser to Paul Moakley. Pettena also writes about his cabin on Elba, Biren's "Eye to eye" is excerpted, and "To Craft a Life" gathers conversations with Bikôkô, Carlota Guerrero and Ouka Leele. Zebadiah Keneally's graphic novel reaches chapter two. The materials study, this time, is shit.

Biren's Eye to Eye: Portraits of Lesbians (1979) was reissued in 2021, which is what put her in this issue; she returned in issue 30 with a piece called "At Home".

title: Apartamento Issue 29
description:
Spring/Summer 2022, with Álvaro Siza, Duane Michals, Claudia Roden in London, Marco Glaviano interviewed by Cindy Crawford, Allen Frame remembering Darrel Ellis, and a trip to Adrere Amellal in the Siwa Oasis.

Rafram Chaddad visits Claudia Roden. Camille Okhio talks to the designer Minjae Kim in New York City, Omar Sosa to Mounir Neamatalla in Cairo, Fabio Cherstich to Allen Frame about Darrel Ellis, Jocko Weyland to the ceramicist Alice Mackler, Ji-Un Nah to Choi Byung-Hoon in Paju, Novena Carmel to Sydney Loren Bennett in Los Angeles, Leah Singer to Duane Michals, Giacomo De Poli to Joan Thiele in Milan, Michael Bullock to Sarah Ortmeyer in Vienna, Jina Khayyer to Reza and Mamali Shafahi in Tehran, Cindy Crawford to Marco Glaviano, Daniel Riera to Álvaro Matxinbarrena at Elgorriaga, Kim Hastreiter to the architect Solveig Fernlund, Anne Hanavan to Kunle Martins and Sara Flynn to Bryan Harding in London. Arquitectura-G write on Siza, Antonio Porteiro and Miles Hudson travel to Adrere Amellal, and the issue carries "Eleven Stories about Food" and Fernanda Ballesteros's short story "400 Breasts".

Allen Frame kept Darrel Ellis's work together after the artist's death in 1992, and this piece ran as Ellis's first museum retrospective was being prepared.

title: Apartamento Issue 30
description:
Autumn/Winter 2022-23, the thirtieth issue, with Solange Knowles, Mel Ottenberg, Raghu and Avani Rai, Ugo La Pietra, Channa Daswatte in Colombo, Clayton Patterson, and a short story by Dodie Bellamy.

Chloe Sultan visits Solange Knowles in Los Angeles. Kaisha Davierwalla and Andrea Grecucci talk to Ugo La Pietra in Milan, Leah Singer to Marina Faust in Vienna, Michael Bullock to Mel Ottenberg in New York City, Zico Judge to Avani and Raghu Rai at Gurugram, Osayi Endolyn to Jon Gray, Bernat Daviu to the painter Ángela de la Cruz in London, Anne Hanavan to Clayton Patterson, Andrea Lazarov to the designer Alejandro Gómez Palomo at Posadas, Oliver Mol to the filmmaker Levan Koguashvili in Tbilisi, Ruby Neri to Woody de Othello in Oakland, Jocko Weyland to Kitty Brophy in Tucson, Lena Solà Nogué to Wilfredo Prieto in Havana and Sarah Souli to the architect Channa Daswatte and, in Paris, to Yasmine Dubois and Brian Rogers. Raghu Rai contributes "Chinar Havely" and Arquitectura-G "Looking for Problems". A run of shorter texts follows: Sam Chermayeff on universal individualism, Michael Bullock on alpha misfits, Emanuele Quinz on haunted houses, JEB (Joan E. Biren) at home, Ciaran Thapar outside his cocoon, Enrique Giner de los Ríos on his dream house, Andrés Jaque on transscalarity and Leah Singer on remembering to bring flowers.

This is where the magazine's back section changed shape: from issue 30 the interviews are followed by a suite of commissioned essays and fiction, a pattern that grew in the issues after it.

title: Apartamento Issue 31
description:
Spring/Summer 2023, with Pedro Costa building the house from the inside, Dayanita Singh in Goa, Alexander Calder's houses at Saché, Paul Mpagi Sepuya, Abdellah Taïa, and Khushnu Hoof's memory of Balkrishna Doshi.

Robbie Whitehead visits Tal R and Emma Rosenzweig in Copenhagen. Zico Judge talks to Dayanita Singh and writes on her as an offset artist, Carmen Hall to Laura and Deanna Fanning in London, Pablo Cendoya to the sculptor Seyni Awa Camara at Bignona, Beatrice Domond to the filmmaker William Strobeck in New York, Jocko Weyland to Robert Barber in Tucson, Jina Khayyer to Abdellah Taïa in Paris, Camille Okhio to Misha Kahn in New York City, Lucy Kumara Moore to Supriya Lele in London, Javier Codesal to Pedro Costa at Amadora, Michael Bullock to Paul Mpagi Sepuya in Los Angeles and Fabio Cherstich to Lucia di Luciano and Giovanni Pizzo at Formello. Leah Singer covers Calder's Saché houses and Arquitectura-G the photographer Bas Princen. Taïa contributes the story "The Goodbyes", and the back section carries John Douglas Millar's "Blue Overture", Oscar Perry's conversation with a fish, Layla Benitez-James on corners, Estelle Hoy's "We'll try existing another day" and Diana McCaulay making stew peas for her mother.

Doshi had appeared as an interview subject in issue 22; he died in January 2023, and Hoof's tribute here is the magazine's farewell.

title: Apartamento Issue 32
description:
Autumn/Winter 2023-24, with King Krule and his nothingness of possessions, John Divola in Riverside, Deanna and Ed Templeton at Huntington Beach, Tom of Finland's Pleasure Park, Not Vital, and Kazuo Shinohara's House with an Earthen Floor.

Svetlana Kitto visits the photographer Marianna Rothen at Livingston Manor. Carmen Hall talks to King Krule in London, Zico Judge to John Divola, who also contributes "More beautiful times", Jina Khayyer to Akwaeke Emezi in New York City, Pablo Bofill to Vincent Darré in Paris, Mariah Nielson to Ruby Neri in Los Angeles, Oliver Mol to the chess champion Nona Gaprindashvili in Tbilisi, Kim Hastreiter to the Templetons, Andrew Bonacina to Anthea Hamilton in London, Rory Seydel to the potter Wayne Ngan on Hornby Island, Andrew Romano to Louise Bonnet and Adam Silverman in Los Angeles, Michael Bullock on Tom of Finland's house, David Khalat to Not Vital and Tosia Leniarska to Jago Rackham and Lowena Hearn in London. Seng Kuan writes on Shinohara. Bryan Washington contributes the story "Commonwealth", and the back section runs Rafram Chaddad's guide to Libyan prison, Emily Balistrieri on The Tatami Galaxy, Gerardo Sámano Córdova's "Motel", Leeor Ohayon's recipe for his grandmother's marak dl'hrira, Estelle Hoy's glossary of threats, Eva Baltasar on her cave house, Victoria Cirlot in the cell and Danyel Smith's "Walls of sound".

Chaddad's prison piece, translated by Joanna Chen, is a long way from the interiors that fill the front half of the issue.

title: Apartamento Issue 33
description:
Spring/Summer 2024, with Hari Nef in New York, Franz Erhard Walther in Fulda, Ron Arad and Madelon Vriesendorp in London, Lloyd Kahn at Bolinas, Enrique Olvera in Mexico City, and the interiors of Pedro E. Guerrero.

Michael Bullock visits Hari Nef. Estelle Hoy talks to Franz Erhard Walther, Maddy Weavers to Madelon Vriesendorp, Deyan Sudjic to Ron Arad, Camille Okhio to the artist Eric N. Mack in New York City, Carla Fernández to the chef Enrique Olvera, Anissa Touati to the designer Najla El Zein in Amsterdam, Lukas Feireiss to Shelter author Lloyd Kahn, Alex Whyte to the cook Rachel Roddy in Rome, Fabio Cherstich to the painter Jimmy Wright in New York City, Stuart Munro to the photographer Motoyuki Daifu in Tokyo, Rhea Dillon to Antonia Marsh in London and Oliver Mol to the winemaker John Wurdeman in Tbilisi. Arquitectura-G write on Hans-Walter Müller and Leah Singer on Guerrero, the photographer of Frank Lloyd Wright's houses. Diana McCaulay's essay "Termite Trails" leads a back section with Yemisi Aribisala, Sophie Mackintosh, Jenny Wu, Fadi Kattan, Stephen Kearse, Amanda Maxwell, David Zilber and Ronan Mckenzie.

Amanda Maxwell's "Odontalgia" is a return: she wrote for the magazine's first years, from "Whole earth" in issue 4 through the fiction supplement of issue 9.

title: Apartamento Issue 34
description:
Autumn/Winter 2024, with Ronan Bouroullec somewhere in Brittany, Rose Wylie photographed by Ben Rivers, Tove Jansson's island of Klovharun, Agosto Machado and Jane Dickson in New York, Olivia Laing at Yoxford, and a short story by Alejandro Zambra.

Durga Chew-Bose visits the stylist Miyako Bellizzi in New York City and Omar Sosa the designer Ronan Bouroullec. Ben Rivers talks to Rose Wylie in Kent, Claudia Durastanti to SAGG Napoli at Presicce-Acquarica, Michael Bullock to Agosto Machado, Hugo Macdonald to Beca Lipscombe in Edinburgh, Anna Prudhomme to Celeste in London, Sini Rinne-Kanto on Tove Jansson, whose key to her island hangs by the door, Emanuele Coccia on why Espace Aygo in Brussels lives forever, John Douglas Millar to Gary Schneider and John Erdman at Brookhaven, Lou Stoppard to Bethan Laura Wood, Pablo Bofill to Edgardo Giménez at Punta Indio, Meara Sharma to the painter Danny Fox in St Ives, Leah Singer to Jane Dickson, Clem Macleod to Olivia Laing, Leonard Koren to Luca Lo Pinto in Rome and Zico Judge to the director Molly Manning Walker in London. The back section carries Maria Judite de Carvalho's "The Aquarium", Zambra's "The Kid with No Dad", and texts by Phoebe Chen, Miguel Ángel Hernández, Thea McLachlan, Elena Saavedra Buckley, Janika Oza, Wale Ayinla and Claudia Durastanti.

Translated fiction has become a regular part of the magazine since issue 32: Zambra is translated by Megan McDowell, Carvalho by Margaret Jull Costa and Hernández by Fionn Petch.

title: Apartamento Issue 35
description:
Spring/Summer 2025, with Camille Henrot in New York, Darius Khondji in Paris, Leïla Slimani in Lisbon, Chilly Gonzales, Wendy Whiteley in Sydney, Vivian Suter at Panajachel, Dan Friedman's seismic visions, and a screenplay by Efthimis Filippou.

Estelle Hoy visits Camille Henrot. Zico Judge talks to the cinematographer Darius Khondji, Elise Lammer to Catherine Schroeder on Ibiza, Laura Barton to Chilly Gonzales in London, Jina Khayyer to Leïla Slimani, Michael Bullock to the designer Raul Lopez, Ashleigh Wilson to Wendy Whiteley, Noah T. Britton to the novelist Robert Plunket at Palmetto, Martha Kirszenbaum to the painter Huong Dodinh in Paris, Michael Cukr to Deaton Chris Anthony in Los Angeles, Sini Rinne-Kanto to Erna Aaltonen and Howard Smith at Fiskars, Rui Hua to the painter Zhou Yilun in Hangzhou, Jocko Weyland to Steve Bailey at Center Valley and Laura Cabezas to Vivian Suter. Hannah Martin writes on Dan Friedman and Nacho Alegre on Miguel Milá, the punk. Plunket contributes the story "The Divine Art of Living" and Filippou the screenplay "14 Stout Men"; the back section adds Silvina Ocampo, Durga Chew-Bose, Charlie Porter, Lina Soualem, Yilin Wang, Nate Lippens and Hiroko Oyamada.

Robert Plunket's 1983 novel My Search for Warren Harding was reissued in 2023 after decades out of print, which is how a retired Florida columnist came to be photographed at home for a Barcelona interiors magazine.

title: Apartamento Issue 36
description:
Autumn/Winter 2025, with Noreen Masud on Charleston House, Louis Fratino in New York, Graciela Iturbide in Mexico City, Takashi Homma in Tokyo, Moki Cherry's schoolhouse at Tågarp, Lourdes Castro on Madeira, and a short story by Mariana Enriquez.

The issue opens with "Time 2 Kill", a series of pastimes by Jody Barton. Philippa Snow visits Isamaya Ffrench in London, Jordan Weitzman the painter Louis Fratino in New York City, Zico Judge the filmmaker Dea Kulumbegashvili between Berlin and eastern Georgia, Carmen Hall Moki Cherry's schoolhouse, Craig Mod the photographer Takashi Homma in Tokyo, Olukemi Lijadu Taiwo Lijadu of the Lijadu Sisters, Noreen Masud Charleston House at Lewes, Robbie Whitehead Konstantin Kakanias and Joe Pickman in Los Angeles, Leah Singer Lourdes Castro at Caniço, Vusumzi Nkomo the ceramicist Zizipho Poswa in Cape Town, Ramón Reverté Graciela Iturbide, Sandy Powell the set designer Simon Costin at Launceston, Fabio Cherstich Valerie Giampietro and Alessandro Cicoria in Rome and John Douglas Millar Anita Vitale in New York City. Arquitectura-G call Christian Kerez an architect from outer space, and Laura Frade's "This is not a house" features Ignasi Monreal and friends in Madrid. Enriquez's "Nelly", translated by Megan McDowell, runs with "Mrs Tependris Takes a Bath".

Takashi Homma's own photobooks are held elsewhere in this library, and his first appearance in Apartamento was in issue 5, in 2010, so the interview here closes a fifteen-year loop.

title: All The Young Punks
description:
All The Young Punks is a two-headed book, balancing candid photographs Graham MacIndoe took during the formative punk years of his youth with a more recent series of the objects he later came across from that time.

After rediscovering the photographs, records and ephemera from his days as a young punk in Scotland in the late 1970s, MacIndoe re-photographed those artifacts as precisely lit and composed still lifes. The book juxtaposes the candid old pictures of his life as a punk with the new images of ticket stubs, concert badges, record covers and music press clippings, setting the people and the objects of that period in dialogue.

Published in a limited edition of 125 signed copies.
