title: Backstage Pass: Rock & Roll Photography
description:
Backstage Pass: Rock & Roll Photography collects nearly one hundred portraits of rock’s central figures caught away from the stage, most of them made before their subjects had become famous enough to be well practiced at posing.

Shot from the mid-fifties to the mid-nineties, the pictures run from Elvis to Eric Clapton, the Beatles to Bob Dylan, Jimi Hendrix to John Coltrane, and many have rarely been published. The spontaneous, informal, everyday register is the point: these are glimpses of celebrities off stage, away from the glare of the spotlights.

More than fifty photographers contribute, among them Lee Friedlander, Lynn Goldsmith, Bob Gruen and Mick Rock, with texts by Glenn O’Brien, Anne Wilkes Tucker, Laura Levine and Greil Marcus. Published by Yale University Press for the Portland Museum of Art.

title: CREEM: America's Only Rock 'N' Roll Magazine
description:
With raw photographs of rock’s greatest stars and insightful prose by the rock journalists who were stars in their own right, CREEM stood at the forefront of youth counterculture from 1969 to 1988 as America’s Only Rock ’n’ Roll Magazine.

A product of Detroit’s revolutionary counterculture, CREEM cultivated an iconoclastic staff of scribes, editors, photographers and graphic artists whose work continues to resonate — Lester Bangs, Dave Marsh, Richard Meltzer, Nick Tosches and a not-yet-famous Cameron Crowe among them. They invented a raucous new form of journalism in which the writing and photographs were as much an expression of rock ’n’ roll as the music itself.

The magazine embraced and abused the best and worst of the era: MC5, Led Zeppelin, the Rolling Stones, the Faces, Lou Reed, the Stooges, T. Rex, Kiss, Mott the Hoople, the Who, the New York Dolls, Bob Seger, Ted Nugent, Aerosmith, the Ramones, Cheap Trick, the Clash and Van Halen. This retrospective draws on the magazine’s archive of photographs, illustrations and articles to cover rock’s golden age, from the end of the hippie days through glam and punk into 1980s metal.
tags: CREEM, Design, Magazines, Music, Music Journalism, Periodical, Rock and Roll
notes: Three copies in the collection.

Early Photography 1977–87
description:
This definitive publication documents three simultaneous Gagosian exhibitions presenting Prince's revolutionary early photographic practice.

Over seventy works demonstrate how Prince redefined authorship through 'rephotography,' appropriating advertising imagery and transforming it into artworks that critique consumer desire and American mythology. The volume includes the complete Entertainers series (1982-83), rarely exhibited manipulated photographs evoking Times Square's adult entertainment venues. Sydney Stutterheim's eight-section essay explores Prince's pivotal role in establishing appropriation as artistic strategy, supported by archival materials from his Time magazine work and installation views.

title: New Paintings
description:
Published by Fulton Ryder in September 2022, this 377-page cloth hardcover artist's book presents Richard Prince's New Paintings alongside dense autobiographical and art historical commentary.

The paintings focus on portraits of painters painting on Instagram, often with their backs to the camera, facing away from the viewer. The resulting images are ambiguously manipulated through digital means, creating what Prince describes as 'social science fiction.'

The image captions contain Prince's characteristic 'Bird Talk' text, weaving together autobiography, art history, and cultural commentary. With 370 color images, the book documents Prince's continued engagement with appropriation in the digital age, examining how contemporary artists construct identity and visibility through social media platforms.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Instagram, Social Media, Appropriation Art, Digital Culture, Photography, Fulton Ryder

description:
Published by Fulton Ryder in February 2025, this 96-page hardcover artist's book documents Richard Prince's 1-2-3-4 series begun around 2008.

The work sequences found photographic portraits into simple numerical headcounts: one person, two people, three people, four people. Prince applies this system to images of musicians, actors, celebrities, and anonymous subjects, transforming them into 'performing acts: solo artist, duo, trio, quartet.' The numbering concept references punk-rock count-ins (1-2-3-4!) while incorporating jersey-number aesthetics from sports culture.

The project connects to Prince's Instagram handle @richardprince1234 and demonstrates his continued interest in seriality, appropriation, and the transformation of found imagery through systematic recontextualization. The 80 color images document this cheekily compounding approach to group portraiture.
tags: Art, Photography, Appropriation Art, Conceptual Art, Seriality, Music, Celebrity, Fulton Ryder

title: The Entertainers
description:
Published by Fulton Ryder in 2023, this 152-page artist's book features The Entertainers (1982–83), an early series of photographs made during Prince's 'Time Life' years spent around the theaters, grind houses, bars and restaurants of New York's 42nd Street and Times Square.

The photographs manipulate publicity shots of aspiring singers, actors, and models, softening their focus, heightening their contrast, and adding garish colors and graphic elements that capture the area's sleazy glamour. The volume includes 135 color plates documenting this rarely exhibited body of work. Prince's introductory text 'The Counterfeit Memory' (1981) describes his experiences compiling tear sheets for magazines and spending time in adult film theaters, restaurants, and bars. The book concludes with another text by the artist entitled 'The Lone Ranger.'
tags: Art, Photography, Times Square, Celebrity Culture, Appropriation Art, 1980s New York, Entertainment Industry, Fulton Ryder

title: Gangs
description:
This book was published on the occasion of the exhibition "Richard Prince: Gangs" at Gladstone New York.

Its introductory text records an intimate discussion between the artist and Nancy Spector on the iconic series. Prince placed pilfered images into "gangs" coordinated by subject matter—surfer waves muscle cars biker "chicks" criminals celebrities heavy metal bands. "Gang" was the word used by the photo lab in the early 1980s for the technique of gathering slides into a printed photograph. Spector writes: "There is a defining ethos of criminality in Prince's work. He jailbreaks the art world does what he wants and we as his audience reap the benefit of his renegade vision."

title: Family Tweets
description:
For Desert X 2017 in California's Coachella Valley, Prince installed printouts from his Birdtalk blog—originally posted on Twitter (@richardprince4) in 2014—inside and outside an abandoned house in Desert Hot Springs.

The works explored familial relationships, social media appropriation, and domestic dysfunction through appropriated and original tweets. Three days after installation, visitors removed most works, creating an unintended participatory performance that became integral to the piece's meaning. This book preserves the ephemeral installation, documenting Prince's investigation of digital culture, social media, and the constructed self in the age of Twitter.

title: You Can't Drink It If It's Frozen
Purple Book
description:
Published in 2012 as a special edition for Purple Fashion Magazine #18 in celebration of the magazine's 20th anniversary, this 80-page artist's book features Richard Prince's collages using celebrity promotional photographs combined with his own text comments and questions.

The work includes images of Cher, Keanu Reeves in Point Break, Snoop Dogg, Terence Stamp, Milla Jovovich, Brian Eno, Mel Gibson, and other celebrities. Printed on superior quality glossy and matte paper in A4 format, the publication demonstrates Prince's characteristic appropriation of mass media imagery and his layering of found photographs with text. The collaboration with Purple magazine positions Prince's work within fashion and contemporary culture discourse, extending his practice of transforming celebrity imagery through recontextualization and textual intervention.
tags: Art, Fashion, Celebrity, Appropriation Art, Purple Magazine, Photography, Text Art, Collage

title: Mister Nicotine: The George Condo Purple Book
description:
Special artist book created by George Condo for Purple Institute's Purple Books series, a supplement to Purple Fashion magazine issue 23 (Spring/Summer 2015). Titled "Mister Nicotine," this publication represents Condo's collaboration with Purple, the influential Paris-based fashion and contemporary art magazine founded by Olivier Zahm and Elein Fleiss in 1992. Purple Books, launched as an extension of the magazine, commissions artists to create autonomous book works that exist at the intersection of artist publication, magazine supplement, and independent edition.

Born in 1957, George Condo pioneered "Psychological Cubism," representing multiple emotional and psychological states simultaneously within single figures. His "Artificial Realism" synthesizes Old Master painting techniques with American pop culture and cartoon aesthetics, creating distorted portraits that authentically depict psychological complexity and contradiction. Emerging from New York's 1980s East Village scene, Condo has maintained close connections to fashion and music worlds throughout his career, collaborating with Kanye West on album artwork and participating in fashion magazine projects that blur boundaries between fine art and popular culture.

"Mister Nicotine" likely explores Condo's recurring themes of consumption, addiction, and psychological states through his signature visual language of fragmented faces, multiple eyes, and distorted features. The title evokes both the glamorous smoking culture historically associated with fashion imagery and Condo's darker investigations into compulsive behavior and altered consciousness. This format, between magazine and artist book, allowed Condo to reach Purple's international fashion and art audience while maintaining the conceptual autonomy of an independent artist publication.

Published by Purple Institute, Paris, 2015. Format: 21.0 × 29.7 cm, softcover. Part of the Purple Books series. George Condo's work is held in collections including MoMA, The Metropolitan Museum, Whitney Museum, Louisiana Museum, Guggenheim, and The Broad. This publication represents Condo's engagement with fashion world contexts and magazine-format artist books, extending his practice beyond traditional gallery and museum presentations.
notes: Published 2015 by Purple Institute, Paris as Purple Book supplement to Purple Fashion magazine issue 23 (Spring/Summer 2015). Format: 21.0 × 29.7 cm. Softcover. Part of the Purple Books series commissioning artists for autonomous book works. George Condo (b. 1957) coined "Psychological Cubism." His work bridges fine art and popular culture, including collaborations with fashion magazines and musicians. Collections: MoMA, Met, Whitney, Louisiana, Guggenheim, The Broad.

title: 120 crossed out, 121 nurses+
description:
Bootleg artist Eric Doeringer creates a double-appropriation by assembling the original romance novel covers that Prince rephotographed for his iconic Nurse Paintings (2002-2005).

The publication functions as both art historical research and conceptual artwork, revealing Prince's sources while questioning authorship, originality, and the bootleg as artistic practice. Doeringer, known for making and selling unauthorized copies of contemporary artworks, turns Prince's appropriation strategy back on itself, creating a recursive commentary on the art market and intellectual property.
tags: Art, Bootleg Art, Appropriation Art, Meta-Appropriation, Nurses, Romance Novels, Pulp Culture, Copyright, Art Market Critique

title: 1234 Instagram recordings, volume 12
description:
Published by French artist and publisher Sébastien Girard in 2019, this is the final volume (12 of 12) documenting Richard Prince's Instagram account 'richardprince1234.'

Between 2015 and 2017, Prince posted reappropriated images from other Instagram users daily, deleting them after a few hours. Girard saved all 2,664 images and compiled them into a 12-volume set, each with 48 pages. The complete project comprises 2,664 album cover variants, with each volume packaged in a 12-inch (LP-format) record sleeve featuring one of the recorded images.

Launched at the NY Art Book Fair 2019 at MoMA PS1 and Offprint Paris during Paris Photo 2019, the first edition of 150 sets sold out immediately. This bootleg appropriation of Prince's appropriations creates a meta-commentary on digital ephemera, ownership, and archival practice in the Instagram age.

title: Bibliothèque d’un Amateur 1981-2014
description:
Published by Viaindustriae in 2014, this first edition documents Richard Prince's work regarding books and collections from 1981 to 2014.

Conceived as an invitation to browse the library of an amateur collector rather than a formal catalogue raisonné, the publication addresses Prince's production of artists' books and his personal library over 33 years. Edited by Christophe Daviet-Thery and Jérôme Saint-Loubert Bié, the volume captures Prince's engagement with appropriation, collecting, and publishing as artistic practices. Published following exhibitions at Palazzo Collicola Arti Visive in Spoleto and at Christophe Daviet-Thery gallery in Paris in 2012.
tags: Art, Bibliography, Reference, Publishing, Collecting, Appropriation Art, Fulton Ryder

title: Canal zone yes Rasta
description:
This essential volume compiles court documents from Cariou v.

Prince, the landmark 2011 copyright case between photographer Patrick Cariou and Richard Prince. Allen's publication includes Prince's revealing 101-page deposition where he discusses his artistic practice, appropriation strategies, and the Canal Zone series that sparked the lawsuit. The case, which Prince partially won on appeal (2013), established important precedent for fair use and transformative works in contemporary art. The book functions as both legal record and primary source material for understanding appropriation art's relationship to copyright law.
tags: Art, Legal Documents, Copyright, Court Case, Fair Use, Appropriation Art, Canal Zone, Art Law, Primary Source, Deposition

title: Cowboys
description:
Published for the 2013 Gagosian Gallery Beverly Hills exhibition, this 112-page hardcover catalog documents more than fifty paintings from Richard Prince's legendary Cowboys series.

The publication features Prince's appropriated and rephotographed images of Marlboro advertisements, transforming commercial iconography into meditations on American mythology, masculinity, and the constructed nature of Western identity. Novelist James Frey contributes a new text inspired by the series, woven throughout the plates.

Designed by An Art Service and printed by Shapco Printing in Minneapolis, the large-format catalog captures the scale and visual impact of Prince's paintings. The Cowboys series, begun in the 1980s, established Prince as a pioneering appropriation artist and remains among his most recognized and influential work.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Photography, Cowboys, Appropriation Art, Marlboro, American West, Masculinity, Exhibition Catalog, Gagosian

Part of Picture Books, an imprint conceived by author Emma Cline that pairs leading contemporary writers with celebrated artists. The pairing reflects both artists' engagement with American mythology—Everett's literary deconstruction of landscape commodification and Prince's photographic appropriation of the mythic West.

title: Richard Prince - Tiffany Paintings
binding: Author: McWhinnie, John, Richard Prince Language: English Pages: 66 Size: 30.5 x 25.4 cm Weight: 1.3600 kg Binding: Hardcover ISBN: 9781935263135 Availability: - Price: [Request price.](https://www.mottodistribution.com/shop/contacts) Product DescriptionCondition: MINT Gagosian Gallery is pleased to present an exhibition of new paintings and related newsprint collages by Richard Prince. Prince first attracted attention in the early 1980s with images re-photographed from magazine ads, through which he defined for himself the concepts of authorship, ownership, and aura. Applying his understanding of the complex transactions of representation to the making of art, he has evolved a unique signature filled with echoes of other signatures yet that is unquestionably his own. Begun in 2004 at the juncture of the Nurse and De Kooning paintings and evolving through the Canal Zone and After Dark series, the Tiffany paintings reflect Prince's continuing attentiveness to the recurring patterns and suggestive potential of advertising, honed by years of perusing newspapers and magazines. These almost abstract, monochrome paintings treat the plain yet distinctive ads that New York's most famous jewelry brand has run daily for many years in the upper right hand corner of the same page of The New York Times, while echoing associations with another classic, Truman Capote's Breakfast at Tiffany's, whose object of desire Holly Golightly lures admirers only to elude them later. 1st Edition
description:
Published in an edition of 2,000 for the 2010 Gagosian Gallery exhibition, this catalog documents Richard Prince's Tiffany Paintings series.

The works appropriate advertisements from Tiffany & Co., isolating jewelry imagery against monochrome grounds to create paintings that examine luxury, desire, and brand mythology. The catalog includes 42 reproductions of works from the exhibition, a complete checklist, and an essay by John McWhinnie titled 'Breakfast at Tiffany's, painting.'

Housed in a printed cloth-covered slipcase, the publication itself functions as luxury object, mirroring the high-end brand aesthetics of the appropriated source material. The Tiffany Paintings extend Prince's practice of transforming commercial imagery into high art, questioning the boundaries between advertising, fine art, and luxury consumption.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Appropriation Art, Luxury Brands, Jewelry, Tiffany & Co., Advertising, Exhibition Catalog, Gagosian

title: Same man lp
description: Published for Prince's first major retrospective in Scandinavia, featuring 89 works spanning his career from 1970s rephotography to recent Instagram paintings. The LP format references Prince's engagement with music culture while the poster-book hybrid reflects his interest in ephemeral and vernacular publishing formats. Bilingual essays by Nancy Spector and Anders Kold examine Prince's continued relevance and his pioneering role in appropriation art.

title: Spinster poems
description: Bonami's introspective poems meditate on solitude, memory, and the figure of the spinster as a metaphor for creative independence and psychological complexity. Prince's foreword characterizes Bonami's voice as 'shapeshifting, mercurial, wayward,' drawing connections between the curator's poetic sensibility and his decades of engagement with contemporary art. The slim volume reflects Karma's commitment to publishing experimental writing by artists and curators.

title: Super Group
description:
Prince collages inner sleeves from vinyl records onto canvas, then overpaints them with band names, abstract color washes, and figurative elements. The series explores how we construct identity through choices of music, objects, and images. Continuing Prince’s investigation of appropriation and authorship, the works transform music ephemera into paintings that interrogate fandom, nostalgia, and the commodification of counterculture.

Published by Holzwarth Publications in 2018, the large-format 92-page hardcover (11 1/2 × 14 inches) documents the series with full-page reproductions that capture the scale and detail of the works.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Painting, Collage, Appropriation Art, Music, Vinyl Culture, Celebrity, Group Identity, Large Format

title: The first century good life essay by John McWhinnie, Glenn H
The Karpidas Collection
description:
Published in 2022 by Specific Object in a limited edition of 500 copies, this 98-page softcover catalog documents the exhibition at the Karpidas family's private art space in Dallas.

The publication features high-quality reproductions of Richard Prince's art from the Karpidas Collection, including his renowned Cowboys, Nurses, and Joke series. Edited by Sara Hignite and designed by Travis LaMothe, the catalog includes essays by Brandon Kennedy, Mark Flood, and Lucia Simek, providing curatorial notes and scholarly context for Prince's exploration of appropriation, identity, and American culture.

The exhibition and catalog position the Karpidas holdings within Prince's broader artistic narrative, examining four decades of work that interrogates authorship, originality, and media representation.
tags: Art, Contemporary Art, Exhibition Catalog, Cowboys, Nurses, Jokes, Appropriation Art, Private Collection, Dallas, Limited Edition

title: The outdoor coed, topless pop fiction appreciation society
description:
The Outdoor Co-ed Topless Pulp Fiction Appreciation Society was a New York-based feminist group that staged topless reading sessions in public parks and spaces, asserting women's legal right to be topless in public while subverting male gaze through the act of reading.

Prince appropriates their self-published photographs in this limited edition, creating a complex layering of appropriation, feminism, and voyeurism. Published through his Fulton Ryder imprint in an edition of 300, the book raises questions about consent, re-appropriation, and the ethics of using activist imagery as art material.

title: We go to the movies alone
Yea Yea Yea - SUTCLIFFE, Stuart and Richard Prince
description:
Published in 2012 by Harper's Books for an East Hampton exhibition, this limited edition catalog documents 21 paintings and paper-based works by Stuart Sutcliffe (1940-1962), the original Beatles bassist who left the band to pursue painting in Hamburg.

Curated by Richard Prince, the exhibition and catalog examine Sutcliffe's brief but intense artistic career, which was cut short by his death at age 21. Prince authored an essay on Sutcliffe that was included in the limited edition booklet. Of the 500 total copies, 50 were signed by both Prince and Sutcliffe's sister, Pauline.

The collaboration came about serendipitously when Prince, interested in Sutcliffe's work, contacted Harper's to be put in touch with the estate. Prince's curatorial involvement and essay position Sutcliffe's paintings within art historical discourse, connecting his Abstract Expressionist-influenced work to broader narratives of 1960s art and rock culture.
tags: Art, Painting, Abstract Expressionism, Beatles, Stuart Sutcliffe, Rock Music, Exhibition Catalog, 1960s, Limited Edition, East Hampton

title: Richard Prince: Lynn Valley 1
description:
This nicely produced, staple-bound pamphlet is the first in a new series of artist-designed publications, scheduled to come out three times per year.

This first issue contains a selection of works by Richard Prince, the influential New York artist who first created controversy in the 1970s by working with appropriated imagery--then a quite radical concept. Weighing in at only 46 pages, this slim volume nevertheless contains representative samples of all of Prince's most famous work: biker girls, nurses, sculptures, paintings, tattoo pornography, jokes, and other assorted incendiary images. The next issue of Lynn Valley will be designed by Cologne artist Johannes Wohnseifer.

title: Of & About Posters: The Lawrence Weiner Poster Archive (1965-2021)
description:
The first publication to document the 250 posters that comprise the Lawrence Weiner Poster Archive (1965–2021) held in the Vancouver Art Gallery's collection.

Featuring an introductory essay by exhibition curator Grant Arnold, who has worked with the Lawrence Weiner Poster Archive since the mid-1990s, and short commissioned texts from artists, scholars, and curators who worked closely with Weiner throughout his career, Of & About Posters will be the definitive text on this central aspect of Lawrence Weiner's production. Lawrence Weiner is considered one of the foremost conceptual artists worldwide.

His posters, which are a fundamental part of his practice and are designed by the artist himself, have appeared as promotions for exhibitions as well as works in and of themselves. This publication includes a full presentation of the Lawrence Weiner Poster Archive, consisting of more than 250 posters from the collection of the Vancouver Art Gallery. Together, they convey the evolution of Weiner's work over a period spanning more than fifty years.

title: Ayoung Kim: Synthetic Storyteller
contributors: Essays: Nanna Heidenreich, Chien-Hung Huang, Jinshil Lee, Chanda Prescod-Weinstein, Wonhwa Yoon Interview: Hyunjoo Byeon
description: A selection of artworks produced between 2007 and 2022, featuring still images, installation views, and critical essays. The monograph encompasses Ayoung Kim's multimedia practice including video, moving image, VR, game simulation, sonic fiction, diagrams, and texts that explore geopolitics, mythology, technology, and futuristic themes. Published in Korean and English with support from the 2023 ARKO Selection Visual Art.

title: Les Oiseaux
description:
When the forest of Notre-Dame caught fire, Lola Raban-Oliva and Jean René Etienne were at home, just two kilometers away.

Each had their own camera, their own zoom lens. From their window, it became almost possible to imagine the perspective of birds. It was no longer Notre-Dame burning, nor even a cathedral. Not a fire, but a vast disruption of the aerial space. A thick, blazing, chaotic convective column rose above the heart of Paris. Les oiseaux brings together 97 screenshots taken from the footage they captured that evening.
tags: Notre-Dame, Paris, Fire, French, Photography, Documentary, Disaster
notes: About the Authors: Lola Raban-Oliva and Jean-René Etienne are a Paris-based creative duo who work under the name Partel Oliva. They are a creative partnership whose multidisciplinary work spans film, art, and fashion. Hailing from the south of France and the Caribbean island of Martinique, they are visual storytellers that find inspiration in fact, fiction, and feeling. As creative directors for Kenzo, they turned the enduring brand into an avant-garde landmark. Their work has included a short film for KENZO's SS17 Collection called "Club Ark Eternal," a tribute to club culture with original music by Lafawndah and movement direction by Ryan Heffington. They previously published "Formentera Storyline" in The Paris Review (Issue 220, Spring 2017).  About the Publisher: RVB Books is a Paris-based independent publisher (95 rue Julien Lacroix, 75020 Paris, France) specializing in contemporary photography books, known for its innovative approach to design and collaborative projects with artists to create unique, limited-edition publications.  Historical Context: The Notre-Dame fire broke out at Notre-Dame Cathedral, Paris, on the evening of April 15, 2019, damaging the iconic landmark and garnering attention worldwide. The fire destroyed most of the roof and the 19th-century spire. More than 400 firefighters battled the blaze. The cathedral reopened on December 7, 2024, following a restoration that cost approximately €840 million and involved about 2,000 craftspeople.

title: Slanted Magazine #45—Sex
description:
Slanted Magazine #45—Sex explores themes of gender, body image, and sexuality from both contemporary and historical perspectives.

The magazine presents artistic positions dealing with body politics and self-image, featuring work that challenges the underrepresentation of marginalized bodies—including non-binary, queer, disabled, and racialized individuals. Through provocative imagery and diverse stories, the publication opens dialogue about bodies and belonging. The issue draws from the Archive Artist Publications' collection of over 89,988 rare zines, booklets, posters, and printed matter, in collaboration with Archive Artist Publications (AAP), Munich, directed by Hubert Kretschmer.
tags: Magazines, Design, Typography, Gender, Sexuality, Queer Culture

title: AFM Issue 2: Mind Games
description:
AFM Issue 2: Mind Games is an inquiry into and expression of the puzzles our thoughts create—how they shift, deceive, and reshape across love, memory, and identity.

The issue takes on affirmations, revisions, and the rewrites we make to our own stories, turning assumptions inside out. It features essays, fiction, photography, and poetry exploring sexuality and relationships. The cover features musician Kelsey Lu, photographed by Nan Goldin. AFM is an arts and literary publication exploring sexuality and relationships through essays, fiction, poetry, conversations, and visual art.
tags: Periodical, sexuality, relationships, literary, arts, Photography
notes: Editors: Maria Dimitrova and Haley Mlotek. Creative Director: Merel van den Berg (formerly of The Gentlewoman). Illustrator: Mona Chalabi. Photographer: Nan Goldin (cover).

title: AFM Issue 1: Pursuits of Happiness
description:
AFM: A Fucking Magazine is a biannual print publication exploring desire, sexuality, and relationships through essays, fiction, poetry, conversations, and visual art.

The inaugural issue, themed "Pursuits of Happiness," celebrates the many dimensions of desire, sexuality, and relationships. It functions as a physical object of desire, designed to be held, smelled, and flipped through. The issue features contributions from Hanif Abdurraqib, Bruce LaBruce, James Ivory, Juliana Huxtable, Sophie Mackintosh, Daphne Merkin, Allison P. Davis, and other notable figures.

title: Felix Gonzalez-Torres: Always to Return
contributors: Charlotte Ickes, Josh T Franco, Julie Ault, Joshua Chambers-Letson, Teresita Fernández
description: This monograph examines the artist's relationship to portraiture, expanding the genre from static representations of individuals to one with the capacity to change, remain resonant, and encourage collaboration. The publication accompanies a major exhibition at the Smithsonian and combines exhibition documentation with new scholarship and archival materials. Co-published with the National Portrait Gallery and the Archives of American Art, Smithsonian Institution.

title: Purple Issue 5 (Volume II)
description: Purple Magazine Volume II Issue 5. Published during the fusion era (1998-2003) when Purple Prose merged with Purple Fashion and Purple Fiction.

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 1 (Volume III)
description:
The first issue of Purple Fashion, the large-format third volume of the Paris magazine Olivier Zahm and Elein Fleiss had published since 1992, dated Spring/Summer 2004.

The fashion pages open with Paolo Roversi's "Purple People Spring-Summer 2004" and run through Terry Richardson at the Maritime Hotel, Hiromix's "Dragon Boys," Viviane Sassen's "Biotope," Marcelo Krasilcic's "Living Room" and "I'll Be Your Mirror" by Anuschka Blommers and Niels Schumm. Interviews take in the actor Michael Lonsdale, the artists Jeremy Blake and Olivier Mosset, the skater Tony Alva, the director Monte Hellman and the writer Chloé Delaume. A prose section titled "The Future" gathers Slavoj Žižek, Wolfgang Tillmans, François Laruelle, Gary Indiana and Mehdi Belhaj Kacem, and the interiors pages take in Dominique Gonzalez-Foerster's Chinese garden, Marina Faust on Fassbinder's world and Noritoshi Hirakawa on picturing architecture.

Purple began in 1992 as Purple Prose, an anti-fashion quarterly run out of Paris. The 2004 relaunch kept the artists and the philosophers and added a full fashion apparatus, and it set the shape the magazine has kept ever since.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 2 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2004, the second issue of Purple Fashion, built around two long interviews on cinema and a Balenciaga portfolio made under Nicolas Ghesquière.

Gus Van Sant talks to Geoffrey Cruickshank-Hagenbuckle and Olivier Assayas to Matthieu Orléan and Olivier Zahm. The art interviews are John Armleder with Stéphanie Moisdon, Tim Griffin with Dike Blair and Slavoj Žižek with Josefina Ayerza. Fashion runs from Corinne Day's "An English Garden" and Mark Borthwick's "All Around Kim" to Katja Rahlwes on Julia Stegner and Masatumi Sanai's "Age and Innocence," with beauty by Richard Kern, Camille Vivier and Jean-François Lepage. Rita Ackermann contributes collages, Richard Prince a "Birdtalk" portfolio and Christopher Wool a special project shot with Jeff Rian in his New York studio in 2004. Justine Kurland's "Deep America" and Giasco Bertoli's "Reservists" close out the documents.

The issue also carries architecture writing on Rome's lost modernity and mobile architecture, a habit of running buildings alongside clothes that Purple has never given up.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 3 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2005, an issue whose interview list runs from Eminem to the Spanish exploitation director Jess Franco, and whose fashion pages were shot by Hedi Slimane, Gus Van Sant and Terry Richardson.

Yan Céh interviews Eminem and, separately, Jess Franco with Giasco Bertoli. Alison M. Gingeras talks to Ashley Bickerton, Christine Macel to Jonathan Meese, Pablo León de la Barra to Los Super Elegantes and Anna Dubosc to Yann Andréa. Chuck Palahniuk sets out his rules. The fashion stories include Hedi Slimane's "Kamikaze," Gus Van Sant on Dior Homme, Takashi Homma's "Tokyo, City of Golf," Terry Richardson's "Little Glitz Girl" and Pierre Even's "Just Married Béatrice Dalle." Visual essays come from Vanessa Beecroft, Rita Ackermann, Andro Wekua and Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin, whose "1993/2005" sets a pair of their own pictures twelve years apart.

Purple's Best of the Season was shot by Terry Richardson, the start of a run of seasonal portfolios he would photograph for the magazine for most of the next decade.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 4 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2005, opening with Hans Ulrich Obrist's interview with John Baldessari and closing with Juergen Teller's pictures of Kristen McMenamy.

Olivier Zahm interviews Rick Owens, Jun Takahashi, Nicolle Meyer and Mickey Rourke; Craig Garrett talks to Wilhelm Sasnal and Yan Céh to Ellen Allien. The women's fashion runs through Viviane Sassen's "Drugs and Medicine," Daniel Jackson's "My Kingdom," Richard Kern on Shannon Click and "Soft Drag" by Anuschka Blommers and Niels Schumm. Beauty is handled by Katja Rahlwes, Harri Peccinotti, Katerina Jebb and Laetitia Benat, whose "Versailles in June" runs opposite Vava Ribeiro's "New Generation Hollywood." Richard Prince's Brooke Shields and Rita Ackermann's "The Feast of the Beast" anchor the visual essays, and Miltos Manetas contributes "Half of the Sky."

The news pages are filed by city, with Glenn O'Brien on New York, Miltos Manetas on Shanghai, Pablo León de la Barra on Mexico and Valerie Shields on Chicago.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 5 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2006, the issue in which John Galliano, Haider Ackermann, Glenn O'Brien and Miranda July all sit for interviews, and Carine Roitfeld is photographed by Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin.

Olivier Zahm and Stéphane Feugère interview Galliano; Zahm talks to Ingrid Caven and, with Terry Richardson, to Glenn O'Brien; Hans Ulrich Obrist meets Miranda July in Portland. Johan Sandberg photographs Haider Ackermann and Ariel Wizman interviews the filmmaker Raphaël Nadjari. Fashion includes Terry Richardson and Richard Prince's "The Private Case," Chloë Sevigny nude by Inez and Vinoodh, the Yves Saint Laurent summer campaign by Stefano Pilati and Juergen Teller, and Katja Rahlwes's "Nothing but Dresses." The travel pages visit a Le Corbusier house, Riviera villas and the Villa Noailles at Hyères, and Terry Richardson contributes a memorial tribute to his father, Bob Richardson.

The news section is given over to islands, with Paola Pivi on Alicudi, Glenn O'Brien on Vieques and Jeff Rian on a private island of his own.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 6 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2006, with Charlotte Gainsbourg and Riccardo Tisci interviewed by Olivier Zahm and a Christopher Wool visual essay closing the issue.

Gary Indiana interviews Chris Kraus, Bob Nickas talks to Gardar Eide Einarsson and Glenn O'Brien to Christopher Wool, while Zahm takes on Proenza Schouler, Leelee Sobieski and the filmmaker M. Blash. Juergen Teller shoots "Dick & James, A True Story," Hedi Slimane files the latest news on Pete Doherty, and Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin photograph Helena Christensen. Katja Rahlwes contributes "The Birds," Serge Leblon "The Genealogy of Morals" and Jork Weismann "Sport Couture." Vincent Gallo appears in Terry Richardson's Best of the Season, and an insert by Pierre Even surveys the French art scene.

Katsuya Kamo's "Veiled" runs in beauty and Heinz Peter Knes's "Air" in travel, the kind of pairing that has always made Purple read less like a fashion magazine than a Paris art quarterly with clothes in it.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 7 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2007, carrying Olivier Zahm's interview with Alexander McQueen and Juergen Teller's Maison Martin Margiela retrospective.

Zahm also interviews Stefano Gabbana, the architect Rudy Ricciotti, Betony Vernon and Paz de la Huerta; Ariel Wizman talks to David Lynch and Anna Dubosc to Emmanuelle Bercot. Karl Lagerfeld photographs Chan Marshall, Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin shoot Lara Stone, Richard Bush files "Chelsea Girl" and Jeremy Scott contributes "Prête à tout." The men's pages put Juergen Teller on William Eggleston, Marcelo Krasilcic on Glenn O'Brien, Terry Richardson on Jared Leto and Chikashi Suzuki on Kazuhiro Saito and Fumihiro Hayashi. Documents include Thomas Hirschhorn's letter to Olivier Zahm, Glenn O'Brien's "The Real Richard" and Marlene Marino's New York nudes.

The news pages report from London, San Francisco, Milan, New York, Paris, Monte-Carlo, São Paulo and Los Angeles, and Mehdi Belhaj Kacem closes the issue with a visual essay on the death of Pasolini.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 8 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2007, with Jeff Koons, Harmony Korine, Philippe Parreno, Dash Snow and Philip Seymour Hoffman all interviewed in the same issue.

Bill Powers talks to Koons and to Hoffman, Olivier Zahm to Korine, Parreno and Dash Snow, and Liz Goldwyn to Rodarte. Juergen Teller photographs Olya and Caroline, Alexei Hay shoots Shannan Click, Emma Summerton takes Natasa V and Manuela Pavesi photographs Anna Dello Russo before contributing a separate portfolio on Salò. Ellen von Unwerth's Claudia Schiffer runs in beauty, Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin photograph Shalom Harlow naked, and Terry Richardson files a Rio de Janeiro travel story. Maurizio Cattelan documents Terence Koh, Glenn O'Brien writes on Robert Hawkins and Noritoshi Hirakawa contributes "Around the World."

Andro Wekua closes with a visual essay, and Olivier Zahm's night pictures appear as a standing section for the first time, a running photographic diary of the magazine's own social world.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 9 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2008, in which Wes Anderson, Nicolas Ghesquière and the Japanese photographer Kishin Shinoyama sit for interviews and Karl Lagerfeld shoots twice.

Olivier Zahm and Olympia Le-Tan interview Anderson, Zahm takes Ghesquière and the novelist Jean-Jacques Schuhl, Eko Sato talks to Shinoyama and Simon Liberati to Pierre Le-Tan. Mario Sorrenti photographs "The Violinist," Juergen Teller shoots Westwood and a story called "Harmony," Jack Pierson contributes "Butterfly" and Karl Lagerfeld files both "Mademoiselle" and a Versailles portfolio. Mark Borthwick's "Lightness" and Magnus Unnar's "Private Collection" and "After Dark" fill out the fashion. Documents include Bill Powers on Jay-Z and Damien Hirst, Glenn O'Brien on Richard Prince, Jeff Rian on Lizzi Bougatsos and a Dan Colen visual essay.

The news pages carry short items from Chloë Sevigny, Zaha Hadid, Paul McCarthy, M/M (Paris), Nate Lowman and Terry Richardson, a format Purple used for years to open each issue at speed.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 10 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2008, opening with Nobuyoshi Araki interviewed by Olympia Le-Tan and closing with a Richard Prince visual essay.

Bill Powers interviews Ed Ruscha, Glenn O'Brien talks to Ryan McGinley and Olivier Zahm to Benjamin Cho and to M/M (Paris). Bernard-Henri Lévy writes on Spinoza's Ethics. Glen Luchford photographs Malgosia Bela, Chikashi Suzuki shoots Rinko Kikuchi, Richard Bush takes Daisy Lowe, Alasdair McLellan photographs Waris Ahluwalia and Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin shoot Trish Goff. Terry Richardson photographs his mother and files a Los Angeles travel story, Jeff Rian writes on Martin Kippenberger's hotel stationery, Takashi Homma documents contemporary Tokyo houses and Mark Borthwick contributes "French Women."

Purple was five volumes and sixteen years old by this point, and the issue's news pages announce the Purple Anthology, the magazine's first attempt at gathering its own archive.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 11 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2009, with Gaspar Noé, Bernard-Henri Lévy and AA Bronson interviewed and David Lynch photographing Laura Dern.

Olympia Le-Tan talks to Noé, Olivier Zahm to Zac Posen, Lévy and Aurel Schmidt, and Zahm with Dash Snow to AA Bronson. Shamim Momin interviews Alex Bag; Miltos Manetas writes on anti-copyright. Mario Sorrenti photographs a group story with Maryna, Magdalena, Paz, Karmen and Anne, Ari Marcopoulos shoots Mark Gonzales, Max Farago takes Vincent Darré and Elie Top, and Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin photograph Christina Kruse. Steven Klein contributes Courtney Love, Bernard-Henri Lévy writes on Barack Obama, Glenn O'Brien on Robert Longo and Noritoshi Hirakawa files a correlated diagram. Dash Snow's Paris travel pages and Leigh Ledare's visual essay close the issue.

Patrick Demarchelier and Paola Kudaki shoot the beauty pages, and Camille Bidault-Waddington assembles a catalog of the Spring/Summer 2009 collections.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 12 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2009, whose interview list runs Yoko Ono, Karl Lagerfeld, Miuccia Prada and Ivanka Trump, and whose fashion pages include Ryan McGinley's "Kids."

Olivier Zahm interviews Ono, Lagerfeld, Sean Lennon and Charlotte Kemp, Victoire de Castellane, and Nate Lowman with Clarissa Dalrymple. Massimo Torrigiani talks to Miuccia Prada and Sabine Heller to Ivanka Trump. Bruce LaBruce photographs Gareth Pugh, Malerie Marder shoots Charlotte Kemp, Hanna Liden takes the Balenciaga pre-collection, Stefano Pilati shoots both the YSL pre-collection and himself, and Karl Lagerfeld photographs Baptiste Giabiconi. Mario Sorrenti's Milla Jovovich runs in Love and Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin's Dree Hemingway in Naked. Documents cover Memphis legends, Helmut Newton's dentist, the origins of the Tarot of Marseille and Alejandro Jodorowsky's psychomagic.

Dash Snow's "The Wilderness of the North" appears in travel, one of his last contributions to the magazine.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 13 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2010, built as a portrait issue with the fashion pages divided by city and shot by nine photographers.

New York portraits come from Ari Marcopoulos, Max Farago, Marcelo Krasilcic, Mario Sorrenti and Terry Richardson, Los Angeles from Hanna Liden, Paris from Olivier Zahm, Tokyo from Chikashi Suzuki and London from Panos Yiapanis. Zahm and Camille Bidault-Waddington interview Sonia Rykiel; Zahm also talks to Jefferson Hack, Rita Ackermann and Philippe Sollers, Glenn O'Brien to Rob Pruitt and Alex Israel to Doug Aitken. Terry Richardson photographs Lindsay Lohan for Best of the Season, David Armstrong shoots Zac Posen and Max Farago takes Jim Goldstein. Documents run from John Richardson and Robert Longo to Navajo blankets and Paul McCarthy, and Rita Ackermann files a Marfa travel story.

Francis Picabia closes the issue as a visual essay, and Richard Kern's New York girls run alongside Zahm's night pictures.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 14 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2010, with Kim Gordon, Daido Moriyama, Alain Badiou and Bret Easton Ellis interviewed across a single issue.

Olivier Zahm talks to Gordon, Badiou and Romain Gavras, Fumihiro Hayashi to Daido Moriyama, Alex Israel to Bret Easton Ellis, Glenn O'Brien to Banks Violette and Sabine Heller to Mark Ronson. Mario Sorrenti photographs Elisa Sednaoui and Luigi Murenu, Alasdair McLellan shoots Georgia May Jagger, Glen Luchford takes Anja Rubik, Jack Pierson photographs Francesco Clemente and Jessica Craig-Martin shoots Rachel Chandler. Terence Koh contributes still lifes and Skye Parrott a self-portrait. Zahm files portfolios on Chanel Cruise in Saint-Tropez and on Diesel Black Gold, and the documents cover Jeffrey Deitch, Rick Rubin, Pierre Guyotat and Robert Williams.

Piero Fornasetti's "Elogium Mentulae" closes the issue and Christopher Makos supplies the portfolio inside the night pages.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 15 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2011, the issue in which the fashion pages are organised house by house, each collection given to a different photographer.

Collier Schorr shoots Alexander Wang, Takashi Homma shoots Miu Miu, Karl Lagerfeld shoots Chanel, André Saraiva shoots Prada, Giasco Bertoli shoots Céline, Ari Marcopoulos shoots Marc Jacobs, Max Snow shoots Rick Owens, Cedric Buchet shoots Yves Saint Laurent, Marlene Marino shoots Givenchy, Max Farago shoots Lanvin, Theo Wenner shoots Proenza Schouler and Aaron Young shoots Tom Ford. Ryan McGinley contributes nudes and Justine Kurland landscapes. Olivier Zahm interviews Laetitia Casta, Pierre Huyghe and Mehdi Belhaj Kacem; Alex Israel talks to Charles Ray, Chomwan Weeraworawit to Apichatpong Weerasethakul and Alex Gartenfeld to Isabelle Graw. Terry Richardson photographs Lady Gaga.

Viviane Sassen shoots the Brinkman and Van der Vlugt building for the summer pages, and Rodin's erotic drawings close the issue as a visual essay.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 16 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2011, the largest issue Purple had made to that point, with a news section running to nearly forty items before the features begin.

Olivier Zahm interviews Virginie Despentes and Collier Schorr, Alex Israel talks to Kenneth Anger and David Lynch, Sabine Heller to Philip-Lorca diCorcia, Noritoshi Hirakawa to the Japanese director Kaneto Shindo, Rachel Chandler to SALEM and Matt Sweeney to Mick Fleetwood. Kazumi Asamura Hayashi photographs Kiko Mizuhara, Dominique Issermann shoots Chiara Mastroianni, Steven Klein takes Barbara Sukowa, Theo Wenner shoots Jamie Bochert and Martien Mulder photographs Hannelore Knuts. Documents cover Gummo, James Chance, Luigi Ontani and Carlo Scarpa, and Rachel Chandler and James Moore report from Las Pozas.

Jeff Burton and Betony Vernon close the issue inside the Casa Museo Carlo Mollino, and Ron Galella supplies the night pages' portfolio.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 17 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2012, whose fashion stories were photographed inside artists' studios, from Robert Longo's to Tom Sachs's.

Camille Bidault-Waddington shoots in Christophe Brunnquell's studio, Gardar Eide Einarsson photographs his own, Robert Longo photographs his own, Nathaniel Goldberg shoots a Carsten Höller experience and Olivier Zahm files The Corner crossing Irving Penn with Marcel Duchamp. Zahm interviews Olympia Le-Tan and Aaron Young, Spencer Sweeney talks to Abel Ferrara, Alex Israel to Mark Leckey, Glenn O'Brien to David Salle, Sabine Heller to Lisa Yuskavage and Caroline Gaimari to Karley Sciortino. Ari Marcopoulos documents Matthew Barney and Nicolas Ghesquière discusses the Balenciaga boutiques with Dominique Gonzalez-Foerster. Terry Richardson photographs Charlotte Free and Camille Rowe-Pourcheresse.

Steven Parrino's "Exit / Dark Matter" closes the issue, and Roxanne Lowit supplies the night portfolio.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 18 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2012, with the fashion divided by city and Rei Kawakubo, Peter Beard and Brice Marden interviewed in the front of the book.

Camille Bidault-Waddington shoots "Escaping Paris," Mark Borthwick "Red Hook, Brooklyn Blank Canvas," Olivier Zahm "Istanbul Magnetism," Alasdair McLellan "Manchester Division," Miguel Calderón "Mexico City Unlimited," Ola Rindal "Stockholm Psychology," Takashi Homma "Tokyo Decadence" and Maxime Ballesteros "Berlin Biography." Zahm interviews Kawakubo, Chan Marshall and Lou Doillon, Bill Powers talks to Peter Beard, Glenn O'Brien to Brice Marden and Sven Schumann to Cyprien Gaillard. Paul McCarthy's New Museum anniversary speech runs in documents alongside a René Burri portfolio designed by Comme des Garçons, Annabel Mehran on Frida and Trotsky, and Andrew Berardini on Michel Auder.

Quentin Meillassoux contributes an essay on metaphysics and fiction, and Daido Moriyama's "Close Your Eyes" closes the issue.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 19 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2013, with the fashion stories filed under single-word themes and Larry Clark, Phoebe Philo and Marilyn Minter interviewed.

The themed stories are Punk by Alasdair McLellan, Gender by Jeremy Kost, Capitalism by Benjamin Alexander Huseby, Destruction by Theo Wenner, Women Power by Mel Bles, Fetishism by Max Snow and Folk by Camille Bidault-Waddington. Olivier Zahm interviews Larry Clark, Tim Blanks talks to Phoebe Philo, Glenn O'Brien to Marilyn Minter, Sven Schumann to Thomas Demand and Annabel Mehran to Harmony Korine. Larry Clark also photographs Tommaso Guarracino for the men's pages. Documents cover Gabriele d'Annunzio, Edmund Carpenter, Rosemarie Trockel, the Baja 1000 and the Chateau Marmont shot by Jork Weismann.

Slavoj Žižek contributes "Welcome to the Spiritual Kingdom of Animals," and Mick Rock supplies the portfolio running with the night pictures.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 20 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2013, carrying Olivier Zahm's interviews with Raf Simons and Daft Punk and Paolo Roversi's "The Little Prince."

Zahm also talks to Dominique Gonzalez-Foerster and Carsten Höller, Glenn O'Brien to Laurie Simmons, Luca Lo Pinto to Luigi Ontani and Donatien Grau to the architect Claude Parent and, separately, to Julia Kristeva. Camille Bidault-Waddington shoots a story after Roland Barthes's "The Rustle of Language," Mario Sorrenti files "Last Exit to Brooklyn," Katerina Jebb "The Living Currency," Sandy Kim "Nina's Reply" and Marcelo Krasilcic "The Ravishing of Lol Stein." Terry Richardson photographs A$AP Rocky, Chikashi Suzuki shoots G-Dragon and Zahm photographs Johnny and Laeticia Hallyday. Documents take in Dan Colen's farm project, Mike Brodie, a John Lautner house and skate transport by Ed and Deanna Templeton.

The issue introduces the work of Jimmy DeSana as its closing visual essay.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 21 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2014, in which the fashion is organised by garment rather than by house, and Ren Hang's work appears in Purple for the first time.

Benjamin Alexander Huseby shoots graphic jackets and coats, Katerina Jebb theatrical tops, Camille Bidault-Waddington skirts, Theo Wenner trousers, Roe Ethridge leather, Chikashi Suzuki knitwear and Mark Borthwick dresses. Olivier Zahm interviews Juergen Teller with Lily McMenamy, and separately Junya Watanabe, Jean-Philippe Delhomme and, with Francesco Bonami, Toiletpaper. Jeff Rian talks to Vito Acconci and Sven Schumann to Giorgio Moroder. Karim Sadli photographs Erykah Badu, Sante D'Orazio shoots Pamela Anderson and Ryan McGinley files "Togetherness." Katerina Jebb's inventory of Balthus and Gianni Oprandi's La Scarzuola run in documents.

Viviane Sassen reports from Suriname for the travel pages, and Glenn O'Brien supplies a portfolio on the New York nightclub Area.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 22 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2014, a city-by-city fashion issue with Marianne Faithfull, Jean-Pierre Léaud, Paul McCarthy and Paris Hilton among the interviews.

Michel Comte shoots Los Angeles, Johan Sandberg, Katja Rahlwes, Giasco Bertoli and Camille Bidault-Waddington shoot Paris, Benjamin Alexander Huseby, Drew Jarrett and Sandy Kim shoot New York, Takashi Homma and Chikashi Suzuki shoot Tokyo, Paul Wetherell shoots London, Ola Rindal Stockholm and Maxime Ballesteros Berlin. Sabine Heller interviews Marianne Faithfull, Simon Liberati talks to Jean-Pierre Léaud, Donatien Grau to Paul McCarthy, Sven Schumann to Thomas Struth, Olivier Zahm to Jean Touitou and Caroline Gaimari to Paris Hilton. Terry Richardson photographs Larry Clark and Andreas Larsson files the men's fashion.

Tomoo Gokita closes the issue as a visual essay, and Christopher Wool supplies the portfolio inside the night pages.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 23 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2015, whose fashion is a single suite called "Masculin Féminin" handed to seven photographers in turn.

Brianna Capozzi, Anders Edström, Camille Bidault-Waddington, Bella Howard, Robi Rodriguez, Philippe Jarrigeon and Richard Kern each shoot a chapter. Glenn O'Brien interviews Chloë Sevigny, Olivier Zahm and Alexis Dahan talk to Gabriel Orozco, Zahm interviews Jonathan Anderson and Olivier Saillard, and Sven Schumann talks to David Bailey. Benoit Peverelli shoots Haider Ackermann and "Dance of the Darkness" for the men's pages. Documents cover George Condo, Rick Owens with Hood By Air, Claude Rutault with Lawrence Weiner and the Choux de Créteil photographed by Gianni Oprandi. Marilyn Minter photographs Jamie Bochert for beauty and François Jullien is interviewed on philosophy.

Kim Gordon contributes a portfolio of noise paintings, and Wolfgang Tillmans closes with photographs made at the FESPA Digital and Fruit Logistica trade fairs in 2012.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 24 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2015, whose fashion suite runs under the header "fem.i.nism" in nine variants, each shot by a different photographer.

Robi Rodriguez takes teen, Camille Bidault-Waddington French, Petra Collins digital, Alex Antitch zombie, Juergen Teller punk rock, Casper Sejersen lilith, Benjamin Alexander Huseby new, Theo Wenner anti-fashion and Sandy Kim sex-positive. Olivier Zahm interviews Catherine Deneuve, Simon Liberati, André Saraiva and Julien Dossena; Glenn O'Brien talks to Raymond Pettibon and Sven Schumann to Douglas Gordon. Zahm and Donatien Grau interview Hélène Cixous and, separately, Miquel Barceló. Alain de Botton writes on making better porn. Documents cover Éric Troncy, Yves Saint Laurent photographed by Stephan Crasneanscki, the Hotel Okura and the housing blocks of Manuel Núñez Yanowsky and Ricardo Bofill.

Tony Oursler devises the beauty pages as face mapping, and Carol Rama closes the issue in an essay by Anne Dressen.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 25 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2016, led by Olivier Zahm's Chloë Sevigny story and Harri Peccinotti's beauty tribute to Nova magazine.

Zahm interviews Anjelica Huston, Mathias Augustyniak, Simon Porte Jacquemus and Bernard Frize; Sven Schumann talks to JR and Simon Liberati to Monte Hellman. Chikashi Suzuki shoots "Tokyo No Onna," Katja Rahlwes "Mirror Mirror," Maxime Ballesteros "Alone Together," Casper Sejersen "Tear Me Apart" and Kazumi Kurigami "Amour Absolu." Terry Richardson photographs Kenneth Anger and Jack Pierson shoots Miles McMillan. Takashi Homma documents International House and Nishinoyama House, and the issue runs features on Tony Duquette and on Paulin, Paulin, Paulin. Mehdi Belhaj Kacem interviews the philosopher Markus Gabriel.

Benoit Peverelli presents a set of Balthus Polaroids as the closing visual essay, and Sophie Bramly supplies the night portfolio.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 26 (Volume III)
description:
Fall/Winter 2016, with Ren Hang's "Harmony Exercises," Petra Collins's "Anti-Capitalist Romance" and Craig McDean's Best of the Season.

Glenn O'Brien interviews Carroll Dunham, Olivier Zahm talks to Philippe Parreno and India Menuez, Zahm and Katerina Jebb interview Marisa Berenson, Terry Richardson talks to Mary Woronov and Donatien Grau to Sylvère Lotringer. Jack Davison shoots "Fashion Ceremony," Max Farago "Modernist Transference," Casper Sejersen "Conceptual Streetwear" and Heji Shin with Bernadette Van-Huy "High-speed Historical Accidents." Jean de Loisy documents Michel Houellebecq, Bill Powers writes on David Hammons, Jeff Rian on Ron Nagle and Maurizio Cattelan on Gianni Piacentino. Gareth McConnell shoots "Psychodrama City" for beauty and Zahm reports from Chanel Cruise in Havana.

William N. Copley closes the issue, and Gianni Oprandi photographs the Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris for the architecture pages.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 27 (Volume III)
description:
Spring/Summer 2017, the last issue of Volume III, running a "Sex Fashion" suite across six photographers and William Eggleston interviewed by Terry Richardson.

Camille Vivier, Jack Pierson, Casper Sejersen, Sandy Kim, Pierre-Ange Carlotti and Olivier Zahm each shoot a Sex Fashion chapter. Zahm interviews Rick Owens and Vanessa Beecroft, Aaron Rose talks to Mike Mills and Jérôme Sans to Julio Le Parc and to Alan Vega. Ren Hang contributes "Endgame" and Ryan McGinley "Early" and "Ryan and Marc." Beauty is given to Charlotte Rutherford under the heading H+/Transhumanism, and the news pages carry Karley Sciortino on anti-penetration, Daniel Pinchbeck on fake news, Éric Troncy, and Glenn O'Brien's "If you can make it here." Zahm photographs Frank Lloyd Wright's Los Angeles houses.

John Currin closes the issue with "To paint is to love again." Purple relaunched as Volume IV the following season.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 28: 25YRS Anniversary (Volume IV)
description:
Fall/Winter 2017, the first issue of Volume IV and Purple's twenty-fifth anniversary, opening with a portfolio of twenty-five years and twenty-five covers introduced by Olivier Zahm.

Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin photograph Guinevere van Seenus, Susan Cianciolo and Chloë Sevigny; Juergen Teller shoots Stella Tennant, Wolfgang Tillmans shoots Michèle Lamy, Viviane Sassen shoots Anna Cleveland, Anders Edström shoots Alek Wek, Takashi Homma shoots Rila Fukushima and Casper Sejersen shoots Grace Hartzel. Sven Schumann interviews Wolfgang Tillmans, Zahm talks to Haider Ackermann and Jeff Rian to Richard Prince. A philosophy forum titled "On Radicality" gathers Alain Badiou, Jean-Luc Nancy, Chris Kraus with Hedi El Kholti, Paul B. Preciado, Nicolas Bourriaud, Emanuele Coccia, Tristan Garcia, Dodie Bellamy, Ariana Reines, Paul McCarthy, Bernard-Henri Lévy and Mehdi Belhaj Kacem.

The news pages carry Richard Prince and Glenn O'Brien on the deaths of Basquiat and Warhol, published in the year of O'Brien's own death.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 29: Purple 76 Index (Volume IV)
description:
Spring/Summer 2018, an issue built entirely as an index: seventy-six people, filed alphabetically from Sita Abellan to Slavoj Žižek, each given a portrait or a short interview.

The list runs through Virgil Abloh, Doug Aitken, Alain Badiou, Vanessa Beecroft, Maurizio Cattelan, Sadie Coles, John Galliano, Nicolas Ghesquière, Thomas Hirschhorn, Carsten Höller, Anne Imhof, Rei Kawakubo, Chan Marshall, Kiko Mizuhara, Jean-Luc Nancy, Rick Owens, Miuccia Prada, Chloë Sevigny, Juergen Teller, Lotta Volkova and Chloe Wise, among others. Teller photographs Balenciaga, Andrea Spotorno shoots Kawakubo and Ghesquière, Chikashi Suzuki shoots Kiko Mizuhara, Henrik Purienne shoots Galliano and Heji Shin shoots Camille Bidault-Waddington. Jérôme Sans, Sven Schumann, Bill Powers, Xerxes Cook and Joshua Glass conduct the bulk of the interviews.

The format turns the magazine's masthead and address book into its editorial structure, and Purple has returned to the index idea in later anniversary issues.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 30: The Los Angeles Issue (Volume IV)
description:
Fall/Winter 2018, the first of Purple's city issues, given over to Los Angeles across fourteen covers and seventy-six features.

Olivier Zahm interviews Kim Gordon, Alex Israel, Jeffrey Deitch, Kenneth Anger, Bret Easton Ellis, Wes Anderson, Aaron Rose, Benjamin Millepied and Laura and Kate Mulleavy. Donatien Grau talks to David Hockney and to Michael Chow, Bill Powers to Louise Bonnet, Dorothée Perret to Henry Taylor, Emilien Crespo to Jonathan Gold, Peter Shire and Jim Heimann, and Maurizio Cattelan with Marta Papini to Martine Syms and Shahryar Nashat. Mike Kelley, Charles Ray, Catherine Opie, Raymond Pettibon, Doug Aitken, Andrea Zittel, Jack Pierson, Gary Simmons and Paul and Damon McCarthy all appear. Eli Russell Linnetz shoots Comme des Garçons, Juergen Teller shoots Balenciaga and Hans Feurer shoots Miu Miu.

Eve Babitz, Norman M. Klein and Lisa Eisner supply the city's own account of itself, and John Jefferson Selve writes on Deleuze and California.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 31: The Paris Issue (Volume IV)
description:
Spring/Summer 2019, the Paris issue, running fifteen covers including one by Nobuyoshi Araki.

Araki shoots Prada, Martin Parr shoots Gucci, Paolo Roversi shoots Comme des Garçons, Daido Moriyama shoots Saint Laurent, Juergen Teller shoots Balenciaga, Andrea Spotorno shoots Bottega Veneta and Anders Edström files "Quiet Days in Clichy." Olivier Zahm interviews Gaspar Noé, Eva Ionesco, Olivier Saillard, Kamel Mennour, Bernard-Henri Lévy and the florist Pierre Banchereau; Donatien Grau talks to Camille Henrot and Tatiana Trouvé, and Jérôme Sans to Daniel Buren. Mehdi Belhaj Kacem, Éric Troncy, Simon Liberati, Anna Dubosc, Emanuele Coccia, Catherine Malabou, Bob Nickas, Ariana Reines and John Jefferson Selve write in their own voices. Emilien Crespo reports from L'Arpège, Le Servan and Iñaki Aizpitarte's kitchen.

Kira Bunse and Maxime Ballesteros photograph the Paris scene, and Gianni Oprandi documents the city's art nouveau.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 32: The Cosmos Issue (Volume IV)
description:
Fall/Winter 2019, the Cosmos issue, with sixteen covers including Judy Chicago, Hilma af Klint, Emma Kunz and an image from the Hubble Space Telescope.

Étienne Klein writes on the origin of the universe, Peter Sloterdijk on panic civilization, Félix Guattari on chaosmos, Jean-Luc Nancy on the creation of the world, Emanuele Coccia on the planet and Maxine Bédat on the hundred and fifty billion garments made each year. Jeffrey Deitch interviews Judy Chicago; Hans Ulrich Obrist takes Hilma af Klint, Emma Kunz and the astronomer Martin Rees; Olivier Zahm talks to Christophe Galfard, Philippe Parreno and Doug Aitken. Juergen Teller shoots Balenciaga as astro-monastic, Camille Vivier shoots Gucci at Bomarzo, Coco Capitán shoots Miu Miu and Takashi Homma photographs a zen garden. Tom Sachs's Space Program: Mars is revisited.

Éliane Radigue, Alicja Kwade, Urs Fischer and Carsten Höller round out an issue that treats cosmology and fashion as one subject.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Fashion Magazine Issue 33: The Brain Issue (Volume IV)
description:
Spring/Summer 2020, the Brain issue and the last of Volume IV, built around attention, connection and what screens have done to both.

Jeff Rian writes on the online brain, Mark Alizart on the world brain, Emanuele Coccia on what plants know, Éric Troncy on what has been lost in a world of connection, Joshua Decter on the post-brain and John Jefferson Selve on the attention economy. Daphna Joel writes on sex and the brain and Alejandro Jodorowsky on the cosmic one. Olivier Zahm interviews Gus Van Sant, Daniel Arsham, Carsten Höller, Sadhguru, Genesis Belanger, Harold Ancart, Dike Blair, Brad Phillips and Catherine Malabou. New York labels get their own pages, among them Telfar, Pyer Moss, Ottolinger and Puppets and Puppets. Juergen Teller shoots Balenciaga, Mario Sorrenti files "New York State of Mind" and Colin Dodgson shoots Miu Miu.

Thirteen covers, one of them by Paul McCarthy, close out the volume Purple had opened with its twenty-fifth anniversary issue three years earlier.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 34: The Love Issue
description:
Fall/Winter 2020, the Love issue, published in the first year of the pandemic with sixteen covers and Glenn O'Brien's "True Love" at the front.

Paul B. Preciado writes a library of love, McKenzie Wark on femmunism, Claire Fontaine on the twenty-fifth hour, Emanuele Coccia on love as a domestic mystery, Alain de Botton on Pygmalion, Frédéric Beigbeder on the French kiss, Simon Liberati on his own love stories and Alejandro Jodorowsky on what love is. Allen Ginsberg's "Song" is reprinted. Interviews take in David Hockney, Sarah Lucas, Pierre Cardin, Urs Fischer, Deana Lawson, Nicolas Party, Ed Atkins, Camille Henrot, Virgil Abloh, Jenna Gribbon, Somaya Critchlow, Nevine Mahmoud and AA Bronson. Juergen Teller shoots Balenciaga, Bruce Gilden shoots Gucci, Casper Sejersen shoots Louis Vuitton and Katja Rahlwes shoots Saint Laurent.

Hans Bellmer, Paul McCarthy, Francis Picabia and David Horvitz contribute portfolios, Katerina Jebb files "Love Letters," and Maurizio Cattelan closes with a tribute to Black Lives Matter.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 35: The Island Issue
description:
Spring/Summer 2021, the Island issue, opening with Édouard Glissant on archipelagic thought and running to eighteen covers.

Donna Haraway, Catherine Malabou, Hans Ulrich Obrist and Carsten Höller all appear, alongside features on the Ibiza myth, wild swimming, island undergrounds, Sweden's islands and the red island. The artists include Lisa Yuskavage, Miriam Cahn, Elizabeth Glaessner, Raoul Hausmann, Alejandro Cardenas, Anna Uddenberg, Rachel Rose, Mark Dion, Lola Montes Schnabel and Torbjørn Rødland. Architecture runs from Isamu Noguchi's playscapes and Ricardo Bofill's Marina Baie des Anges to Terunobu Fujimori, Le Grand Chalet, La Cupola and Philippe Starck. Fashion covers Mugler, Balenciaga, Prada, Chanel, Comme des Garçons, Gucci, Berluti, Emporio Armani, Jil Sander and Ami.

The issue was assembled during the second year of lockdown, and its subject, an island of one's own, is the reason for the covers being handed to painters rather than photographers.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 36: The Mexico Issue
description:
Fall/Winter 2021, the Mexico issue, with fifteen covers and its features reported almost entirely from Mexico City and Oaxaca.

Daniel Pinchbeck writes on the country's psychedelic renaissance, Elena Reygadas on corn, Sayak Valencia and Juan Villoro on the present, and the issue reprints Antonin Artaud's account of the peyote dance. The artists include Dr. Lakra interviewed by Aaron Rose, Frieda Toranzo Jaeger, Paloma Contreras Lomas, Pedro Friedeberg, Stefan Brüggemann, Tezontle, Manuel Álvarez Bravo and Agustín Hernández. Bárbara Sánchez-Kane and Víctor Barragán appear among the new Mexican labels. Dorian López photographs the muxes of Juchitán, and a feature titled "Nos están matando" addresses the killing of women. Josef Albers in Mexico supplies one cover and Robert Nava another.

Juergen Teller shoots Balenciaga, Dario Catellani shoots Chanel, and Olivier Zahm photographs Flores Cosmos alongside interviews with Homero Aridjis and Alejandro Jodorowsky.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 37: The Future Issue
description:
Spring/Summer 2022, the Future issue, opening with Jean-Luc Nancy's "The Fragile Skin of the World" and running to nineteen covers.

Carlo Rovelli writes on the sources of time, Mark Fisher on acid communism, Jean Baudrillard on tetanized inertia, Hakim Bey on the will to power as disappearance, Marc Augé on individual and collective futures, Adam Greenfield on artificial intelligence, and The Invisible Committee on the world to come. Vivienne Westwood closes the issue. Olivier Zahm interviews Paul B. Preciado, Demna, Eliza Douglas, Tobias Spichtig and George Rouy; Jérôme Sans and Zahm talk to Pierre Huyghe; Aleph Molinari interviews Jon Rafman, Makoto Azuma, Julia Watson and T.J. Demos. Harmony Korine shoots Saint Laurent, Juergen Teller shoots Balenciaga, Takashi Homma shoots Comme des Garçons and Henrik Purienne shoots Courrèges.

Ram Han's digital painting supplies the first cover, and a set of VanMoof bikes customised by Mathias Kiss, Nina Kraviz, André Saraiva and Mei supplies another.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 38: The 30YRS Issue
description:
Fall/Winter 2022, the thirtieth anniversary issue, organised as thirty numbered parts, one for each strand of the magazine's history.

The parts run from Elein Fleiss, who co-founded Purple in 1992, through Martin Margiela, who contributed new collages, and on to Wolfgang Tillmans, Comme des Garçons, Purple Tokyo, Purple New York, Chloë Sevigny, Maurizio Cattelan, Bernadette Corporation, Dominique Gonzalez-Foerster, Rita Ackermann, Inez and Vinoodh, Glenn O'Brien, Dash Snow, Juergen Teller and Richard Prince. Purple Cinema gathers David Lynch, Larry Clark, Wes Anderson, Harmony Korine, Gaspar Noé, Gus Van Sant, Abel Ferrara, Mamoru Oshii, Kenneth Anger and Philippe Parreno. A thirteen-part section on women and painting runs alongside. Catherine Deneuve appears in Saint Laurent and Chikashi Suzuki shoots "Black Rose" for Comme des Garçons.

Glenn O'Brien's memorial text for Dash Snow is reprinted, and Bernadette Van-Huy speaks for Bernadette Corporation.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 39: The New York Issue
description:
Spring/Summer 2023, the New York issue, opening with the question "What is New York?" and answering it across forty-three features.

Ser Serpas, John Currin, Jamian Juliano-Villani, Ebecho Muslimova, Jonathan Lyndon Chase, Emma Stern and AA Bronson appear among the artists, Laura Poitras among the filmmakers, and Elena Velez, Puppets and Puppets, Matthew Williams and Carolina Herrera among the designers. Bob Colacello, Amy Fine Collins and Jenny Schlenzka supply the institutional memory, and Tourmaline, Charlotte Kemp Muhl, Tali Lennox, Paul Sevigny and CumGirl8 the present tense. Guen Fiore photographs "Candy Darlings" and a feature reads Guy Bourdin's New York as a love letter to America. Fashion covers Gucci, Saint Laurent, Balenciaga, Givenchy, Bottega Veneta, Miu Miu, Valentino and Cartier.

Essays titled "Letter From Harlem," "Rectangular World" and "Will New York Return To Its Glory Days?" set the issue's argument with the city.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 40: The Revolutions Issue
description:
Fall/Winter 2023, the Revolutions issue, with twenty-one covers and Cindy Sherman on the first of them.

Alain Badiou writes on art and the possibility of the impossible, Paul B. Preciado on electronic heroin, Byung-Chul Han on the idiots' revolution, Val Plumwood on angels in the ecosystem, Bayo Akomolafe on what climate collapse asks of us, and The Invisible Committee on finding each other. Aleph Molinari interviews Merlin Sheldrake, Daniel Pinchbeck talks to Douglas Rushkoff and Bernardo Kastrup, and Olivier Zahm with Molinari to Neville Wakefield and Cyrill Gutsch. Steven Klein photographs Hari Nef, Juergen Teller shoots Balenciaga, Richard Kern shoots Guess USA, Cameron McCool shoots Milla Jovovich in Gucci, Kira Bunse shoots Caroline Polachek in Givenchy and Takashi Homma shoots Louis Vuitton.

John Giorno, Dash Snow, Charles Ray, Anthea Hamilton, Mariko Mori and De Wain Valentine round out an issue that puts ecological argument and fashion photography on facing pages.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 41: The Essence of Fashion Issue
description:
Spring/Summer 2024, the Essence of Fashion issue, with twenty-one covers and Nicolas Ghesquière's ten years at Louis Vuitton on the first.

Roland Barthes writes on a violent sensation of time, Emanuele Coccia on an excess of sensitivity, and Olivier Zahm files an essay called "Time Machine." Zahm interviews Cathy Horyn, Marc Jacobs with Bill Powers, Francesco Risso, Mel Ottenberg, Dilara Findikoglu, Elena Velez, Dion Lee, Bárbara Sánchez-Kane, Cédric Rivrain and BFRND; Bobbi Salvör Menuez talks to Susan Cianciolo. Mark Borthwick photographs Malgosia Bela for Balenciaga, Juergen Teller shoots Anja Rubik in Saint Laurent and Vivienne Westwood, Vidar Logi shoots Björk in Noir Kei Ninomiya, Gray Sorrenti shoots Chloë Sevigny in Prada and Paul Kooiker shoots for Courrèges and Bottega Veneta.

Rineke Dijkstra, Lee Friedlander, Walker Evans, Thomas Struth, Mike Kelley and Jessica Eaton appear in the photography pages, set against the season's collections.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 42: The Magic Issue
description:
Fall/Winter 2024, the Magic issue, with twenty-one covers and Carl Jung on the first of them.

Michel Foucault writes on the limits of the world, Jules Michelet on the heresy of witches, Mark Alizart on the magic wand, Simon Liberati on amulets, talismans and pantacles, Alexandre Samson on fashion and superstition, Emanuele Coccia on the Harry Potter syndrome and Tobie Nathan on love as the trance of worlds without gods. Aleph Molinari interviews David Lynch, Patti Smith and Anohni; Björk writes on sonic magic; Olivier Zahm talks to Ariana Papademetropoulos, Philippe Parreno and Pino Pascali. Steven Klein photographs "Warrior Hearts: A Centaur's Tale," Juergen Teller shoots Isabelle Huppert for Balenciaga, Mark Borthwick shoots Comme des Garçons, Venetia Scott shoots Prada and Katerina Jebb scans the high jewelry.

Leonora Carrington, Wolfgang Tillmans and Tobias Spichtig close out the art pages, and Mitch Horowitz and Federico Campagna supply the occult scholarship.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 43: The Tokyo Diary Issue
description:
Spring/Summer 2025, the Tokyo Diary issue, Purple's largest, with a hundred and ten features and eighteen covers.

Roland Barthes's "Empire of Signs" and Tanizaki's "In Praise of Shadows" are reprinted, and Leonard Koren writes on wabi-sabi. Jérôme Sans interviews Takashi Murakami, Olivier Zahm talks to Tomoo Gokita, Kei Ninomiya, Hajime Kinoko and Yōko Yamanaka, Aleph Molinari to Motoko Ishibashi, Jun Takahashi, Masaru Hatanaka and Tadashi Kawamata, and Zahm with Molinari to Wim Wenders. The photography runs through Nobuyoshi Araki, Daido Moriyama, Masahisa Fukase, Hajime Sawatari, Keiichi Tanaami, Tadanori Yokoo, Chikashi Suzuki and Takashi Homma, who shoots zen gardens, trails, waves and the season's collections. Nikolai von Bismarck photographs butoh, and Kazuo Ohno, Ruth Asawa, Yoshitomo Nara, Mariko Mori and Ozu all get their pages.

A recurring "Why Japan?" question is put to Urs Fischer, Helmut Lang, Stefano Pilati, Coco Capitán, Setsuko and André, and Ryoko Sekiguchi files an announcement to humanity.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 44: The Analog Issue
description:
Fall/Winter 2025, the Analog issue, arguing for the hand and the negative against the machine across sixteen covers.

A running "Why Analog?" question is answered by David Lynch, James Cameron, Brian Eno, Marguerite Duras, Carl Sagan, Isamu Noguchi, Robert Montgomery, Thomas Lélu, David Sax and Artus de Lavilléon. Hakim Bey writes on immediatism, Byung-Chul Han on the gaze, Emanuele Coccia on animism, Frédéric Beigbeder on France against the robots, Daniel Pinchbeck on technofeudalism and Beau Friedlander on what AI cannot do. Aleph Molinari interviews Candida Höfer, Thomas Ruff, Lina Ghotmeh, Mark Leckey and Sharon Eyal; Olivier Zahm talks to Harri Peccinotti, David Carson, Willy Chavarria and Nicolas Godin, and is himself interviewed by Rita Ackermann. Juergen Teller photographs Balenciaga's fifty-fourth couture collection and Cameron McCool shoots Kim Gordon in Gucci.

Irving Penn, Nan Goldin, Joanna Piotrowska, Katerina Jebb, Richard Prince and Takashi Homma supply the photography, and Alighiero Boetti and Roman Signer the art.
tags: Magazines, Purple Magazine, Fashion, Art, Culture

title: Purple Magazine Issue 45: The New Glamour Issue
description:
Spring/Summer 2026, the New Glamour issue, with seventeen covers and Laurie Simmons on the first.

Susan Sontag's "Notes on Camp" and Roland Barthes's "The Face of Garbo" are reprinted alongside Jean Baudrillard on seduction and Kenneth Anger on the new gods. A running "Notes on Glamour" collects statements from Junya Watanabe, Duran Lantink, Nicolas Di Felice, Rachel Scott, Vaquera, Raul Lopez, Elena Velez, Dilara Findikoglu, Bárbara Sánchez-Kane, Taller Marmo, Andreas Kronthaler and Women's History Museum. Olivier Zahm interviews Anthony Vaccarello, Francesco Vezzoli, Christeene, Betony Vernon and Miguel Adrover, and Aleph Molinari talks to Martin Parr and Kali Malone.
